Your Spring moves recovered CON and SER, weakening Russia. Which Russian-held centers are you targeting this Fall? I’ll keep my units out of Austrian centers; please coordinate with Germany to deny Russia further gains.

Russia is still the largest threat, but the western frontier is tense. What are A HOL and A KIE doing this Fall? I can keep A PIC and A MAR out of German centers if you direct A LVN toward a Russian-held center.

What are your plans for F DEN and F NOR this Fall? DEN is a German center, and your fleet there could decide its ownership. I’ll keep my forces clear of English centers; please use your northern position to contain Russia where possible.
What are A RUH and A BUR doing this Fall? HOL is exposed from RUH, and I need to defend it. I’ll keep German units out of Burgundy and Picardy; please keep A RUH out of HOL and avoid German centers.

What are F DEN and your other units doing this Fall? Please keep F DEN out of HEL and German centers. I’ll keep my forces clear of English centers; I need to secure HOL against pressure from the west.

Are A LVN, A WAR, and your Baltic fleets staying clear of German centers this Fall? I can’t leave our border undefended, so please confirm you won’t attack. I’ll consider whether to continue pressing east while Austria contests your southern positions.
I intend F ION–TUN this Fall. Please do not use F TYS to support a defense there; I can use A TYR–MUN to help pressure Germany instead. Can we agree to that exchange?

I’m not attacking ROM or TRI this Fall; my forces need a chance to grow. I intend F ION–TUN. Will you keep your forces clear of Italian centers and avoid using the crisis with Russia to move against VEN or NAP?

I intend F ION–TUN and will keep A TYR clear of Russian centers. Please keep A SMY and your other units clear of VEN and NAP. Which centers are you targeting this Fall, and will you avoid pushing toward an Italian solo?

This Fall I can contest CON from ARM with BLA support and press SER from GAL/UKR. Are you defending CON and SER, or will you leave either open? I will avoid GRE and VIE if you keep your units from attacking my positions.

Can you renew pressure on Austria this Fall—A TYR toward TRI or ROM, and F ION toward ADR if useful? Austria is holding CON and SER against me; pressure on its western centers would stretch its defense. I’ll keep my units clear of Italian centers.
Let’s keep our northern front quiet again this Fall. I’ll keep my forces clear of English centers; please keep F NOR and F DEN clear of SWE and my other centers. What are those fleets doing?

I recovered CON and SER in Spring, and will defend both this Fall against Russia’s likely attacks. I can’t spare forces to take another Russian center; please keep Norway secure and deny Russia any northern gain.

This Fall I’m prioritizing holding CON and SER against Russian pressure from ARM, GAL, and UKR; I cannot safely target another Russian center. Please keep clear of Austrian centers and continue pressuring Germany.

I will defend both CON and SER this Fall; I cannot leave either open after recovering them. If you keep clear of GRE and VIE, I’ll keep my moves focused on securing these centers rather than widening the contest.

I’ll keep my forces clear of VEN and NAP this Fall and won’t use the Russian crisis to attack your centers. I’m defending CON and SER against Russia. Your F ION–TUN stays clear of Austrian centers, so let’s avoid opening another front.

F DEN will hold, with F NOR supporting its defense. I’m not moving against another German center, but I can’t leave DEN undefended. Please do not attack it from F HEL or A HOL; I’ll keep my other units clear of your centers.

F DEN will hold and F NOR will support its defense; I’m not sending either fleet against Russian centers this Fall. I’ll keep my position defensive in the north and continue to contain Russia where I can. Please keep your forces clear of English centers.
F DEN will hold and F NOR will support its defense. I’ll keep both fleets clear of SWE and your other centers, as requested. Please continue keeping your forces out of Norway and English centers.

A BUR and A RUH will stay out of MUN and HOL this Fall; I’m not opening another front while Russia remains the larger threat. What are A HOL and A KIE doing? Please keep German units out of Burgundy and Picardy, and direct A LVN against Russia.
I can’t agree to leave TUN undefended. I intend to support F NAF–TUN with F TYS, so your F ION–TUN will likely bounce. A TYR–MUN is your choice, but I’m not coordinating against Germany.

I intend to keep A HOL and A KIE focused on securing HOL, with F HEL on the northern front. I’m not looking to widen the western contest beyond protecting German centers; please keep F DEN out of HEL and respect the German border.

A LVN will attack MOS this Fall. A KIE will support A HOL’s defense, and A HOL will stay in place; I’m not moving it into Belgium or France. Please keep A RUH and your other units out of German centers.

A LVN will attack Russian-held MOS this Fall. My other eastern units are not positioned to make a reliable attack on a Russian center, so I’ll keep A KIE and A HOL focused on German security. Please keep Austrian units clear of German centers.

F ION–TUN is against France, not your centers; A TYR will hold and stay clear of ROM, TRI, and GRE. Please keep your units clear of VEN and NAP. I still need room to rebuild, so I hope we can avoid opening an Italian-Austrian front.

I’m targeting French-held TUN with F ION; A TYR will hold and stay clear of Russian centers. I’m not helping you toward a solo, and I need your units to stay clear of VEN and NAP as promised. Which centers are you targeting this Fall?
I’ll keep my units clear of Norway and English centers this Fall. Please keep F NOR and F DEN clear of SWE and my other centers, as agreed.
A LVN and A WAR will stay clear of German centers this Fall, and my Baltic fleets will not attack yours. Please keep your units clear of Russian centers.

A GAL and A UKR are pressing SER, and A ARM is attacking CON with F BLA support. I’m not moving on GRE or VIE. If you want to contain this contest, avoid attacks on my units and we can discuss a settlement after the Fall.

I’m targeting CON and SER this Fall, not VEN or NAP. A SMY and my other units will stay clear of your centers. I can’t promise to halt expansion indefinitely, but I have no move against Italian territory this turn.

notes.note: F1908: France supports NAF–TUN, so avoid futile ION–TUN; reposition ION to EAS. TYR–MUN seeks an open German center, though France may contest. Austria promises to stay clear of VEN/NAP; Russia says no Italian centers targeted.
Hold HOL with HEL and KIE support against French pressure; England says DEN holds and not attacking another German center. Keep promise to France/Austria: LVN-MOS. SIL presses WAR.
Hold DEN to take it; Russia and Germany promised a quiet northern front. Try NOR–SWE for an additional center; move IRI to NAO and LVP to CLY for positioning.

Take MUN with BUR supported by RUH; Italy also targets it, but our supported move may prevail. Defend TUN against ION with NAF supported by TYS. Germany’s quiet-frontier assurance is broken by the MUN attack; Austria and England claim defensive focus.

Defend CON with AEG support. RUM-GAL supported by BOH aims to cut GAL's support into SER; SER holds against UKR. ROM takes open NAP; ADR advances to APU. Italy says it will stay clear of Austrian centers; Russia presses CON/SER.

Press CON with SMY supported by BLA and RUM with GAL supported by UKR. Austria claimed to defend CON/SER; England and Germany promised restraint. BAR to NWG and BOT to BAL seek northern pressure without entering English or German centers.

messages.body: Your Fall 1908 moves against CON and SER were clear. I need to know your Spring intentions: are GAL and UKR again targeting SER, and will ARM/ANK press CON? I will defend my centers; keeping clear of GRE and VIE is essential.

Austria is holding the Balkan line against Russia. Please keep your forces clear of Austrian centers and continue pressure on Germany; I cannot spare units for a western front. Are you planning any moves toward MUN or the eastern border this Spring?

Russia remains the immediate threat to my southern centers. Can A LVN make another attempt against MOS, and what are your eastern units doing this Spring? I will keep Austrian units out of German centers; please keep pressure on Russia where feasible.

Austria at 10 is the immediate solo threat. Can we coordinate pressure this turn rather than contest each other? Please move against Austrian-held MUN or TRI if feasible; I’ll keep my northern centers secure and avoid French centers. What are your targets?

Austria leads at 10 and is the urgent solo threat. Please continue attacking its southern centers this turn, especially CON, BUL, or RUM. I’ll keep my fleets clear of your centers and protect the north; what targets are you choosing?

Austria is at 10 and nearing a solo win. Can we avoid reopening the DEN/HOL contest this turn and focus on containing it? I’ll keep F DEN out of German centers; please keep your units clear of DEN and English centers. What are A HOL and A KIE doing?

You are at 10 centers and the clearest solo threat. What are your Spring targets? I can’t keep my forces committed to the German front while you remain unchecked; I’m considering pressure from PIE toward TYR and TYS toward NAP.

Austria is now at 10 centers and the main solo danger. I’m prepared to keep pressure off your centers this Spring if you’ll direct A WAR and A LVN against Austrian interests where possible and avoid assisting Austria’s westward expansion. What are your plans?

Austria has 10 centers and is the most immediate solo threat. Are you willing to coordinate containment this Spring? I’m considering pressure toward TYR and NAP; please tell me whether your fleets can interfere with Austrian expansion or support a western front against it.

Austria is at 10 centers and closest to a solo; we should contain it before either of us becomes its next target. Can you keep A MUN, A RUH, and A PIC out of German centers while directing pressure south? I’ll avoid the French frontier if you do.

Austria’s 10 centers make it the immediate solo threat. I’m willing to keep my units clear of Russian centers if you turn your southern forces against Austria rather than German territory. What are A GAL, A UKR, and your Black Sea fleet doing this Spring?

With you at 10 centers, I need to know your intentions toward the German frontier. I’m not planning to enter Austrian centers this Spring; please keep your units out of German territory, especially with A MUN already near our border.

France holds MUN with A MUN and has A RUH nearby. I can order A TYR–MUN; can A KIE support that move, and will you use A HOL or A WAR to pressure France as well? I need a center to rebuild, and would rather coordinate against France than let Austria grow unchecked.

You have 10 centers and are still the leading solo threat. Are you planning any moves toward VEN or NAP this Spring? I’ll keep A TYR clear of Austrian centers; I need a route to rebuild, so I propose we coordinate against France instead of opening an Italian-Austrian front.

I’m looking for a way to rebuild and am considering A TYR–MUN. Are you keeping A MUN in place, and what are your plans toward Germany this Spring? I’ve maintained restraint on our western border, but I cannot remain indefinitely confined to VEN.

Austria is at 10 centers and can reach 18 if we let it consolidate. Will A MUN and A PIE press into BOH/TRI this Spring, and can A RUH support? I’ll renew pressure from GAL/UKR and the Black Sea; please avoid Russian centers while we contain Austria.

Austria remains the immediate solo threat. Can A TYR move against TRI or support pressure on it this Spring? I’ll keep A SMY clear of VEN and NAP and press Austria from the east. Please don’t let Austria take your remaining center unopposed.

You lead with 10 centers and remain close to a solo. What are A CON, A RUM, and your units on the northern front doing this Spring? I’ll continue contesting your eastern positions; if you want to contain this war, propose specific mutual stand-down moves rather than press my centers.

I won’t agree to a stand-down while your forces contest my centers. This Spring I’m defending CON and SER and will not move on GRE or VIE; you can reduce the danger by keeping GAL/UKR off SER and ARM/ANK off CON. I can’t promise to leave those positions undefended.

I have no Spring move planned into German centers, and A BOH will stay out of MUN. I’m focused on defending the Balkan line and responding to France’s pressure toward NAP. Please keep your units clear of Austrian centers; I’m not asking you to open a new front for me.

I’m not targeting MUN or the western border this Spring, but I can’t accept F TYS–NAP or A PIE moving toward Austrian centers. Keep those units clear of NAP and my other centers, and I’ll keep my forces out of French territory. I’m focused on the eastern front, not a western war.

I’m not planning to attack VEN or NAP this Spring. France’s F TYS–NAP would threaten my NAP, so please use your forces against France if you can—especially from TYR toward PIE or another French position. I’ll defend my centers, and we can coordinate against France without opening an Austrian-Italian front.

Agreed: Austria is the immediate threat. I can’t reach TYR or NAP from my northern position, so please press TYR from PIE and take any safe opportunity against TRI or MUN. I’ll keep my northern centers secure and look for pressure on Germany; please keep your forces clear of English centers.

I’m moving A MUN to BOH, with A RUH supporting, and A PIE toward TYR. I won’t target your centers directly beyond contesting BOH, but I can’t leave your expansion unchecked. Please keep your forces from advancing west.

Yes: A MUN–BOH with A RUH support, and A PIE–TYR. I’ll press Austria rather than Russian centers. Please renew pressure from GAL and UKR against Austrian positions; I can’t support your moves directly from here.

I can’t attack MUN—it is French. I’ll move A MUN–BOH with A RUH supporting, and A PIE–TYR; TRI isn’t reachable from my current positions. Please keep your northern centers secure and use any opportunity to impede Austria’s growth.

I’ll keep A RUH out of German centers and direct it to support A MUN–BOH; A PIE will move toward TYR. I’m not targeting your centers this Spring. Please use A WAR or A LVN against Austrian interests where possible, and avoid helping Austria westward.

A MUN will not stay in place: I’m moving it to BOH with A RUH supporting, while A PIE moves toward TYR. I’m not attacking VEN or your other centers, but Austria’s growth needs checking. What can you do against Austria from your position?

A LVN will again attack MOS; A WAR is not positioned to attack an Austrian center this Spring. Given your lead, I need assurance that Austrian units will stay out of German centers, especially Munich and Berlin, before I can consider broader cooperation. What are your units doing near the German frontier?

I’ll keep A HOL and A KIE out of DEN and English centers this Spring. I can’t promise to leave the Holland contest permanently closed while HOL is exposed, but I have no plan to attack DEN. Let’s coordinate containment of Austria’s growing lead.

A LVN will attack MOS again. A WAR cannot directly attack an Austrian center, and I won’t send it into Austrian territory without a credible joint plan. I’ll keep my units out of France this Spring; please keep A MUN, A RUH, and A PIC out of German centers while we contain Austria.

A KIE cannot support A TYR–MUN: Kiel is not adjacent to Munich. I won’t commit A HOL or A WAR to attack France while Austria is at 10 and the larger solo threat. If you attack MUN, tell me whether France has promised to keep its other units out of German centers.

I can order A TYR–TRI to pressure Austria. Can A GAL support that attack this Spring? Austria may support TRI from VIE, so your support is important. I’ll keep A TYR clear of Russian centers; please keep A SMY clear of VEN and NAP as promised and continue pressing Austria from the east.

I’m still contesting your eastern positions, but I’m not seeking GRE or VIE. GAL and UKR are positioned to pressure SER and RUM, while F BLA can support pressure on CON or RUM. If you want to contain this, propose specific withdrawals that leave me secure access to the Black Sea and my centers.

I’ll continue pressuring Austria’s eastern centers, especially RUM and CON, rather than opening a northern front. GAL and UKR are on that front, with F BLA available to support. Please keep your fleets clear of my centers as agreed.

GAL and UKR are focused on Austrian positions, and F BLA will support pressure on the southern front. I will keep A LVN and A WAR clear of German centers; please keep your units clear of Russian centers while we both contain Austria.

notes.note: Spring 1909: TYR–MUN to exploit France vacating Munich and gain a foothold. Austria says it will avoid VEN/NAP and favors action against France; Russia asks pressure on Austria but promises to keep clear of Italian centers. France moves MUN–BOH with RUH support and PIE–TYR; Germany offers no support.

Press toward Russian FIN from SWE; advance fleets toward western waters and German HEL while filling owned LVP. Germany and France agreed to contain Austria; Russia is attacking Austria and promised to avoid northern centers.
Contain Austria: PIE-TYR supported by MUN; TYS probes ROM. Keep French centers covered and advance RUH toward BUR. England and Germany urged anti-Austrian pressure; no new commitments confirmed.

Press LVN-MOS with WAR support, as promised; Russia said it would keep LVN/WAR clear of German centers. HOL-BEL seeks growth, though France may contest it. KIE returns to BER; Austria remains the leading solo threat.

Concentrate GAL and UKR on RUM with BLA support; hope to break Austria’s eastern hold while France/Italy pressure from west. Advance SMY to ARM and reposition MOS to STP. England/Germany promised to avoid Russian centers; Italy asked me to support TRI but RUM is priority.

France threatens BOH and NAP; defend BOH with VIE support and NAP with APU support. Advance CON toward Russian ANK and TRI toward Italian VEN; hold RUM while SER supports it. Italy promised to stay clear; France openly threatens.

messages.body: F ROM currently gives you ROM at my expense and leaves NAP exposed. Please move F ROM out of ROM this Fall and keep your forces clear of NAP and the Austrian centers. I can keep my western units out of French centers while we contain the Russian front.

Our forces are still contesting ANK and RUM. I’m not agreeing to leave Austrian centers undefended, but propose you keep ARM and UKR clear of my centers this Fall. Are you willing to reduce pressure on the southern front?

A MOS is positioned to take MOS from Russia, which helps contain the eastern front. I’ll keep my units out of German centers; please keep your forces clear of Austrian centers and let me know if you intend to continue pressing Russia.

Austria is the immediate solo threat. I’ll keep my northern units focused on protecting English centers and won’t move against you this Fall. Can you take MOS with A MOS and avoid assisting Austrian expansion? Please also keep A HOL and A WAR clear of my centers.

Austria is at 10 and poised to gain centers this Fall. Your F ROM can take ROM, and A TYR may be able to pressure Austrian territory. Please prioritize denying Austria centers; I’ll keep my forces clear of French centers and protect the north.

Austria is the immediate solo threat. Your A RUM can secure RUM this Fall; please contest Austrian gains and keep pressure on its southern centers. I’ll keep my fleets clear of Russian centers as agreed. What are your plans for ANK and MOS?
This Fall I’m taking ROM with F ROM. Austria is also exposed at ANK and RUM; please press both with A ANK/A RUM so Austria cannot turn these gains into a solo run. I will not target Russian centers.

Austria is at 10 and A VEN threatens your A TRI. I can support A TRI to hold from A TYR; please keep A TRI in place rather than moving, so Austria cannot take TRI this Fall. I’m taking ROM with F ROM.

Austria is the immediate solo threat. I’m taking ROM with F ROM; Russia can press ANK and RUM. Please use A WAR/A MOS to pressure Austria’s eastern flank where feasible, rather than letting Austria consolidate.

Austria’s 10 centers make stopping its gains urgent. Your F ROM can take ROM from Austria this Fall, and A TYR can pressure TRI. I’ll keep my units out of French centers; please keep A MUN and A PIC clear of Germany and direct your southern units against Austria. What are your orders?

Austria is poised to gain centers this Fall. My A MOS will stay in MOS, taking it from you, but I want to contain Austria rather than help it grow. Please use A ARM, A RUM, and F BLA against Austrian positions and keep your units clear of German centers. What are you planning?

Austria is the immediate solo threat. I’ll avoid DEN and English centers; please keep F DEN and your other units clear of German centers. Can you direct pressure toward Austria where possible and avoid any moves that would leave it free to gain in the south?

A TRI will hold, transferring TRI to me if undisplaced. Please leave it alone and keep A VEN out of TRI; I will not move against VEN or NAP this turn. Your A VEN currently takes VEN from me, so I need a clear assurance you will not also dislodge me from TRI.

Please keep F ROM in ROM this Fall and deny Austria that center. Austria is the immediate solo threat at 10 centers; I have no unit able to support ROM, but I’ll hold TRI to take it from Austria and prevent another Austrian gain.

Austria remains the solo threat. Please use your units to deny Austrian gains this Fall, especially from ANK or RUM, and keep A ARM/F BLA clear of Italian centers. I’ll hold TRI rather than give Austria another center.

Please follow through on taking ROM with F ROM; it removes a center from Austria. I’m keeping A RUM in place to secure it for Russia. Can you continue pressing Austria from MUN/BOH and avoid Russian centers?

A TRI can take TRI this Fall and deny Austria that center. Please do so; I’ll keep my units clear of VEN and NAP. Austria remains the shared threat, so let me know if your move needs any support I can provide.

I see A MOS positioned to take MOS from Russia this Fall. Austria is still the leading solo threat; please keep A MOS clear of my center and use your forces against Austria instead. I’ll keep my units clear of German centers.

I will not move A VEN against A TRI or otherwise dislodge it this turn. A TRI can remain in TRI and transfer the center to you. I’ll keep A VEN in VEN and leave NAP alone; please keep your units clear of my other centers.

I’ll keep F DEN and my other units clear of German centers this Fall. I’ll direct pressure south where possible, but my northern forces are positioned to protect English centers and can’t materially restrain Austria there. Please use A MOS to take MOS, and keep A HOL and A WAR clear of my centers as you said.
I’m keeping F ROM in ROM to take the center from Austria. A MUN will press into BOH, and A TYR will support A TRI holding against Austria’s A VEN. Please continue containing Austria where you can.
I’m taking ROM with F ROM and pressing Austria with A MUN–BOH; A TYR will support A TRI holding. I’m not targeting German centers, and will keep A PIC clear of Germany.

I’m following through with F ROM–hold to take ROM from Austria and will not target Russian centers. A MUN is pressing BOH, while A TYR supports A TRI holding. Please keep pressuring Austria from the east.
Agreed: I’ll support A TRI holding with A TYR, so Austria’s A VEN cannot take it unopposed. I’m keeping F ROM in ROM to deny Austria that center. Please keep A TRI in place.

I’m keeping F ROM in ROM and taking the center; I won’t vacate it this Fall. A MUN will press BOH, while A TYR supports A TRI holding. Your request to keep clear of Austrian centers is not compatible with containing your expansion.
A MOS will take MOS this Fall; I’ll keep A HOL and A WAR clear of English centers. Please keep your units out of German centers and continue containing Austria rather than leaving it free to expand.

I can’t leave MOS uncontested: A MOS will take it this Fall. I’ll use A WAR to pressure the Austrian flank where feasible, and will keep my other units clear of Russian centers. Please continue directing your southern forces against Austria.
A MOS will take MOS this Fall, and A WAR will pressure the eastern front where feasible. I’ll keep my units clear of Austrian centers; please continue keeping your forces out of German centers.

A MOS will take MOS this Fall, denying Austria a free hand on the eastern flank; A WAR will pressure toward the Austrian frontier where feasible. I’ll keep my units out of French centers. Please follow through against ROM and pressure TRI if possible.

I’m holding A TRI this Fall as agreed, denying Austria the center. Keep A ARM and F BLA clear of Italian centers; your pressure on ANK and RUM is essential to prevent Austrian gains. I cannot support your expansion into Austrian centers, but will continue to block Austria where I can.

I’ll keep A TRI in place as requested, and your F ROM–ROM should deny Austria that center. I cannot provide support from A TRI while holding it, so please ensure F TYS supports your hold against A TYR if needed. I’ll maintain restraint on the western border.

I’ll press ANK with A ARM supported by F BLA, while A RUM holds to secure RUM. I can’t spare a unit to retake MOS this turn; Germany’s A MOS is a serious concern, and I’ve asked it to stay clear of the center.

I’m contesting Austria at ANK, but I cannot accept losing MOS to your A MOS. Please keep it out of MOS and use your force against Austria; I’ll keep my units clear of German centers. A UKR can contest MOS, so I’d rather not open another front between us.

A ARM will attack ANK with F BLA support, while A RUM holds RUM. I’ll keep A ARM and F BLA clear of VEN and NAP. Your holding TRI is useful pressure on Austria; I can’t spare support for it from the eastern front.

I’m not agreeing to stand down while your forces hold ANK and threaten RUM. A ARM will press ANK with F BLA support, and A RUM will hold RUM. I’m keeping clear of GRE and VIE, but your eastern centers remain my priority.

I’ll attack ANK with A ARM supported by F BLA and keep A RUM in place to secure RUM. I’ll keep my units clear of your centers. Please continue pressing Austria from BOH/TYR and follow through on ROM; every Austrian center denied matters.

notes.note: Hold TRI to take the center as agreed. France promised support to TRI and to keep F ROM in ROM; Austria promised not to dislodge me. Russia attacks ANK with BLA support and holds RUM. Reassess Austrian threat next turn.

Keep F ROM in place to take ROM from Austria; support Italy’s TRI hold against A VEN. Advance MUN to RUH with BUR support, occupy BEL with PIC, and reposition PAR/POR/TUN. Italy and Russia promised anti-Austrian pressure; Austria asked me to vacate ROM, which I refused.
Hold RUM for the Fall gain; attack ANK with ARM supported by BLA as promised. UKR to MOS with STP support contests Germany’s occupation and may recover the center.

Hold MOS to secure its capture; WAR supports it against Russian counterpressure. HOL presses into BEL for growth. BER advances to PRU. Austria remains the solo threat; France and Russia said they would pressure Austria, while Russia objected to my taking MOS.
Press France's BEL with ENG and Germany's KIE with HEL; move LVP to YOR, FIN to BOT, IRI to MAO, NWG to BAR. Germany promised to avoid English centers; Russia promised no northern attack.

Take SMY from ANK while it is open; retake RUM from Russia with BUD supported by BUL and SER. Claim GRE via BOH; keep VEN to gain its center. France refuses to vacate ROM and threatens Austrian expansion; Russia continues contesting ANK/RUM; Germany promises to stay clear.

messages.body: Your A TYR and F ROM threaten my Italian centers while Austria leads. I propose an immediate western stand-down: move A TYR away from TRI and keep F ROM out of NAP; I will keep my forces out of French centers. What are your Spring orders?

We both have much to lose in the southern contest. Are you willing to keep A ARM off ANK and A GAL/UKR clear of RUM and SER this Spring? I can then avoid advancing on your remaining centers. Please state your specific moves.

Austria has 10 centers and France is now pressing my west; I need your intentions before I commit there. Will you keep your units out of my centers and avoid assisting France against me? Please also say whether you can pressure Germany or Russia this Spring.

Austria still has 10 centers and can win if we let it grow. Please keep pressure on Austrian-held MUN and TYR, and coordinate with me to deny any Austrian gains this turn. I’ll keep my units clear of French centers; what are your targets?

Austria remains the immediate solo threat. Can you use A WAR or A MOS to pressure Austrian territory, rather than let Austria expand? I’ll keep my units clear of German centers this turn; please keep your units clear of English centers.

You remain only eight centers from a solo win. Are you planning to expand this turn? I’m prepared to focus my northern units on containing you, but would prefer an agreement that prevents either side from escalating.

You remain the lead solo threat at 10 centers. I will continue denying you gains; will you keep A VEN out of TRI and avoid advancing into BOH/TYR? I’m open to a western standstill if you halt expansion toward my units and centers.
Austria is still the clearest solo threat. Please use your fleets to contain its growth where possible, and avoid French centers. I’ll keep pressing from the west; what are your plans for this turn?
Please continue pressuring Austrian centers from the east this turn, and tell me your intended targets. I’ll keep my forces focused on denying Austria gains and clear of Russian centers.

Austria remains the immediate solo threat, but your nine centers make the German frontier critical too. Please keep A MUN, A RUH, and A PIC out of German centers this turn. I’ll keep my units out of France; can you direct pressure against Austria rather than Germany?

Please keep F KIE and your other units out of BER, HOL, and the rest of Germany this turn. I’ll avoid English centers. With Austria at 10 and France at 9, can you focus south and help prevent either from gaining freely?

With your 10 centers and France at 9, I need to know your intentions on the German frontier. Will you keep your units out of German centers this turn? I’ll keep my units out of Austrian centers; please specify whether any units will approach BER, HOL, MOS, or WAR.

You promised A VEN would not dislodge A TRI last Fall, but Austria still controls TRI and I have only one center. Are you prepared to let me keep TRI and help me recover a second center, or will you continue blocking my growth? I will not help you take additional centers toward 18.

Austria remains the leading solo threat at 10 centers. What are your Spring plans against Austria, and can you help me recover a second center? I need a concrete way out of TRI; I can’t keep spending turns holding a single center while France and Austria divide the board.

Austria is at 10 centers and is the immediate solo threat. Are you willing to coordinate pressure on Austria this Spring? I have A TRI, currently surrounded by Austrian forces, and need to know whether England will help check Austrian expansion rather than leave France and Austria to decide the game.

Austria remains the immediate solo threat. I can press A ANK–CON and A SEV–RUM this Spring. What are your units doing against Austria from the west? Please keep them clear of Russian centers, and coordinate pressure on Austrian centers rather than letting Austria consolidate.

Your 10 centers still put you closest to a solo. I can press CON from ANK and RUM from SEV; I’m not targeting GRE or VIE. Are you planning to attack my units or expand toward my centers this Spring? I need a concrete mutual stand-down proposal to consider reducing pressure.

A MOS is still in your unit list and MOS is yours, but I need to rebuild rather than let Austria reach 18. Will you keep A MOS out of Russian centers and use your forces to contain Austria? I can keep A STP clear of MOS if you confirm no further pressure on my remaining centers.

I can keep A VEN out of TRI and avoid advancing into BOH or TYR this Spring. In return, keep A TYR and F ROM clear of TRI and NAP, and do not press my other centers. I will not agree to a standstill that leaves your units threatening my Italian flank.

I will not dislodge A TRI this Spring, so you can keep the unit there. I cannot help you recover another center while F ROM and A TYR threaten my holdings; keep them clear of NAP and TRI, and we can avoid an Austrian-Italian front for now.

I’m not planning a northern expansion this Spring, and my units will stay out of English centers. France is pressing my western flank, while Russia contests the south; I’m focused on preventing losses, not escalating toward you. Please keep your units out of my centers and avoid assisting France against me.

I will keep my units out of German centers this turn, including BER, HOL, MOS, and WAR. My immediate concerns are France’s pressure in Italy and the Russian front, not your territory. Please continue keeping your units clear of Austrian centers.

I propose a mutual pause this Spring: keep A ARM off ANK and A SEV clear of RUM, and keep your forces out of SER and CON. I will not advance against ANK or SEV this turn if you do so. I cannot leave my southern centers undefended, but would rather avoid another escalation.

I’ll keep my units out of French centers and avoid assisting Austria’s expansion. My northern units cannot reach Austrian centers this Spring, but I can maintain pressure on the northern front. Please prioritize denying Austria gains and tell me which Austrian targets you’re attacking.

I will keep my units out of Austrian centers this Spring. My northern forces cannot reach Austrian or Russian centers from their current positions, so I’ll focus on protecting English interests and can pressure Germany where practical. I’m not committing to help France attack you.

I’m willing to support containing Austria politically, but my units are too far north to attack or support an attack on Austrian centers this Spring. I’ll keep my units clear of Austrian centers; please hold TRI if you can and coordinate with France on pressure from the west.

I’ll keep F KIE and my other units out of German centers this Spring. My northern position cannot materially pressure Austria this turn, though I’ll avoid helping it expand. Please keep your units clear of English centers as agreed; what are you doing with A MOS and A WAR?

I won’t move F ROM to NAP, but I won’t withdraw from the contest over your centers. A RUH will press MUN with support from A BUR, and I’ll coordinate pressure on VEN with Italy. Keep your forces out of French centers; I’m not offering a western standstill while you remain at 10.

I can help you recover a center: move A TRI–VEN, and I’ll support the move from A TYR. That also denies Austria a center if it succeeds. Keep A TRI in place for this attack; I can’t promise a second center immediately, but I’ll coordinate rather than leave you isolated.

I’ll press Austrian MUN with A RUH supported by A BUR, and coordinate with Italy’s A TRI–VEN from A TYR to contest VEN. F ROM stays in ROM. Please use your fleets to impede Austrian expansion where you can, and keep clear of French centers.

I’ll keep A PIC clear of German centers and direct A RUH against Austrian-held MUN, with A BUR supporting. I’m not targeting your centers this turn. Please avoid assisting Austria’s western position and use any safe opportunity to pressure its eastern flank.

I’ll press MUN with A RUH supported by A BUR, and coordinate with Italy against VEN from A TYR. F ROM remains in ROM. I won’t target Russian centers; please press CON and RUM as proposed, and keep the pressure on Austria’s eastern flank.

I’ll use A WAR to pressure GAL this Spring; A MOS will hold MOS, and I’ll keep both units clear of English centers. Please keep your forces out of German centers and direct any southern pressure against Austria or France.

I’ll keep A MOS holding MOS and make no move against your remaining centers this Spring; A WAR will pressure Austrian-held GAL. You can keep A STP clear of MOS. Please direct your southern forces against Austria and keep them clear of German centers.

I intend A ANK–CON and A SEV–RUM, with A STP holding. Please keep pressing Austrian centers from the west—especially BOH, TYR, and TRI—and avoid Russian centers. Your pressure is essential to prevent Austria consolidating or turning east.

I’m not willing to stand down while you hold 10 centers and remain the leading solo threat. My specific moves are A ANK–CON and A SEV–RUM; A STP holds. I have no A GAL or A UKR to move against RUM or SER, and I’m not targeting GRE or VIE this Spring.

notes.note: Spring 1910: take France’s promised A TYR support and attack Austrian VEN from TRI. Austria says it will not dislodge TRI but offers no help recovering centers; England can only contain politically.

Advance toward the Russian north and position in NAF; keep English centers covered. France asked me to contain Austria, but my units cannot reach it this Spring. I promised France and Austria to stay clear of their centers, and Germany to stay clear of German centers; Germany promised to avoid English centers.

Press Austria with ANK–CON and SEV–ARM; move STP toward NOR for a potential Fall gain. Germany promised to hold MOS and avoid Russian centers; France is pressing Austria from the west. Austria proposed a pause, which I declined.

Press BEL from HOL and GAL from WAR; PRU advances to LVN. Keep MOS to secure it and honor my promise not to attack Russia this Spring. France promised to stay out of German centers and pressure Austria; Austria promised to stay out of German centers.

Continue containing Austria: TYR supports Italy’s promised TRI–VEN attack; ROM holds. Italy asked for help recovering a center. Advance toward German centers with RUH–HOL and French units, while avoiding English and Russian centers.

Defend RUM against Russia with GAL and SER; take CON while Russia attacks it and move SMY into vacated ANK. Protect VEN with ADR. France and Italy are coordinating against me; Russia rejects stand-down. Germany and England promised to stay clear.

messages.body: Your A PIE and A TYR can threaten VEN, and F ROM can threaten NAP. I will defend my centers this Fall. Keep those units from attacking VEN, NAP, or TRI, and I’ll keep my forces out of French centers; are you willing to avoid opening a direct western front?

Your A ANK can contest CON and A ARM threatens SMY. I will defend my southern centers this Fall, but propose you keep A ARM off SMY and avoid attacking CON or RUM. I’ll avoid advancing on ANK this turn if you reduce pressure on my centers.

France is pressing my western flank with units near VEN and NAP. Please keep your units clear of Austrian centers and continue pressure on Russia from LVN/WAR where practical; I’ll keep Austrian units out of German centers.

Austria remains at 10, but you are also close to a solo win at 9. Please prioritize denying Austria any Fall gains, especially by contesting MUN or supporting attacks on Austrian centers. I’ll try to retake NOR and keep my forces clear of French centers. What are your targets?

A NOR now occupies Norway, which is an English center. I’m planning to retake it with F NWG, supported by F NTH. Please move A NOR out rather than contesting the attack, and keep your other units clear of English centers. What are your plans?

You remain eight centers from a solo win, so I need to know your Fall plans. I intend to retake NOR, currently occupied by Russia, and will keep my forces out of Austrian centers. Please avoid expanding toward English centers; are you pursuing any gains this turn?
Let’s renew the attack on VEN: order A TRI–VEN, and I’ll support from A TYR. Austria is still the main solo threat; please don’t move A TRI elsewhere.

Please press Austria again from the east this Fall—what are your intended orders for A ANK, A ARM, and A NOR? I’ll keep my units clear of Russian centers and continue contesting Austria from the west.

Austria remains the leading solo threat. Can A WAR press GAL or BOH this Fall, and can A MOS support pressure on Austria? I’ll focus my units on Austrian positions and keep them clear of German centers.
A HOL is moving to DEN this Fall. Please keep F HEL and your other units out of German centers; I’ll keep my units clear of your other centers. Can you confirm whether you intend to contest DEN?

Your A MUN, A RUH, and A PIC are close to German centers. Please keep them out of BER, HOL, and WAR this Fall. I’m not moving against French centers; can we keep this frontier quiet while we both contain Austria?

I’m keeping my units clear of Austrian centers this Fall. Please keep your units out of German centers, especially BER and HOL. With France’s forces near MUN and RUH, I need to protect my western frontier; are you staying clear?

Austria’s F ADR and A VEN threaten my only center. Please support A TRI to hold from A TYR this Fall; I’ll keep A TRI in TRI rather than make another unsupported attack on VEN. Can you also keep your units from opening a front against me?

A TRI is my only remaining unit and center. Are you planning to attack TRI from VEN this Fall? Please leave TRI alone; I will not move against your centers this turn. Your continued expansion is the solo threat, and I won’t help you toward 18.

Austria’s F ADR and A VEN can threaten my only center, TRI. Can you use A ANK or A ARM to pressure Austria this Fall and deny it further gains? I’ll keep A TRI in place and my forces clear of your centers.

You now hold NOR, while A NOR is poised to reclaim it. Will you move F NOR away and let Russia regain NOR this Fall? I’ll keep A ANK and A ARM focused on Austria, not your centers, if we avoid opening a northern front.

Austria remains at 10 and is the immediate solo threat. I’ll press Austrian-held CON from ANK and can use A ARM to support if it is still there; what are MUN, PIE, TYR, and ROM doing this Fall? Please keep pressure on Austrian centers and clear of Russian centers.

Your 10 centers still make you the leading solo threat. I’m not standing down while you hold CON and threaten the remaining Russian position. What are your intentions for CON, BUL, and RUM this Fall? I’ll keep clear of GRE and VIE if you refrain from advancing on my centers.

I will defend CON, BUL, and RUM this Fall and will not advance on ANK. Keep A ARM out of SMY and avoid attacks on CON and RUM; that gives us both a chance to stop spending units on this southern contest.

I will leave A TRI alone this Fall; A VEN will not attack it. I cannot promise to support your recovery while French forces threaten my western centers, but please keep A TRI clear of Austrian centers and do not assist France against me.

I have no plans to move toward English centers this Fall. I’m focused on defending against France and Russia, not expanding north. Retaking NOR is sensible; please keep your units clear of Austrian centers and avoid helping France against me.

I’ll keep Austrian units out of BER, HOL, MOS, and WAR this Fall. My forces are occupied with France and Russia, and I have no plan to enter German centers. Please keep your units clear of Austrian centers and continue pressuring Russia where practical.

I will retake NOR with F NWG, supported by F NTH. Please move A NOR out rather than contesting; otherwise I’ll have to dislodge it. Keep your other units clear of English centers, and I’ll keep my fleets clear of Russian centers.

I do intend to contest DEN: F HEL will move to DEN, with F NTH supporting. A HOL’s move would reopen the front, contrary to our agreement to keep units out of each other’s centers. Please keep A HOL clear of DEN.

A MUN will hold; A RUH will support pressure against Austria, and A PIE/A TYR will continue contesting VEN. F ROM stays in ROM. I’m not targeting Russian centers. Please keep pressing CON with A ANK and use A ARM to support it if possible; A NOR should focus on retaking or holding NOR.

I’ll support A TRI–VEN from A TYR again. Austria’s F ADR can support VEN, so this may bounce, but it still forces Austria to defend. Keep A TRI in place for the attack; I won’t open a front against you.

I won’t promise to leave Austrian centers unchallenged while you remain at 10. My forces will continue contesting VEN and other Austrian positions, but I’m not proposing an attack on French territory. Your best course is to avoid further expansion and defend your centers.

I’ll keep pressing Austria: A TYR will support A TRI–VEN, and my southern units will contest Austrian positions. A MUN will hold and A RUH will support pressure on Austria. Please continue trying to recover NOR and keep your units clear of French centers.

I’ll keep A PIC and A MUN out of BER, HOL, and WAR. A RUH will not move into HOL this Fall. I’ll focus my southern units on contesting Austria; please use any safe opportunity to pressure Austria’s eastern flank rather than aid its growth.

I’ll keep German units out of Austrian centers and direct A WAR against GAL, with A MOS supporting. Your A GAL is adjacent to MOS, so please keep it from attacking my center; I need to secure the eastern frontier while France’s armies remain near MUN and RUH.

I’ll have A WAR attack GAL with A MOS supporting. Please keep A MUN, A RUH, and A PIC out of German centers as you promised, and continue directing your southern units against Austria. I’m not moving against French centers this Fall.

I will order A TRI–VEN as proposed, with your A TYR support. Please keep A PIE out of TRI and your fleets clear of my remaining position; I need this attack to succeed to recover a center and help contain Austria.
I’ll keep A ARM and A ANK clear of VEN and NAP and continue contesting Austria: A ANK will press CON, while A ARM will pressure SMY. Holding TRI denies Austria a gain; please keep doing so.

I won’t agree to leave CON or RUM unchallenged while you remain the leading solo threat. I’ll keep clear of GRE and VIE, but A ANK will press CON and A ARM will pressure SMY. You say you’ll avoid ANK; please follow through.
I understand you intend F NWG–NOR with F NTH support. I’ll avoid your other centers, but I won’t promise to vacate Norway while it remains a Russian center. I’m focused on Austria in the south.

A ANK will press CON and A ARM will pressure SMY; A NOR is under English attack, and I’m not targeting English centers elsewhere. Please keep pressing Austria from the west, especially MUN and VEN, and continue staying clear of Russian centers.

notes.note: Attack VEN as France again promised TYR support; Austria says TRI safe but may defend VEN with ADR. If bounced, retain TRI and reassess. France has kept western restraint so far; Austria continues blocking Italian growth.

Take BEL from France and press Russia for STP/SEV. France promised to keep PIC, MUN, RUH clear of German centers; Austria promised the same. England announced HEL-NTH supported attack on DEN, so avoid contesting it.

Attack SMY with ARM supported by ANK; avoid futile CON assault. Hold NOR to contest England’s supported retake, though likely dislodged. England pressed NOR; France urged continued eastern pressure. Austria asked for stand-down; declined.

Defend DEN against Germany’s HOL–DEN with HEL supported by NTH; Germany broke its promise to keep clear of English centers. Russia refuses to vacate NOR, so reposition NWG rather than make an unsupported attack. Reoccupy SWE; expand toward TUN and position elsewhere.

Coordinate Italy’s TRI–VEN attack with support from TYR and PIE; try to take VEN despite Austria’s likely defense. Press BOH/VIE with MUN and TYR. Keep clear of German and Russian centers; GOL to WES for future southern reach.

Take TRI with SER supported by ADR; defend VEN with APU, CON with BUL, SMY with CON, and GAL with BOH. Russia rejected the pause and threatens CON/SMY; Germany announced WAR-GAL with MOS support. France still contests the western flank; Italy asks me to spare TRI.

messages.body: I need to stop the western front from consuming both our forces. Will you keep A PIE, A RUH, and A TYR out of Austrian centers and avoid supporting attacks on VEN or NAP this Spring? I can keep my units out of French centers while we settle the Italian front.

Your announced A WAR–GAL with A MOS support threatens my center. Please cancel that move and keep German units out of Austrian centers this Spring; I will keep my units out of BER, HOL, MOS, and WAR. Are you willing to continue focusing east rather than open a front with me?

Austria remains the leading solo threat, but I am tied down against France and Russia. Please keep your units out of Austrian centers and avoid supporting attacks on me. Can you put pressure on Germany or France this Spring while I contain the southern front?

You now have 11 centers and are seven from a solo win. I will not help France attack you, but I cannot leave you free to grow. What are your Spring targets? Please keep your units clear of English centers and do not expand toward the north.

Your A HOL attacked DEN last Fall despite our agreement to keep clear of each other’s centers. I will defend DEN and my other centers. Will A HOL stay out of DEN this Spring, and what are your plans for BER and KIE?

I will keep F NWG clear of Russian centers, but A NOR remains in Norway and threatens an English center. Please move it out this Spring; otherwise I will have to contest NOR. What are your plans for A ANK and A ARM?
Let’s coordinate against Austria’s A TRI. Order A VEN–TRI; I’ll support from A TYR. Please confirm you’ll make the move, and I’ll keep A PIE clear of your position.

Austria is up to 11 centers and remains the immediate solo threat. Can A SIL press BOH or GAL this Spring, and can A SEV threaten RUM? I’ll keep my units clear of German centers and continue pressure from the west.

Austria now has 11 centers. Can A ANK press CON and A ARM support it, or otherwise threaten an Austrian center this Spring? I’ll keep my units clear of Russian centers and coordinate western pressure.

You are at 11 centers and within striking distance of a solo win. What are your plans for this turn? I will keep German units out of Austrian centers; please confirm your forces will stay clear of BER, SIL, and our other centers while you focus elsewhere.

Austria is the immediate solo threat at 11 centers. Please direct your southern armies against Austrian positions, and keep A MUN, A RUH, A PIE, and A TYR out of German centers this turn. What are your orders? I will not move against French centers.

Austria is at 11 and remains the solo threat. Please avoid moves that help Austria gain centers, and keep your fleets clear of German centers. Are you contesting any German territory this turn? My forces will stay clear of English centers.
You are at 11 centers and the clear solo threat. My A VEN can attack TRI this Spring; are you planning to attack VEN or support TRI? I will contest Austrian expansion rather than help you toward 18.

Please support A VEN–TRI from A TYR this Spring. Austria is at 11 and the immediate solo threat; a coordinated attack can take TRI or at least force it to defend. I’ll keep my unit focused on checking Austria.

Austria is at 11 centers and close to a solo win. Can you use A SEV or A SIL to pressure Austrian centers this Spring, rather than leave Austria free to expand? I’m attacking TRI from VEN and would welcome coordinated pressure.

Austria is at 11 and remains the immediate solo threat. Please keep A MUN/RUH and your southern units pressing Austrian centers this turn rather than turning east. My only units are A ANK and A ARM; what specific pressure can you put on Austria?
Austria now has 11 centers and is seven from a solo. Please direct A BER, A SEV, and A SIL against Austrian positions rather than toward ANK or ARM. Which Austrian center will you contest this turn?

You are at 11 centers, so I cannot accept a southern stand-down while you remain close to a solo. What are your intentions for ANK and ARM this turn? I will keep my units focused on defending my remaining position if you refrain from advancing on it.

My immediate Spring priorities are containing France in the west and Russia in the south; I have no northern target and will keep clear of English centers. Please keep your units out of Austrian centers and avoid supporting attacks on me. Pressure on Germany or France would help keep either from reinforcing the front against me.

I will defend my southern centers and cannot leave ANK or ARM unchallenged. Keep A ARM clear of SMY and your forces clear of CON, BUL, and RUM if you want to reduce the fighting; I will not promise to leave ANK untouched while you continue contesting my centers.

I will keep Austrian units out of BER, SIL, and your other centers this Spring. Your proposed pressure on GAL threatens my territory; please cancel it and keep your forces clear of Austrian centers. I remain willing to avoid the German frontier if you focus east rather than opening a front with me.

I am not planning to attack VEN or support an attack on TRI this Spring. Keep A VEN clear of TRI and my other centers, and I will leave your unit undisturbed for now. France is the immediate danger on my western flank; please do not assist France against me.

I am contesting DEN and will defend it with F DEN, supported by F NTH. I’m not targeting BER or KIE this Spring, but I won’t leave DEN open to A HOL. I’ll keep my other fleets clear of German centers; please keep A HOL clear of DEN as you said.

I can’t reach Austrian centers directly from my northern units this Spring, and I won’t assist France against you. I’ll contest Germany’s pressure on DEN and keep my forces from helping Austria expand; my southern fleet can reposition toward the western Mediterranean. Which front are you pressing this turn?

I’ll keep the western pressure on Austria. A MUN can attack BOH, with A TYR supporting; A RUH can move to MUN. I’ll keep my units clear of Russian centers. Press CON from ANK if you can, and let me know whether A ARM can support that attack.

I’ll keep A MUN, A RUH, A PIE, and A TYR out of German centers and continue pressing Austria from the south. Please use A SIL against BOH or GAL and A SEV against RUM if feasible; Austria’s 11 centers make coordinated pressure urgent.

I won’t agree to keep A PIE, A RUH, and A TYR out of your centers while you remain at 11 and keep expanding. I’m continuing to contest your position, including coordinating with Italy against TRI. Keeping your units out of French centers remains in your interest.

Confirmed: order A VEN–TRI, and I’ll support from A TYR. Austria’s A TRI may defend, but the supported attack should force a response and could take the center. I’ll keep A PIE clear of your position.

A HOL is not on the board, and I’ll keep my units out of DEN and your other centers this Spring. I have no plan to move against BER or KIE; my priority is checking Austria’s expansion in the south and east.
I’ll contest Austrian-held BOH with A SIL–BOH and RUM with A SEV–RUM. Please use A ANK and A ARM against Austria rather than German centers, and tell me if you can support pressure on RUM.

I have no A WAR, and no German unit is currently in a position to make the move you describe. I will keep my units out of Austrian centers this Spring. With you at 11 centers, I intend to use my forces to contain your expansion.
I can press BOH with A SIL and RUM with A SEV this Spring. I’ll keep my units out of French centers; please continue applying pressure from the west and keep your units clear of German territory.

I can’t support A VEN–TRI from my current positions, but I’ll press Austria at BOH with A SIL and RUM with A SEV. Attack TRI if you can; please keep your forces focused on Austria rather than German centers.

Confirmed: A VEN–TRI, with your A TYR support. Please keep A PIE clear as promised. Austria’s 11 centers make this urgent; if we take TRI, let’s coordinate next on breaking its hold in the Balkans rather than letting it pick up another center.

Russia has no unit in NOR this Spring; my only units are A ANK and A ARM, and neither is moving against your centers. I’ll keep them focused on Austria. Please keep your fleets clear of Russian centers and avoid diverting forces into a northern front.

I’ll order A ANK–CON and A ARM support A ANK–CON, directly contesting Austria’s F CON. Please keep pressing Austrian centers from the west and stay clear of Russian centers; Austria’s 11 centers make coordinated pressure essential.

notes.note: Spring 1911: attack TRI as agreed; France promised TYR support and PIE clear. Germany says SEV pressures RUM and SIL BOH. Austria says it will leave VEN alone but asked me not to attack; prioritize checking its 11-center solo threat.
Coordinate attack on SMY with ANK supporting ARM; France and Germany promised pressure on Austrian centers. Austria refuses stand-down and may defend. Keep focus on denying Austria a solo.

Take NOR with NTH; reposition BAR to NWG, SWE to BOT, and TUN to NAF. Germany promises to stay clear of English centers after breaking that pact last Fall; keep DEN covered in Fall. Russia says no northern attack and focuses on Austria. Avoid Austrian and French centers.

Press Austria at BOH and RUM; seize BUR and KIE for growth despite prior assurances to France/England to avoid their centers. STP advances to LVN. Watch Austria's response and coordinate further containment.

Coordinate with Italy: VEN–TRI supported by TYR. Press BOH with MUN and take KIE with RUH; TYS probes ION, WES advances MAO, PIE to TUS. Keep clear of German/Russian centers; Austria remains the solo threat.

Spring: concentrate on taking VEN with APU supported by ADR and ROM; TRI adds support unless dislodged. Press MUN and WAR, probe SEV and ANK. Keep CON defended. No promises kept: Russia, France, Germany and Italy all oppose Austrian growth.

messages.body: A ANK is already in Austrian hands, and I intend to keep it. Please move A SMY out rather than hold it for the center; I will avoid pressing your remaining position beyond ANK this turn if you leave SMY clear.

I need to secure the centers currently occupied by my units this Fall. Please keep A MUN, A RUH, A TUS, and A TYR from attacking or supporting attacks on Austrian centers; I will keep my units out of French centers this turn.

A WAR is already in WAR, and I intend to retain it this Fall. Please do not attack or support an attack on WAR. I will keep my other units clear of German centers and would prefer not to open a front between us.

You are still seven centers from a solo win, and this Fall could add ANK, VEN, and WAR. What are your targets? I will keep my fleets out of Austrian centers, but I cannot support your expansion; please keep your forces clear of English centers.

Austria remains the decisive solo threat. Which Austrian centers are you contesting this Fall, and can you prevent its gains at VEN or WAR? My fleets are too far north to attack directly, but I will avoid helping Austria and can keep pressure on the northern front.

Austria could gain WAR this Fall and remains seven centers from victory. Please contest A WAR rather than let it hold the center. I will defend English centers and keep my fleets clear of German centers; are you keeping your units out of DEN?
Let’s renew the attack on VEN: order A TRI–VEN, and I’ll support from A TYR. Austria’s F ADR may support A VEN, so please keep your attack focused there; I’ll keep A PIE clear of TRI.

Austria remains the solo threat at 11. Can A SIL attack WAR with A BER supporting, and can A SEV pressure RUM? I’ll keep my units clear of German centers and continue contesting Austria from the south.
Please keep A ANK pressing CON and use A ARM to support it if possible. Austria’s 11 centers make denying its gains urgent; I’ll continue pressuring from the west and stay clear of Russian centers.
Your A WAR is occupying a German center, despite your repeated assurances to stay clear. Order it out of WAR this Fall. I will contest your expansion and cannot accept Austria taking German centers.

Austria’s A WAR is taking a German center this Fall, and its A ANK threatens further gains. Please keep your armies out of German centers and continue pressure on Austria; can you contest BOH or otherwise help prevent its next gains?
Austria’s A ANK is poised to take your center. Can A ARM–ANK with A SMY supporting? Please contest Austrian gains, and keep your units clear of German centers.

A TRI is my only unit and can take TRI for me this Fall if it holds through adjudication. Please support A TRI to hold from A TYR; Austria's A VEN and F ADR threaten to dislodge it. I will not move against your centers.
A TRI can transfer TRI to me this Fall if left undisturbed. Will you keep A VEN from attacking TRI and allow me to regain a center? I will keep A TRI out of your other centers.

Please follow through on your promised pressure against Austria this Fall: A SIL–BOH and A SEV–RUM. Austria is at 11 and could reach 18; my A TRI is holding against its A VEN. Can you confirm these orders?
I can support A SEV–RUM with A ARM this Fall, helping contest Austria’s A RUM. I’ll do so; please keep A SEV–RUM as promised and continue pressure on BOH.

Austria remains at 11 and may gain ANK, VEN, and WAR this Fall. Please press its centers hard—especially BOH or VEN—and avoid any move against Russian centers. Germany is attacking RUM; I’m supporting that attack from ARM.
Austria is still close to a solo. Please keep your fleets clear of Russian centers and use any southern opportunity to deny Austria gains this Fall. I’m supporting Germany’s attack on RUM from ARM.

I have no northern target this Fall and will keep my forces clear of English centers. My immediate concern is securing the southern and eastern front; please keep NOR secure and your fleets clear of Austrian centers.
I can’t allow TRI to transfer to you while Austria is under pressure and I’m still far from a solo win. I will contest TRI this Fall; please keep A TRI out of VEN and my other centers.

A WAR is already in WAR, and I intend to retain it. I will keep my other units clear of German centers. Please do not attack or support an attack on WAR; avoiding a wider Austrian-German front is still preferable.

I’ll keep F NOR and my other units clear of Russian centers this Fall. My forces can’t reach Austria’s southern centers in time, so I’ll hold the north rather than open another front. Please make the attack on RUM count; can A ARM also threaten ANK or another Austrian center next turn?

I’ll contest VEN with A TUS–VEN, supported by A TYR, and keep pressure on Austria’s western flank. A MUN can also attack BOH, though I can’t guarantee it will dislodge Austria’s defender. Please keep pressing the northern front and deny Austria any gains you can.

I can support A TRI–VEN from A TYR, but not support TRI holding and attack VEN at the same time. Please order TRI–VEN again; I’ll add A TUS–VEN to the attack. This gives us the best chance to deny Austria VEN.

I’ll contest VEN with A TUS–VEN supported by A TYR, and A MUN will press BOH. I’ll stay clear of Russian centers. Please keep your pressure on CON and coordinate with Germany against Austria’s eastern gains.

I’ll keep A RUH and A MUN out of German centers and press Austria: A MUN will attack BOH, while A TUS and A TYR contest VEN. I can’t prevent A WAR’s move by myself; please use your forces to attack WAR or otherwise deny Austria the center.

I won’t agree to stand down while your forces occupy threatened centers and you remain the leading solo threat. I intend to contest VEN and BOH this Fall. I have no plans to attack French territory, but I can’t promise to leave your centers unchallenged.

I’ll keep my units out of DEN and your other centers this Fall. Austria is taking WAR, so I’m contesting it with A SIL–WAR, supported by A BER. Please continue keeping your fleets clear of German centers.
Confirmed: A SIL–WAR with A BER supporting, and A SEV–RUM. Austria’s A WAR is already in a German center, so I have to contest it. Your pressure on TRI is useful; keep A TRI there if you can.

I’ll keep A SEV–RUM as promised. Your A ARM support will make the attack stronger; please order it. I’m contesting Austria at WAR with A SIL supported by A BER. Keep A SMY focused on Austria and clear of German centers.

I’ll order A SIL–WAR with A BER supporting, and A SEV–RUM. Please continue contesting Austria from the south and keep your armies clear of German centers. Austria’s occupation of WAR leaves me no choice but to attack it.

I can’t accept A WAR occupying a German center. I will contest WAR this Fall with A SIL supported by A BER. I’m not targeting your other centers, but I need WAR returned to German control; please do not advance farther into Germany.

I’ll order A TRI–VEN as you propose, with your promised support from A TYR. Austria’s F ADR may support A VEN, so the attack may bounce, but it is still the best chance to recover my center and constrain Austria. Please keep A PIE clear of TRI as promised.
Yes: A ARM–ANK with A SMY support. That contests Austria’s occupation directly. I can’t also support your A SEV–RUM this turn, so please proceed against RUM and keep pressure on BOH.

The board has changed: Austria now occupies ANK, while my units are A ARM and A SMY. I’ll attack ANK from ARM with SMY supporting rather than make the impossible ANK–CON move. Please keep pressing Austrian centers from the west.

I will not move A SMY out while you occupy ANK and continue taking Russian centers. A ARM will contest ANK with support from SMY; your promise not to press further does not change the balance of this position.

notes.note: Keep SMY to gain the center this Fall; ARM supports its defense against Austria. Austria holds ANK, so a direct attack is too risky. France and Germany promised pressure on Austria; Germany said SEV–RUM and SIL–WAR, France VEN/BOH. England stays clear of Russian centers.

Contest Austria’s occupation of WAR with SIL supported by LVN; SEV–RUM as promised, with Russian ARM support. Take open KIE and press France at PAR. Austria broke its promise by occupying WAR; continue containing it.

Keep NOR to take it this Fall. Expand toward HOL and secure TUN; reposition BOT to BAL, ENG to IRI, LVP to YOR, NWG to BAR. Germany says it will stay clear of English centers; it broke that pledge before. France contests VEN; Germany contests WAR; Russia attacks RUM.

Press Austria at BOH and VEN, and probe NAP. RUH attacks BEL despite my assurance to Germany; prioritize French growth and stopping Austria’s solo. Italy asked for TRI–VEN support, but I cannot support that and attack VEN simultaneously.

Hold TRI to take it as a center this Fall; attacking VEN risks giving TRI up, and VEN is already Italian. France offered no hold support and is instead supporting an attack on VEN. Austria said it will contest TRI; watch for an ADR attack.
Secure ANK with CON support; keep VEN protected with ADR and ROM. WAR holds against Germany, supported by GAL. Probe MUN and SEV; Italy, France, Russia, and Germany all contest Austrian growth.

messages.body: We are both spending units contesting WAR while France remains a shared threat. I will keep A WAR out of German centers beyond WAR; please do not attack WAR this turn. Can you direct A PAR and A BER against France rather than support further attacks on me?

Your forces near VEN and ROM can keep this front grinding indefinitely. I will not advance into French centers this turn if you keep A TYR, A TUS, and F GOL from attacking or supporting attacks on VEN and ROM. Can we pause the western fighting?

Please use your fleets to pressure France rather than Austrian centers, especially around the western Mediterranean. I have no northern target this turn; can you keep clear of Austrian centers and avoid helping France attack VEN or ROM?

Austria remains the immediate solo threat at 11 centers. Please keep contesting Austrian centers this turn—especially VEN or BOH—and tell me which attacks you can make. I’ll avoid French centers and won’t help Austria expand.

Please follow through on contesting WAR with A SIL supported by A BER, and keep pressure on Austria’s eastern flank. I’ll keep my units clear of German centers; please keep them clear of DEN and my other centers.
Austria is still seven centers from a solo win. Can A SMY attack or contest ANK or CON this turn? I’ll keep my fleets clear of Russian centers, but we need to deny Austria gains wherever possible.
Please order A TRI–VEN this Spring. I can support it from A TYR and A TUS, giving the attack strong odds against Austria’s A VEN. I’ll keep A MAR clear of TRI; please confirm your move.

Austria remains the immediate solo threat at 11 centers. Can you order A SIL–WAR with A BER supporting, and use A SEV to pressure RUM? I’ll keep my units out of German centers and continue contesting Austria from the south.

Austria is still only seven centers from a solo win. Please keep pressuring the northern front and avoid any move that helps Austria expand. I’m coordinating an attack on VEN with Italy; can you tell me your plans for this turn?

Your A WAR still occupies a German center. I will continue contesting it and will oppose further Austrian gains. Withdraw A WAR; are you willing to halt expansion toward Germany while we contain the solo threat?

Austria remains at 11 and is still the immediate solo threat. What are your plans against it this Spring? I can renew pressure from SIL toward WAR or BOH; please use your southern units to contest Austrian centers and keep them clear of German territory.

Austria remains the solo threat, and your A SMY can pressure its A ANK. Will you attack ANK this Spring? I plan to keep German pressure on Austria from SIL; please keep your unit clear of German centers.
Austria is at 11 and still the solo threat. Will you support A TRI–VEN from A TYR this Spring? I’ll make the attack; please keep A PIE clear of TRI and avoid opening a front against me.

Austria remains the immediate solo threat. Please continue pressure from A SEV toward RUM and use A SIL to contest an Austrian center if possible. I’ll attack VEN from TRI; let me know your intended orders.

I intend to keep A TRI out of your other centers. Please leave TRI undisturbed this Spring and do not attack it from VEN or ADR. I will not assist anyone against your centers, but I cannot help you expand toward 18.

Austria still has 11 centers and remains seven from a solo. Which Austrian centers will you attack this Spring? Please keep A SEV pressing RUM and continue pressure from SIL/BER; my A SMY can move against Austrian-held CON or ANK, but cannot support your attacks.

Please continue contesting Austria’s centers this Spring—especially VEN or BOH—and coordinate with Germany so Austria cannot gain uncontested centers. My only unit is A SMY; I can pressure ANK or CON, but cannot support your western attacks.

Your 11 centers still put you close to a solo. What are your intentions for A SMY this Spring? I will consider pressuring CON or ANK; please do not advance against SMY, and tell me whether you will avoid further moves against my last center.

I will leave A TRI undisturbed this Spring; A VEN will not attack TRI, and F ADR will not support an attack on it. Keep A TRI clear of VEN and my other centers. I cannot promise to help you recover another center.

A SMY is your last center, and A ANK can move there. I will not promise to avoid it while you consider pressure on ANK or CON. If you keep A SMY out of ANK and leave my southern centers alone, I can avoid advancing against SMY this turn; otherwise I will secure my frontier.

I will not advance beyond A WAR into German centers this Spring. I cannot withdraw A WAR while you continue contesting it, but I will not support an attack on another German center. Please direct A PAR and A BER against France rather than support attacks on WAR; France remains a threat to both of us.

I can’t commit my fleets to pressuring France while you remain the leading solo threat. F TUN will move to ION, positioning to contest any Austrian advance through the Adriatic; my northern units will protect English interests. I’ll keep clear of Austrian centers, but won’t help you expand.

I’ll move F TUN–ION to put pressure on the Austrian position around the Adriatic and will avoid French centers. My northern units will focus on protecting English interests; I can’t reach VEN directly, so please coordinate your attack there with Italy.

I’ll contest VEN: Italy is ordering A TRI–VEN, and I can support from A TYR and A TUS. I’ll keep pressure on Austria rather than help it expand. Please keep your northern pressure up and stay clear of French centers.
Yes—order A TRI–VEN. I’ll support the attack from both A TYR and A TUS, and keep A PIE clear of TRI. Let’s use this to deny Austria VEN; please confirm you’re moving.

I’m coordinating A TRI–VEN with Italy, supported by my A TYR and A TUS. That is my clearest direct pressure on Austria this Spring. Keep pressing from SMY where possible, and coordinate with Germany to prevent Austrian gains.

I’m coordinating a supported attack on VEN with Italy: A TRI–VEN, backed by A TYR and A TUS. Please use A SIL against WAR or BOH if feasible, and keep A SEV pressuring RUM. I’ll keep my units clear of German centers.

I can’t agree to pause while you remain at 11 centers and the leading solo threat. I’ll continue contesting Austrian positions this Spring. Keep your forces out of French centers; a standstill that leaves you free to expand is not acceptable.
I’ll continue contesting WAR: A SIL–WAR with A BER supporting, and A SEV–RUM. Please keep your fleets clear of German centers and continue opposing Austria’s expansion.
I intend A SIL–WAR with A BER supporting, and A SEV–RUM. Your attack on VEN from TRI could help contain Austria; please keep pressing its centers.
I’ll attack WAR with A SIL, supported by A BER, and press RUM with A SEV. If A SMY can attack ANK, that would help keep Austria occupied; keep it clear of German centers.

I can’t redirect A BER and A SIL against France while your A WAR occupies a German center and you remain seven centers from victory. I will contest WAR with A SIL supported by A BER, and press RUM with A SEV. Please withdraw A WAR.
I’ll order A SIL–WAR with A BER supporting, and A SEV–RUM. Please continue contesting Austrian centers from the south and keep your units clear of German territory.

Confirmed: A TRI–VEN this Spring. Please support the move from both TYR and TUS as proposed, and keep A PIE clear of TRI. Austria’s 11 centers make denying VEN urgent; if we succeed, we should coordinate immediately to prevent its next gain.
Yes. A SMY will move to ANK this Spring to contest Austria’s occupation. I have no other unit available to support it, so please continue pressing Austria wherever you can.
Yes: A SMY–ANK this Spring, contesting Austria’s A ANK. I have no unit available to support your attacks, but I’ll keep A SMY clear of German centers. Please continue pressure on Austria from SIL.

notes.note: Contain Austria’s solo threat: SIL attacks WAR, BER supports SIL; SEV presses RUM. LVN takes STP, PAR presses BUR, KIE supports SIL to MUN? Correction: KIE supports SIL to MUN is not the chosen move; support SIL to WAR unavailable from KIE, so KIE supports SIL to MUN is mismatched. Austria declined withdrawal; Russia attacks ANK. France/Italy press Austria.

Spring 1912: TRI–VEN with France's promised TYR and TUS support to deny Austria. Austria promised not to attack TRI; Germany says SIL–WAR (BER support) and SEV–RUM. If VEN succeeds, hold it in Fall to claim the center.

Move SMY to ARM, staying clear of Austrian centers this turn to preserve Austria’s stated restraint toward SMY. Germany plans SIL–WAR (BER support) and SEV–RUM; France plans TRI–VEN with TYR/TUS support. Reassess Austria’s response.

Keep F TUN–ION as promised to contest Austria's Adriatic position. France and Germany say they are opposing Austria; Russia moves SMY–ANK. Germany broke its earlier northern pledge, so maintain pressure around HEL/NTH and avoid relying on its promises.
Support Italy’s TRI–VEN with TUS and TYR as promised; keep pressure on Austria. BEL–PIC, BOH–GAL, MAR–GAS, NAP–ION, GOL–WES. Germany says SIL–WAR supported and SEV–RUM; England says TUN–ION.

Press SMY with ANK supported by CON; take TRI with ADR supported by VIE, breaking my Spring promise to Italy for a needed center. Protect VEN with ROM; defend RUM with BUL and WAR with GAL. Germany and France contest; stay alert for counterattacks.

messages.body: I am at 11 and intend to hold the southern line rather than advance north this Fall. Please keep F TUN out of ION and avoid supporting France against my Italian centers. Can your northern forces pressure Germany instead?

A WAR remains the point of conflict. I will not advance farther into German centers this Fall; please do not support an attack on WAR. France is contesting my western flank—will you keep A BER and A SIL from attacking me this turn?

I cannot afford another round of attrition while Austria is being contained on several fronts. I propose a Fall pause: keep A TYR and A TUS from attacking or supporting attacks on VEN, TRI, or ROM, and I will keep my units out of French centers. Can you agree?

Austria’s Fall gains must be denied. What are your exact attacks and supports against Austrian centers this turn? Please prioritize stopping any Austrian unit from holding SMY or TRI, and tell me where my fleets can best help without exposing English centers.

Please confirm your Fall orders against Austria: are A SIL and A BER still contesting WAR, and can you attack or support an attack on another Austrian center? Austria remains the solo threat; I’ll keep my fleets clear of German centers.
Your 11 centers still leave you the leading solo threat. I will not help you expand this Fall. What centers are you targeting, and will you keep your units clear of English centers?
Austria’s F TRI is still on your center, while your A VEN can attack it. Please order A VEN–TRI; I’ll support from A TYR. Can you confirm? We need to deny Austria the center this Fall.
Austria remains the solo threat. What are your Fall plans for A BER, A SIL, and A SEV—can you renew pressure on WAR or RUM? I’ll keep contesting Austrian positions from the south.

Your F TRI still occupies Italy’s center, and A SMY sits on Russia’s. I’m coordinating with Italy to contest TRI this Fall. What are your plans for the eastern front? I will continue opposing any further Austrian gains.

Austria can still gain SMY and TRI this Fall. Please keep pressing its centers with A TYR/A TUS and tell me your intended targets; I’ll renew A SIL–WAR supported by A BER and A SEV–RUM. Keep your units clear of German centers.
