Austria’s A SMY and F TRI could secure two centers this Fall. Can A ARM attack ANK or CON to disrupt its gains? I’ll continue A SIL–WAR supported by A BER and A SEV–RUM; please keep your unit clear of German centers.

Austria remains close to a solo and may gain SMY and TRI this Fall. Please use your forces to contest Austrian centers or otherwise prevent those gains, while keeping fleets clear of German centers. I’m continuing pressure on WAR and RUM.
Your promised A TYR and A TUS support for TRI–VEN is crucial. Please confirm you will support the attack this Fall; Austria now has F TRI, so I need the support to dislodge it and reclaim VEN.
Will you attack A VEN this Fall, and what are your intentions for TRI? I will contest your expansion; my A VEN can move to TRI, and I need to know whether you plan to support or attack it.
Austria remains at 11 and is the solo threat. Are A SEV–RUM and pressure from A SIL still your plan this Fall? Please also tell me whether A WAR will continue contesting Austria.

Austria is at 11 and can gain SMY and TRI this Fall. Please keep A SEV–RUM and continue pressure from SIL/BER; your attacks are vital to deny Austria gains. My A ARM can move to SMY to contest its occupation, but cannot support your attacks.

Austria may gain SMY and TRI this Fall. Please keep pressing Austrian centers from the west, and coordinate with Italy to ensure A VEN stays in VEN and denies Austria that center. I’ll use A ARM to contest Austrian control in the south.
Please keep A VEN in VEN this Fall; holding it denies Austria a center. Austria’s F TRI also threatens to take TRI, so if you can contest TRI, do so. Austria is at 11 and every center denied matters.
I intend to keep F TRI in TRI and will not attack A VEN from TRI this Fall. I cannot promise to support your move to TRI; please keep A VEN out of TRI and avoid supporting France against my centers.

My eastern priority is holding SMY and the Balkan line; I am not planning an advance into French centers this Fall. I will defend TRI and my other Italian centers. Please keep A TYR and A TUS from attacking or supporting attacks on them.

I am focused on holding the southern and eastern line, including SMY and TRI, and have no northern target. I will keep my units clear of English centers. Please keep F TUN out of ION and avoid supporting attacks on my Italian centers.

F TUN is still in TUN, and I intend to move it to ION; I won’t withdraw it from the area. My northern forces cannot reach Austrian centers this Fall, and I’m not supporting your expansion. Please keep your units clear of English centers.

I can’t reach an Austrian center with my current units this Fall. F TUN can move to ION to contest the southern position, while my northern fleets must protect English interests. I support your pressure on WAR and RUM; I’ll keep my fleets clear of German centers.
No. I’ll support Italy’s A VEN–TRI with A TYR, contesting your fleet on Italy’s center. I won’t promise a pause while you remain the leading solo threat and hold 11 centers.
I confirm A TYR–support A VEN–TRI this Fall. That is my priority to dislodge Austria’s F TRI and help you recover your center. I can’t support this attack and make a separate supported attack on VEN.

I’m supporting Italy’s A VEN–TRI from A TYR to contest Austria’s F TRI. I can’t reach SMY or support your A ARM from here; please use ARM to challenge Austria directly if possible. I’ll keep pressing Austria from the west.

I’ll support Italy’s A VEN–TRI from A TYR, contesting Austria’s F TRI. I can’t also use TYR to support an attack on VEN. Please renew A SIL–WAR with A BER supporting and A SEV–RUM as you proposed; I’ll keep my units clear of German centers.

I’ll support Italy’s A VEN–TRI from A TYR to contest Austria’s F TRI. I can’t reach SMY, and my units can’t affect Austria’s eastern front directly. I have no way to guarantee Austria loses SMY this turn; please keep pressure on the north and avoid helping Austria.
I will continue contesting WAR with A SIL–WAR supported by A BER, and A SEV–RUM. Your occupation of WAR is still unacceptable, and I won’t promise to leave it unchallenged.
Yes: A SIL–WAR with A BER supporting, and A SEV–RUM. I have no separate unit available to support an attack on another Austrian center. Please keep pressing Austria from the south.
I’ll continue A SIL–WAR supported by A BER and A SEV–RUM. A ARM–SMY would contest Austria’s occupation there; please order it if you can.

I’ll renew A SIL–WAR supported by A BER and A SEV–RUM. Those are my available units for direct pressure on Austria this turn. Please continue contesting Austrian centers and keep your units clear of German territory.
Yes: A SIL–WAR supported by A BER, and A SEV–RUM. I have no separate unit available to attack or support an attack on another Austrian center; I’ll keep my remaining units clear of English centers.

Confirmed: I’ll order A VEN–TRI this Fall. Please support it from A TYR as proposed. I understand this leaves VEN unoccupied, but dislodging Austria’s F TRI is the priority; keep A TUS clear and help prevent Austria supporting the defense from VIE if possible.

I can’t hold A VEN and contest TRI simultaneously. I’m ordering A VEN–TRI, with French support from TYR, to challenge Austria’s F TRI and deny its gain in TRI. Please continue pressuring Austria from the east; I’m not moving against SMY.

I’ll order A ARM–ANK to contest Austria’s A ANK directly; CON is beyond reach this turn. Please proceed with A SIL–WAR supported by A BER and A SEV–RUM as promised. I’ll keep my unit clear of German centers.

notes.note: Attack SMY to contest Austria's occupation and deny its gain if Austria moves. Germany promised SIL–WAR supported by BER and SEV–RUM; France supports Italy VEN–TRI. Italy says it will contest TRI. Austria's earlier restraint was conditional and unreliable.

F1912: Attack TRI with France's promised TYR support to deny Austria TRI; this risks giving up the chance to take VEN, but prevents Austria's growth if successful. France has kept its promise so far; Austria says it will not support TRI.

Take French centers BRE and BEL while keeping TUN–ION as promised to contest Austria. Advance toward CLY; other fleets reposition or cover English centers. Germany says it continues pressure on WAR/RUM; France supports Italy against TRI. Austria asked me to stay out of ION; refused.

Hold SMY and TRI to claim them. GAL supports WAR against Germany; BUL supports RUM against SEV; VIE supports TRI against France/Italy. France rejected the pause and supports Italy; Germany contests WAR and RUM; England refuses aid. Protect the gains.

Press Austria at RUM, but prioritize supported entry into MUN with SIL/BER; BUR takes PAR, KIE presses HOL, STP presses NOR. Austria remains the solo threat; Russia said ARM–ANK, so SMY may still fall to Austria.

Support Italy's VEN–TRI as promised; TUS and NAP coordinate a supported attack on Austrian ROM. Move GAS to MAR and keep PIC on BEL; BOH relocates to MUN. Germany renewed SIL–WAR/BER support and SEV–RUM. Austria requested a pause; refused.

messages.body: F ION is the immediate danger to my southern flank. Please keep it out of ADR and avoid supporting France against ROM or TRI this turn. I will keep my units clear of English centers; can your northern forces pressure Germany instead?

We are both spending forces on WAR and RUM while France contests my western flank. Can we agree not to attack or support attacks on WAR or RUM this turn, and direct pressure toward France? I will not advance into any other German center.

The fighting over TRI and the Italian front is costing both of us. Keep A TYR and A TUS from attacking or supporting attacks on TRI or ROM this turn, and I will keep my units out of French centers. Can we pause this front?

Austria is now at 12 and six centers from a solo. Which Austrian centers will you attack this Spring, and can you keep pressure on TRI or VEN? I will keep F ION positioned against Austria and avoid French centers this turn; please tell me your exact plan.

Austria is at 12 and close to a solo. Are you continuing pressure on WAR and RUM this Spring? Please keep A BER/SIL and A SEV focused on denying Austrian gains; I’ll keep my fleets clear of German centers.

Austria is at 12 and remains the immediate solo threat. Can A VEN attack TRI this Spring, and are you coordinating support with France? My F ION is positioned to pressure Austria from the south; tell me what Austrian center you can contest.

Austria is at 12, so we must keep denying it centers. Please order A VEN–TRI; I’ll support from A TYR. I can’t promise success, but this is our clearest immediate chance to dislodge Austria from TRI. What are you planning for VEN?

Austria is up to 12. Please renew pressure on its eastern centers—can A SEV attack RUM, and can your northern armies contest WAR or another Austrian center? I’ll keep pressing from the south and keep my units out of German centers. Let me know your exact orders.

Austria is at 12 and remains the immediate solo threat. What are your plans for F ION and the northern fleets? If you can put pressure on an Austrian center or otherwise deny Austria a gain, please do; I’ll continue contesting it from the south.

Your 12 centers put you six from victory, so I will keep opposing further expansion. A WAR still occupies a German center. Will you withdraw it, and can we agree not to attack each other’s remaining centers while we contain the solo threat?

Austria is at 12 and remains six centers from victory. I’m renewing pressure from the east; can you use F BAL or another unit to contest Austrian gains or otherwise constrain Austria this turn? I’ll keep my units clear of English centers.

Austria is at 12, six from victory. Please keep pressure on Austrian centers from TYR/TUS and tell me your targets. I’ll press east from SEV and BER/MUN; I’ll keep my units clear of German centers and would welcome coordination against Austria.

Austria is now at 12, so we must deny it further centers. I have only A VEN against Austrian A APU and F TRI. Will you support A VEN holding from TYR, or support VEN–TRI if I attack? Please keep your other units clear of VEN.

Austria has 12 centers and is six from winning. Please continue pressure on RUM and WAR this Spring, and tell me your intended orders. I have only A VEN available to contest Austria in the south; any pressure you can sustain is vital.
You are at 12 and six centers from a solo win. I will contest your expansion. What are your intentions toward VEN and TRI this Spring? If you leave VEN alone, I will avoid attacking TRI this turn.

I will leave A VEN alone this Spring, and F TRI will hold rather than attack it. Please keep A VEN out of TRI and avoid supporting France against my western centers. I cannot promise to leave VEN alone indefinitely, but there is no need to open another front this turn.

I will not withdraw A WAR while you continue contesting it, but I will not advance into another German center this Spring. I cannot promise not to contest WAR, which is already occupied by Austria. Please keep A SIL/A BER from attacking it and direct A SEV away from RUM; we can avoid widening the conflict.

I will not keep F ION out of ADR; it will move there to constrain your southern flank and support a future attack on TRI. My northern fleets will protect English centers, not assist your expansion. Keep your units clear of English centers as you have promised.

F BAL cannot reach an Austrian center this Spring. I’ll move F ION–ADR to constrain Austria’s southern flank; my northern fleets must cover English interests. Please continue A SIL/BER pressure on WAR and A SEV against RUM, and tell me your exact orders.

F ION will move to ADR to constrain Austria and position against TRI; I’ll keep clear of French centers. My northern fleets must protect English interests, so I can’t directly contest an Austrian center this Spring. Which Austrian centers are you and Italy attacking, and with what supports?

I’ll support Italy’s A VEN–TRI from A TYR. I can also pressure Austria from the west: A TUS–APU and F NAP–ION are available. Please keep F ION focused on denying Austria room to expand, and use your northern fleets to contest any Austrian gains you can.

No. You remain at 12 centers and six from victory, so I won’t pause the front while you retain that threat. I intend to support Italy’s A VEN–TRI from A TYR and continue pressuring your southern position. Keep your units out of French centers.

Please order A VEN–TRI; I confirm support from A TYR. I’ll keep A TUS clear of VEN and TRI, and can use it to pressure APU. This is our best immediate chance to dislodge Austria’s F TRI and deny it the center.

I’ll support Italy’s A VEN–TRI from A TYR and use A TUS to pressure APU. Please renew pressure on Austria from the east—especially A SEV–RUM and attacks toward WAR—so it cannot shift forces south or gain another center. I’ll keep my units clear of German centers.

I’m continuing pressure: A BER–WAR and A SEV–RUM. I can’t spare another unit to attack or support an Austrian center this turn. F BAL could not directly reach one, but your pressure elsewhere may still constrain Austria; please keep your fleets clear of German centers.

I can’t agree to leave WAR and RUM unchallenged while you hold 12 centers and are six from victory. I intend A BER–WAR and A SEV–RUM. I’m not targeting any other Austrian or German centers this turn, but I won’t promise to stop opposing your expansion.

I intend A BER–WAR and A SEV–RUM this Spring. Please use A VEN to contest an Austrian position if you can; I have no unit available to support it. Austria’s 12 centers make continued pressure essential.

My exact orders are A BER–WAR and A SEV–RUM. I can’t support either attack from my other units this turn. Please keep pressing Austrian centers from the south, and keep your units out of German centers.

I’ll order A VEN–TRI with France’s promised support from TYR, aiming to dislodge Austria’s F TRI. Please use F ION to pressure the Adriatic if possible; that could complicate Austria’s defense and keep it from simply shifting south. I have no other unit or Austrian center I can contest this turn.

Confirmed: I’ll order A VEN–TRI. Please support from A TYR as proposed, and keep your other units clear of VEN. Austria’s A APU may move into VEN, but dislodging its F TRI is our best immediate chance to deny it a center. If we succeed, let’s coordinate the follow-up before Austria can retake TRI.

notes.note: Spring 1913: attack Austrian TRI as promised with France's TYR support; France says it will keep VEN clear. Austria says TRI holds and VEN left alone, but is immediate solo threat at 12. Germany presses WAR/RUM; England pressures south.

Italy/France/England threaten TRI: TYR supports VEN–TRI, ION moves ADR. Cover TRI with SER support, preserving fleet TRI. Germany attacks WAR and RUM; holds there are unsupported, so prioritize centers? Hold BUD/BUL. Avoid needless moves into occupied centers; VIE probes TYR. Germany may take WAR/RUM.

Keep F ION pressuring Austria via ADR; France/Italy claim to attack TRI and APU. Germany says it will pressure WAR/RUM but remains unreliable. Advance against French/central positions while securing HOL; avoid Austrian centers directly.

Support Italy’s VEN–TRI with TYR. TUS attacks ROM, supported by NAP, to dislodge Austria and threaten its center; GOL to TYS for future options, MAR to BUR. Germany promised eastern pressure; England says ION–ADR.
Contain Austria: BER–SIL supported by MUN, SEV contests RUM. KIE presses English HOL; PAR probes GAS, NOR to FIN. Austria refused withdrawal from WAR; England and France urged eastern pressure.

messages.body: This Fall, can we stop spending units against each other? I propose A WAR hold and A SEV avoid RUM; I will not advance into another German center. France is taking ROM and England holds BEL, so let’s contain their gains rather than weaken both our fronts.

F ADR is now adjacent to TRI, and your support could decide whether France and Italy take it. Please keep F ADR from supporting an attack on TRI this Fall. I will keep Austrian units clear of English centers; can we avoid opening another front while France takes ROM?

France’s A ROM threatens my center, while F ADR and French forces threaten TRI. Please keep A VEN out of TRI this Fall and do not support France there. I will leave VEN alone this turn; let’s avoid helping France gain from our fighting.

Please hold A ROM in ROM this Fall so Austria loses the center, and keep pressure on Austria wherever possible. I intend to keep F BEL there to take BEL; avoid ordering against it. Can your other units help deny Austria a gain?

Austria remains six centers from a solo. Please continue the attack on WAR with A BER supporting A SIL–WAR, and pressure RUM with A SEV–RUM. I’ll keep my fleets clear of German centers; please keep them clear of English centers.

Please coordinate with France to contest F TRI: will A VEN–TRI again have support from A TYR? Austria remains the leading solo threat, so denying it a center matters more than preserving a position you cannot hold.

F BEL is occupying BEL, which becomes yours if it remains there, while my A ROM can return ROM to France. Please move F BEL out this Fall and avoid supporting any attack on ROM; I’ll keep my forces clear of English centers. What are your orders?

My A ROM will hold ROM this Fall, restoring it to France. I will continue contesting your expansion; please tell me whether you intend to attack ROM or move against other French centers. I’m coordinating pressure with Germany and Italy.

Austria remains six centers from victory. Please keep pressing its centers this Fall, especially WAR or RUM, and avoid any move that helps Austria expand. I’ll hold ROM and continue contesting Austria from the south. What are your orders?

You still occupy German WAR, and at 12 centers you remain the immediate solo threat. I will keep contesting your expansion. Will you withdraw from WAR and agree not to attack any other German center this turn?

Austria remains six centers from victory. Please use your forces to keep pressure on Austria where possible, and keep them clear of German centers. I’ll continue contesting WAR and RUM; what are your Fall intentions?

Please keep pressing Austria and avoid German centers. ROM is now Austrian-owned, so your A ROM can take it this Fall; can you also tell me whether you’ll keep A BUR and A TYR focused on Austria? I’ll continue contesting WAR and RUM.

Austria is at 12 and may take ROM from your A ROM this Fall. Please keep A ROM in ROM and support A VEN holding from A TYR; I will hold VEN. Losing VEN or handing ROM to Austria brings it closer to 18.

Austria is at 12 and A APU threatens my A VEN. Can F ADR support A VEN holding this Fall? Please also keep pressure on Austria wherever you can; losing VEN and possibly ROM would bring Austria closer to its solo.
Austria is at 12 and can reach 18 quickly if it takes more centers. Please continue pressure on WAR and RUM this Fall. My A VEN is threatened by A APU; I will try to hold it.

I intend to contest your A ROM, which occupies an Austrian center, but I am not planning to move against other French centers this turn. I will keep my forces out of French territory otherwise. Your continued coordination against TRI leaves little basis for a broader stand-down.

I will not withdraw A WAR while you continue contesting it, and I will not attack another German center this turn. I cannot promise not to defend WAR if attacked. Please keep A BER and A SIL from supporting an attack there, and direct A SEV away from RUM.

I’m keeping F BEL in BEL to take the center. F ADR will support A VEN holding against Austria’s A APU–VEN. Please keep A ROM in ROM so Austria does not regain it, and consider A TYR–APU supported by F TYS to pressure Austria’s southern flank.

I’ll keep F BEL to take BEL and use F ADR to support A VEN holding against Austria’s attack. Please continue A BER supporting A SIL–WAR and A SEV–RUM; those attacks are vital to denying Austria another gain.

I’m keeping F BEL in BEL and will support A VEN holding from F ADR, so I won’t help France take ROM but will not leave Italy exposed to your attack. My fleets will stay clear of Austrian centers. Please continue keeping your units clear of English centers.
Yes. F ADR will support A VEN holding this Fall against A APU–VEN. Coordinate with France to pressure APU or TRI if possible; preserving VEN and denying Austria another center is essential.

I’ll hold A ROM in ROM so France regains the center, and A TYR will support Italy’s A VEN holding. I’ll keep A BUR focused east rather than attack your F BEL this turn. I can’t promise to leave BEL uncontested indefinitely; please keep F BEL from supporting Austria.

I’ll keep A BUR focused east and out of German centers this turn; A ROM will hold ROM to return it to France, while A TYR supports Italy’s A VEN holding. I can’t directly reach WAR or RUM from my current positions, but I support your pressure there.

I’ll order A TYR to support A VEN holding this Fall, and I’ll keep my other units clear of VEN and TRI. A ROM will hold ROM so France regains it. Please hold VEN; Austria’s A APU is the immediate threat.
I’ll continue opposing Austria’s expansion: A SIL–WAR supported by A MUN, and A SEV–RUM. Please use A BUR and A TYR to contest Austrian centers, and keep your units out of German centers.

I’ll continue A SIL–WAR supported by A MUN and A SEV–RUM to contain Austria. Please keep your fleets clear of German centers and use any available pressure against Austria; let me know your Fall intentions.

I will continue contesting WAR and RUM: A SIL–WAR supported by A MUN, and A SEV–RUM. Your occupation of WAR remains a conflict, and with 12 centers you are still the solo threat. I will not promise to leave your expansion unchallenged.
I’ll continue pressure on WAR and RUM: A SIL–WAR supported by A MUN, and A SEV–RUM. Please keep A VEN contesting Austria if possible; the effort to deny it further centers is essential.

France’s A TYR can support A VEN–TRI, but I cannot rely on that alone. F ADR could support A VEN–TRI as well, giving us a strong chance to dislodge F TRI and deny Austria the center. Can you do that? Austria’s A APU also threatens VEN, so please don’t support me holding there if you support the attack.

I’ll keep A VEN out of TRI and won’t support France there. I intend to hold VEN; your A APU could threaten it, so please keep it clear. France’s A ROM is already a danger to your center, and I can’t help you against it.

notes.note: Hold VEN against Austria's APU; England promised ADR support to hold, and France promised TYR support to hold. Germany says it will press WAR/RUM. Deny Austria further centers.

Keep BEL to capture it. Support VEN hold against APU as promised, denying Austria a gain. Advance fleets east/south for future pressure; occupy HOL with HEL. France says ROM holds; Germany claims continued WAR/RUM pressure.

Take open DEN with KIE; advance elsewhere toward future centers. Keep contesting Austria at WAR and RUM, though RUM is likely defended. Austria remains the immediate solo threat; England and France asked for pressure and promised to avoid German centers.

Contest French A ROM with APU; cover RUM with BLA and BUL, WAR with GAL, TRI with SER. Germany openly attacks WAR/RUM; England backs Italy at VEN, Italy promised not to enter TRI, France remains hostile. Try to recover lost centers and stop Austrian losses.

Keep ROM to regain the center; TYS supports its hold against Austria. TYR supports Italy's VEN hold as promised. NAP advances to ION; BUR shifts to GAS. England plans to keep BEL and take it; I agreed not to contest it this turn.

messages.body: You have A BER, A MUN and A SIL positioned to contest WAR, while A SEV threatens RUM. France is holding ROM and coordinating pressure; can we agree this Spring to leave WAR and RUM unchallenged and turn our forces against France instead? I will not advance into another German center.

Your A ROM occupies an Austrian center, and I intend to contest it. I will not move into other French centers this Spring. Will you keep A TYR from supporting an attack on TRI and avoid widening the front, so we can limit this to ROM?

Your F ADR can support pressure on TRI, while Austria is already tied down against France and Germany. Please keep F ADR from supporting any attack on TRI this Spring and stay clear of Austrian centers. Are your northern fleets moving against Germany or France?

Let’s make a serious attempt to dislodge Austria’s F TRI this Spring. I can order F ADR to support A VEN–TRI; please order the attack and coordinate A TYR’s support with France. This means I cannot also support A VEN holding against A APU–VEN.

Can A TYR support Italy’s A VEN–TRI this Spring? I’m prepared to support the attack from F ADR, giving us a strong chance to dislodge Austria’s F TRI. Please confirm your exact orders and avoid interfering with the attack.

Austria remains the leading solo threat. Please confirm whether you’ll again attack WAR and RUM this Spring, and specify your moves and supports. I’m coordinating a supported attack on TRI from the south; keep pressure on Austria and avoid English centers.

Austria remains the immediate solo threat. What are you ordering A VEN to do? I can keep A ROM in place and use A TYR to pressure an Austrian center, but need to know whether you plan to attack TRI or hold VEN.

Austria still has 11 centers, so please continue contesting it from the east. Are you ordering A BER toward WAR and A SEV toward RUM again? I’ll keep my forces focused on the Austrian front and out of German centers.

Austria remains the leading solo threat. Can F ADR support an attack on TRI or otherwise pressure Austria this turn? Please tell me your plan for F ADR; I’m coordinating pressure from the west and south.

You still hold WAR, a German center, and are only seven centers from a solo. I will keep opposing your expansion. Will you withdraw A WAR and agree not to attack German centers this turn? I will not promise to leave WAR or RUM uncontested.

Austria is at 11 and still the immediate solo threat. Please use F ADR to pressure an Austrian position and keep your fleets clear of German centers. I intend to keep contesting WAR and RUM; what are your exact orders this turn?

Austria remains seven centers from a solo. Please use A TYR or your southern fleets to contest Austrian centers, and keep your units clear of German centers. I intend to keep pressure on WAR and RUM; what are your exact targets this turn?
Austria remains the immediate solo threat. Please confirm F ADR will support A VEN holding against A APU–VEN again this Spring. I’ll hold VEN; can you also keep pressure on Austria elsewhere?
Please support A VEN holding from A TYR against the likely A APU–VEN, and keep your other units clear of VEN. I’ll hold VEN. Austria’s 11 centers make denying it this center essential.

Please continue pressure on Austrian centers this Spring, especially RUM and WAR, and tell me your intended orders. I’ll hold A VEN against A APU; coordinated pressure is needed to stop Austria reaching 18.

I’ll move A WAR to GAL this Spring and will not attack another German center. In return, please keep A SEV from attacking RUM and direct A BER/A MUN against France rather than Austrian units. We can end the WAR dispute and avoid further losses on both fronts.

My F ADR will support A VEN–TRI, coordinating with Italy and France to contest F TRI. My northern fleets will protect English interests and will not move against your northern centers this turn. I cannot promise to stay clear of every Austrian position while your expansion remains the central threat.

I will order F ADR to support A VEN–TRI, as agreed. I cannot also support A VEN holding against A APU–VEN, so your A VEN may be exposed; please coordinate A TYR’s support with France to maximize the chance of dislodging F TRI.

I’m using F ADR to support A VEN–TRI against Austria. My northern fleets will protect English interests and stay clear of German centers. Please continue contesting WAR and RUM; confirm your exact moves and supports so we can judge whether Austria is being denied a gain.

F ADR will support Italy’s A VEN–TRI this Spring to contest Austria’s F TRI. Please have A TYR support the attack as discussed, and keep your other forces pressuring Austria. I’ll keep my northern fleets focused on English interests and avoid French centers.

I won’t leave ROM undefended or help you recover it. A ROM will hold with support from F TYS. I also intend to keep A TYR focused on denying you VEN/TRI, not on widening into your other fronts. Your best course is to keep out of French centers.

I’ll support A VEN holding from A TYR against A APU–VEN. If you instead attack TRI, England says F ADR can support you, but my support is needed to protect VEN; please confirm your choice. I’ll keep my other units clear of VEN.

I’ll keep pressure on Austria: A ROM holds with F TYS supporting, A TYR supports A VEN holding, and A BUR will move to BOH. I cannot reach WAR or RUM this turn. Please renew your pressure there and avoid moves that let Austria gain.

I can’t support A VEN–TRI this turn: Italy says it will hold VEN, and A TYR is needed to support that hold against A APU. Please keep F ADR positioned to constrain Austria and avoid French centers. I’ll keep A ROM in place with F TYS supporting its hold.

I won’t agree to leave WAR and RUM unchallenged while you remain seven centers from victory. I intend A SIL–WAR with A MUN supporting, and A SEV–RUM. I am not targeting another Austrian center this Spring, but I will continue to oppose your expansion.
I intend A SIL–WAR with A MUN supporting, and A SEV–RUM this Spring. Please keep A VEN contesting Austria if you can; I understand you plan to hold against A APU.
Confirmed: A SIL–WAR supported by A MUN, and A SEV–RUM. I’ll keep pressing Austria and avoid English centers. Your pressure on TRI from the south could help deny Austria another gain.

Yes: A SIL–WAR with A MUN supporting, and A SEV–RUM. I’ll keep my forces out of German centers. Please continue pressuring Austrian positions from the south and avoid letting Austria gain another center.

Agreed: A VEN–TRI, with your F ADR supporting the attack. I understand this leaves VEN exposed to A APU–VEN; dislodging F TRI is our best chance to check Austria. Please order the support as proposed.

I’m ordering A VEN–TRI. Please support the attack from A TYR, and keep A ROM in place. England will support from F ADR, giving us strength to dislodge F TRI; VEN may be exposed to A APU, but stopping Austria’s expansion is urgent.

notes.note: Hold ROM with TYS support against APU; support Italy’s VEN–TRI attack with TYR as England promised ADR support. ION to ALB, BUR to GAS. Austria remains the immediate solo threat.

Italy now plans to hold VEN, and France says TYR supports it; support VEN hold against APU with ADR. Germany claims continued pressure on WAR/RUM. Advance fleets toward NOR, NAF, and northern seas; avoid German centers for now.
Attack TRI with England's promised ADR support; France instead supports VEN holding, leaving APU–VEN a risk. Germany presses WAR/RUM. Reassess in Fall; deny Austria's solo if possible.

France and England are coordinating against TRI; SER and VIE support its defense. Germany announced SIL-WAR and SEV-RUM; APU retreats toward NAP, WAR probes MOS, GAL advances UKR. BLA/BUD cover RUM. Italy had promised to stay out of TRI; verify.

Continue opposing Austria: SIL-WAR while Austria promised WAR-GAL; SEV-RUM remains pressured. France promised to stay out of German centers; England coordinates against Austria. Probe English SWE, HOL and BRE; reclaim STP with FIN. BOH-TYR supported by MUN.

messages.body: A MOS is poised to transfer MOS to Austria, while your A WAR could attack it. I propose we stop the WAR/MOS contest this Fall: keep A WAR in place and do not attack MOS; I will not advance against another German center. Can you agree?

Your F ADR can attack my F TRI, and your northern units are taking several centers this Fall. Please keep F ADR from moving to or supporting an attack on TRI. I’ll keep Austrian units clear of English centers; can we avoid opening a southern front?

A NAP is set to return NAP to Austria this Fall. Please do not attack or support an attack on it; I will not move into another French center this turn. Can we limit the dispute to restoring NAP and avoid widening the front?

Your units on BRE, HOL, SWE and NOR will take English centers this Fall. Please order them out rather than capture them; Austria is still the solo threat, and I need to preserve my centers. What are your exact orders for these units and WAR?
Austria’s A NAP can make NAP Austrian this Fall. Can A ROM attack NAP, with F TYS supporting, to deny Austria that gain? Please confirm your exact orders; I’ll keep my forces clear of French centers.
What are your exact Fall orders for A MOS, A NAP and A WAR? I’m opposing the leading solo threat and won’t help you gain centers. Please keep Austrian units clear of English centers.
Your A NAP is occupying a French center. I’m ordering A ROM–NAP, supported by F TYS. Please tell me whether you intend to hold NAP or move elsewhere; I will continue contesting your expansion.

Austria remains the immediate solo threat. Please contest A MOS and A WAR this Fall and avoid any move that lets Austria keep or gain centers. I’ll attack NAP from ROM, supported by TYS. What are your exact orders against Austria?

Austria still threatens a solo, and this Fall’s center changes could bring it closer. Please use your fleets to prevent Austrian gains where possible, and tell me whether you can contest any Austrian center. I’m attacking NAP from ROM with TYS support.

This Fall my units in MOS and WAR will reclaim those German centers, and A NAP is in a French center. Please do not try to hold or expand into German centers; what are your plans for your remaining units?
My units in BRE, HOL, and SWE are positioned to reclaim those centers this Fall. Please keep your units clear of German centers, including NOR; can you use your forces to constrain Austria instead?

Austria’s A NAP occupies your center, and Austria remains the leading solo threat. Can you dislodge it or otherwise contest Austria this Fall? I’m reclaiming German centers and will keep my forces out of French centers.
Austria is still the immediate solo threat. Please support A VEN–TRI with F ADR this Fall; I’ll make the attack. Can you also keep your other units from helping Austria gain centers?

Austria’s A NAP threatens your A ROM, while its F TRI remains a key center to contest. I plan A VEN–TRI; can F ADR support from England? Please keep A ROM in place and consider support from F TYS against A NAP–ROM if needed.
Austria is still at 11 and gaining MOS and NAP would bring it closer to 18. Please keep contesting WAR and MOS this Fall, and tell me whether you can prevent Austria taking WAR.

A MOS will hold, A NAP will move to APU, and A WAR is German, not mine to order. I’m not targeting English centers. Your F ADR remains the immediate threat to TRI; keep it from supporting France there.

I will not advance against another German center. A MOS will hold; A NAP is moving to APU rather than contesting another French center. A WAR is yours. I suggest you keep A SEV away from RUM and avoid opening another front.

A NAP will move to APU rather than hold against your supported attack. I will not enter another French center this turn. Please keep A TYR from supporting an attack on TRI; we can contain this dispute without widening it.

I’ll support Italy’s A VEN–TRI with F ADR this Fall, and I will not assist your expansion. Your units taking MOS and NAP would bring you closer to a solo; please keep them from English centers. I still need your exact orders for A MOS, A NAP, and A WAR.
Confirmed: F ADR will support A VEN–TRI this Fall. This is aimed at dislodging Austria’s F TRI and denying Austria a secure position there. Please order the attack as agreed.

I can’t leave English centers undefended while your units are poised to take BRE, HOL, SWE, and NOR. Please order A SWE away from NOR and avoid taking BRE or HOL; I’ll keep F ADR focused on denying Austria a gain. I will not move my fleets into German centers.

F ADR will support Italy’s A VEN–TRI. Your A ROM–NAP with F TYS support is the right move to deny Austria NAP; please proceed, and keep your other units from assisting Austria. I’ll keep my forces clear of French centers.

I will not leave NAP uncontested: A ROM is attacking NAP with support from F TYS. I’m also using F ALB to support Italy’s A VEN–TRI, so your position at TRI is contested as well. Keep your units out of French centers.

Confirmed: A ROM–NAP, supported by F TYS, to deny Austria NAP. I’m also supporting Italy’s A VEN–TRI with F ALB; please have F ADR support the same attack if you can. That gives us the best chance to dislodge Austria’s F TRI.

I can’t support from TYR; my current unit there is gone. I will support A VEN–TRI with F ALB. Please order A VEN–TRI, and ask England to support from F ADR as well. A ROM is attacking NAP with F TYS support.
I’m attacking NAP with A ROM, supported by F TYS, and supporting Italy’s A VEN–TRI with F ALB. Please keep contesting WAR and MOS, and avoid any move that lets Austria retain or gain centers.

I can’t agree to leave MOS uncontested while your unit occupies a German center. A WAR will stay in place and support A SEV–MOS; that also leaves my unit in WAR to reclaim the center. I won’t advance against another Austrian center this turn.

I won’t order A BRE, A HOL, or A SWE out; they will remain to reclaim those German centers. A WAR will stay in place, and I’m contesting Austria’s A MOS. F NOR is yours to keep for now, but please don’t move into any other German center.

I’m contesting both: A WAR will remain in WAR to reclaim it and support A SEV–MOS against Austria’s unit there. I can’t prevent Austria taking MOS if the attack fails, but I’m not leaving either German center uncontested.

My exact orders against Austria are A WAR support A SEV–MOS, with A WAR remaining in place to reclaim WAR. A SEV attacks MOS. My units in BRE, HOL, and SWE stay to reclaim those German centers. I hope your supported attack from ROM dislodges A NAP.

notes.note: F1914: Attack TRI as promised, backed by France ALB and England ADR. France says ROM attacks NAP with TYS support; Germany contests WAR and supports SEV–MOS. Austria’s solo remains the priority.

Attack NAP with ROM supported by TYS as promised; support Italy’s VEN–TRI with ALB. GAS moves to PAR to expand at Germany’s expense; PIE to TUS. Austria said NAP–APU and will stay out of other French centers. England promised ADR support for TRI; Germany promised to contest Austria.

Support Italy's VEN–TRI as promised. Secure NOR by staying; contest German-held HOL and take DEN if possible. Germany refused to vacate BRE/HOL/SWE; it is reclaiming them and says NOR is mine for now. France/Italy coordinate against Austria; Austria says NAP–APU and MOS holds.
Reclaim BRE, HOL, SWE, WAR; SEV attacks Austrian-held MOS with WAR support. Pressure Austria from MUN and support England’s promised ADR–TRI. STP contests NOR; PRU advances to LVN.

Protect TRI against the coordinated ADR/ALB/VEN attack with BUD, SER, and VIE support; support RUM with BLA. Hold MOS for its center and support its defense from UKR. NAP retreats to APU; expect France to take NAP. Germany contests MOS/WAR; England and France are hostile in the south.

messages.body: Your A MAR, A NAP, A PAR, A TUS and F ALB/TYS can keep tying down my south, but that only helps Germany. This Spring, keep F ALB from supporting an attack on TRI and leave my Balkan centers alone; I will not move into another French center this turn. Can we contain the front while I deal with Germany?

I propose we stop trading attacks over WAR and MOS this Spring and turn our forces against France instead. Keep A SEV away from RUM and do not attack MOS; I will not move into another German center this turn. Can A WAR and A LVN pressure France rather than Austria?

F ADR is still positioned to threaten TRI, while your northern fleets are not under immediate pressure from me. Keep F ADR from supporting an attack on TRI this Spring and stay clear of Austrian centers; I will keep my units clear of English centers. Can you agree to contain the southern front?
You remain the leading solo threat. What are your Spring orders for A APU, A MOS, and A SYR? I intend to keep F ADR available to help contest TRI; please keep your units clear of English centers.

Can you coordinate pressure on Austria this Spring? I can support Italy’s A VEN–TRI with F ADR if Italy attacks; please confirm whether A TYR or another unit can support, and keep your units from interfering.

Please confirm your Spring orders for A SWE, A HOL, and A BRE, especially whether A SWE will attack NOR. I need to defend English centers while Austria remains the solo threat; I’ll keep F ADR focused on contesting Austria.

Austria remains the main solo threat. Please hold A VEN this Spring; I can support its hold with F ALB while A NAP attacks APU, supported by F TYS. Are you holding VEN, and can you coordinate with England to keep pressure on Austria?

Austria still has 11 centers. Please keep contesting its eastern centers—especially MOS, WAR, or RUM—and avoid any move that lets it gain. I’ll attack APU from A NAP with F TYS support and help protect Italy’s VEN. What are your exact targets?

Austria remains seven centers from a solo. Can you use your fleets to contest Austrian centers or otherwise constrain its southern position this Spring? I plan A NAP–APU with F TYS support and can support Italy’s VEN hold from F ALB. Please keep clear of French centers.

I will continue defending German centers, including WAR and MOS. What are your orders for A MOS and A WAR this Spring? I will not advance on another Austrian center if you keep clear of German centers and do not expand further.

Austria remains the immediate solo threat. Please use F ADR to support pressure on Austria from VEN/TRI if possible, and keep your fleets out of German centers. What are your exact orders this Spring? I intend to keep German centers defended and contest Austrian expansion.

Can you use A NAP to pressure APU this Spring, and keep your other units focused on Austria rather than German centers? I’ll defend German centers and continue opposing Austrian expansion. Please tell me your exact orders.
Austria’s A APU can take VEN if I attack elsewhere. Please support A VEN holding from F ADR this Spring; I’ll hold VEN. What are you doing to contain Austria elsewhere?
Austria’s A APU threatens VEN. Please support A VEN holding from F ALB this Spring; I’ll hold. Keep pressure on Austria’s centers if you can, and let me know your plan.
What are your intentions for A APU this Spring? I will hold VEN and won’t attack TRI this turn, but I need to know whether you intend to attack my only center.

I intend to keep APU clear of VEN this Spring and leave your unit undisturbed. Please continue holding VEN and keep A VEN out of TRI; I need to avoid opening another front while Germany and France contest my positions.

A APU will remain focused on the southern front, A MOS will hold, and A SYR will stay clear of English centers. I’m not targeting your centers. Please keep F ADR from supporting an attack on TRI; that is the key to containing this front.

A MOS will hold, and I will not move into another German center this Spring. A WAR is yours to order. I ask that you keep A SEV away from RUM and avoid attacking MOS; let’s stop trading attacks and direct pressure toward France.

I’ll support A VEN holding from F ADR this Spring. With A NAP–APU and F ALB supporting your hold, we can make A APU’s attack fail and deny Austria VEN. Please hold VEN as proposed; I’ll keep pressing to contain Austria.

I’ll support Italy’s A VEN holding from F ADR, helping stop Austria’s A APU. Your A NAP–APU with F TYS support and F ALB supporting VEN gives us a coordinated defense. I’ll keep F ADR focused on denying Austria a gain.

I can’t agree to stand aside while you remain at 11 centers and keep threatening the solo. F ADR will support Italy’s A VEN holding this Spring. Keep your units clear of English centers as you’ve said; I’m not opening a northern front against you this turn.

F ADR will support A VEN holding against Austria’s A APU, coordinated with France and Italy. I’ll keep my fleets clear of German centers. Please continue contesting Austria’s positions, especially MOS and RUM, and avoid moves against English centers.

Please hold A VEN. I’ll support its hold with F ALB and order A NAP–APU, supported by F TYS, to pressure Austria’s army. I can’t promise that will stop A APU–VEN if it moves, so coordinate with England if possible.

Italy says A VEN will hold, so there is no VEN–TRI attack to support this Spring. I’ll support VEN’s hold with F ALB and order A NAP–APU, supported by F TYS. Please use F ADR to pressure Austria if you can, and keep clear of French centers.

I won’t agree to a stand-down while you remain the leading solo threat. I’m ordering A NAP–APU, supported by F TYS, and F ALB will support A VEN holding; I’m not supporting an attack on TRI. Keep your units out of French centers.

I’ll order A NAP–APU, supported by F TYS, and F ALB will support A VEN holding. My remaining units are focused on France’s southern defense rather than German centers. Please continue contesting Austrian centers, especially MOS, WAR, or RUM.

I will not order A SWE–NOR this Spring, and A BRE and A HOL will stay out of English centers. I’ll keep them defending German positions while I contest Austria in the east. Please keep F ADR focused on Austrian pressure as you proposed.

I intend A SEV–MOS, with A WAR supporting, to contest Austria’s hold there. I’ll keep A BOH and the western units out of French centers. Your attack on APU should help deny Austria a gain; please keep pressing it.

I can’t agree to leave MOS unchallenged while you occupy it and remain the leading solo threat. I intend to contest it from SEV with support from WAR. I will not advance into another Austrian center this Spring; please keep clear of German centers.

I’ll hold A VEN. Please support the hold from F ALB as proposed, and proceed with A NAP–APU supported by F TYS; that pressures Austria whether A APU stays or attacks VEN. I’ll also contact England about F ADR support, but don’t rely on it unless confirmed.

notes.note: Spring 1915: Hold VEN. England promised ADR support; France promised ALB support; France attacks APU with NAP supported by TYS. Austria says APU will stay clear of VEN. Continue denying Austria's solo threat.

Contain French A NAP–APU with APU–NAP; reinforce key centers and regain control of Greece. Germany contests MOS; protect it. England supports VEN, and France supports Italy holding; TRI moves to challenge English ADR.

Support Italy's VEN hold as promised, coordinating against APU with France. France plans NAP–APU; Germany says it will contest Austria and avoid English centers. Attack KIE with HEL supported by DEN; advance northern and western fleets.

Press Austria: NAP attacks APU; ALB and TUS support Italy's VEN hold as promised. TYS to ION, MAR to PIE, PAR to PIC. England promised VEN support and pressure on Austria; Germany says it will contest eastern centers. Austria asked for restraint; refused.

Austria remains the leading threat. France and England promised pressure on Austrian APU/TRI; I promised France SEV–MOS supported by WAR, but WAR can instead move only or hold—orders list offers no support for SEV–MOS from WAR? Keep eastern pressure by SEV–RUM; protect German units and avoid English centers.

messages.body: England’s F KIE is occupying your center, and its fleets are spread across the north. I propose we stop attacking each other this turn and focus on England: keep your units out of Austrian centers, and I’ll avoid advancing into German centers. Can you agree?

With F KIE occupying a German center, you and Germany may come to blows. I’m not targeting English centers this turn; please keep F ADR from supporting attacks on TRI and stay out of Austrian centers. What are your plans for F ADR and F KIE?

Germany’s A SEV and A WAR threaten my eastern position, while you and I have been trading pressure in the south. Please keep F ALB and A NAP out of Austrian centers this turn; I’ll avoid entering French centers. Can we contain the southern front while Germany is distracted by England?

F KIE can secure KIE for me this Fall. Please keep A RUH and your other units from attacking it; I’ll keep my fleets out of your other centers. Can you also confirm whether you’ll continue pressuring Austria rather than English centers?

Austria is still at 11 and remains the solo threat. What are your Fall plans against Austrian centers? I can support Italy’s A VEN–TRI from F ADR if Italy attacks; please coordinate your southern units to make that pressure count.
Can you order A VEN–TRI this Fall? I can support the attack from F ADR, giving us a chance to dislodge Austria’s F TRI. Please tell me your plan, especially whether VEN needs defense against A APU.

Austria remains the solo threat, but KIE is set to pass to England if its fleet stays there. What are your Fall orders against Austria, and can we coordinate pressure on APU or another Austrian center? I’ll keep my units clear of German centers this turn.

F KIE will make KIE English if it remains there. Please tell me your Fall plans, especially whether you intend to keep F KIE there or move it. I want to avoid a clash with you while keeping pressure on Austria; please keep your units out of French centers.

Please hold VEN this Fall if possible; Austria’s A APU remains the immediate threat. I’ll keep pressing from the south, including against APU, and can move A PIE toward TYR to help contest Austria next turn. What are your plans for VEN?
F KIE is sitting in a German center, so I intend A RUH–KIE with A BRE supporting. Please move F KIE out rather than contesting it. Can you use F ADR to pressure Austria again this turn?

You remain the leading solo threat. I intend to contest your eastern positions again and reclaim German centers. What are your orders for A MOS and A RUM? Please avoid further moves into German centers.

Austria remains the immediate solo threat. Please continue pressure on APU and keep your units clear of German centers. I intend to contest Austria from the east and reclaim KIE; what are your exact targets this Fall?
Austria’s A APU still threatens my only center. Will F ADR support A VEN holding again this Fall? Please keep F ADR out of any move that would leave VEN exposed; denying Austria VEN is essential.
Can F ALB support A VEN holding again this Fall, while A NAP attacks APU with F ION supporting? Austria’s A APU is the immediate threat to my only center, and coordinated pressure could contain it.

What are your intentions for A APU this Fall? I’m trying to coordinate a defense of VEN with England and France. Please leave VEN alone; attacking it risks opening another front while you’re already the leading power.

A APU will stay clear of VEN this Fall; I have no intention of opening another front there. Please keep A VEN out of TRI and do not coordinate an attack on my centers with France or England. I need to concentrate on the German and English threats.

A MOS and A RUM will hold their positions; I will not advance into another German center this Fall. Please keep A SEV away from RUM and avoid attacking MOS. England’s F KIE threatens your center, so let’s both focus on stopping English gains rather than weakening each other.

F ADR will support A VEN holding this Fall; A APU remains an immediate threat, and I won't leave VEN exposed for a TRI attack. Please hold VEN. I’ll also try to keep Austria from gaining ground elsewhere.
I’m keeping F KIE in KIE and will support its hold with F DEN against A RUH–KIE. F ADR will support A VEN holding against Austria’s A APU, rather than attack TRI. Please do not attack KIE.

F ADR will support A VEN holding against A APU; I will not use it to attack TRI this turn. F KIE will hold against Germany’s announced A RUH–KIE, with F DEN supporting. I’ll keep my other fleets clear of Austrian centers.

I intend to keep F KIE in place and support its hold with F DEN against Germany’s A RUH–KIE. F ADR will support A VEN holding against A APU rather than leave VEN exposed for a TRI attack. I’ll keep my units out of French centers.
Yes: F ALB will support A VEN holding, and A NAP will attack APU with F ION supporting. Please hold VEN; this gives us the best chance to contain A APU and protect your center.

My targets are A NAP–APU, with F ION supporting, and F ALB supporting A VEN holding. I’ll keep my other units out of German centers. Please continue contesting Austria’s eastern centers, especially MOS, WAR, or RUM.

I won’t agree to leave A NAP or F ALB out of the southern contest while you remain the leading solo threat. I’m pressing APU and helping Italy defend VEN. I’ll continue keeping my units out of other French centers; please keep yours out as well.

A NAP will attack APU with F ION supporting, and F ALB will support Italy’s A VEN holding. Italy plans to hold VEN, so there is no confirmed VEN–TRI attack for F ADR to support. Please keep F KIE in place to secure KIE for England.

I can’t agree to leave German centers exposed while F KIE occupies KIE and your forces still hold MOS. I’ll contest KIE and keep pressing your eastern positions. If you move A MOS or A RUM away from German centers, tell me; I will not promise to abandon the defense of my centers.

I cannot leave F KIE in a German supply center. A RUH will attack KIE with A BRE supporting; please move the fleet out. I will continue contesting Austria in the east, but I won’t sacrifice KIE while Austria still holds MOS and remains the leading solo threat.

I’ll contest KIE with A RUH supported by A BRE, and continue pressure on Austria from the east. France’s pressure on APU could help deny Austria another gain; please keep your units clear of German centers. I can’t promise to leave KIE to England while its fleet occupies a German center.

I’ll hold A VEN this Fall rather than leave it open to A APU. Please support A VEN holding from F ADR as you did before; France is pressing APU, and denying Austria VEN is essential. Keep F ADR out of any move that would leave VEN unsupported.

I plan to hold A VEN against Austria’s A APU. Please have F ALB support A VEN holding, and proceed with your pressure on APU. Let me know if you can confirm the support; I cannot risk leaving VEN open to Austria.

notes.note: Fall 1915: Hold VEN as promised; England and France both promised support for the hold. Austria says APU stays clear, but protect Italy’s only center and keep denying Austria growth.

Support Italy's VEN hold as promised; retain KIE against Germany's announced attack, with DEN support. Germany broke its request/pledge by attacking KIE. Advance BAR to NOR, NWG to CLY; probe SPA and reposition ENG to MAO.

Press for open centers: RUH-BEL, BRE-GAS, STP-NOR with SWE support. Austria holds MOS/RUM and remains the solo threat; keep eastern units away from Austrian centers this turn while maneuvering toward future gains.

NAP attacks APU with ION support; TUS supports Italy's VEN hold as promised. PIC takes undefended BEL for French growth; PIE pressures TYR. ALB has no useful support option. England says KIE stays English; Germany contests it. Austria remains solo threat.

Claim vacant ROM with APU and BUL with GRE. Fortify RUM against Germany; support MOS and TRI against likely attacks. England holds KIE and has pledged ADR will not attack TRI; France remains hostile in the south. Germany continues contesting eastern positions.

messages.body: I’m keeping A APU clear of VEN this turn. Please keep A VEN out of TRI and avoid supporting attacks on my centers; can you confirm your plans for VEN?

England’s F KIE and northern fleets threaten your position. I propose we both focus on England this turn: keep A SEV away from RUM and out of Austrian centers, and I’ll avoid advancing into German centers. Can you agree?
F ADR remains the immediate threat to TRI. Please keep it from attacking or supporting an attack there this turn, and keep your other fleets out of Austrian centers. What are your plans for F ADR?

Austria is at 12 and six centers from a solo. What are your Spring orders for A APU, A TYR, F ION and A PIC? Please coordinate pressure on Austrian centers; I can use F ADR to support VEN or contest the southern position.

Austria is at 12 and remains the immediate solo threat. Which Austrian positions will you contest this Spring with A ARM, A GAL, A WAR and A PRU? I’m considering F ADR support for VEN; please avoid further attacks on F KIE while we coordinate.

Austria is at 12, but A APU is now French and still A ROM/A SER can threaten VEN. Will A VEN hold this Spring? I can support its hold with F ADR, or coordinate a VEN–TRI attack if you prefer to risk it.
Austria is up to 12, so we need to take a center from it this turn. Please order A VEN–TRI; I can support from A TYR, and England’s F ADR can support as well. Can you confirm the attack?

Can F ADR support Italy’s A VEN–TRI this turn? I’ve asked Italy to attack and can support from A TYR; together we may dislodge Austria’s F TRI and deny its expansion. Please confirm your plan for F ADR.

Austria is at 12 and close to a solo. What are your exact Spring targets against it? I’m coordinating A VEN–TRI with Italy and can support from A TYR; please contest Austrian centers in the east rather than let it gain.

Your 12 centers still make you the immediate solo threat. What are A ARM, A GAL, and your southern units doing this Spring? I have no unit positioned to contest MOS or RUM now; please keep your forces out of German centers while I secure my borders.

F KIE remains in a German center, and F DEN can support it. Will you move F KIE out this Spring? I’m willing to discuss a mutual arrangement that keeps your fleets clear of German centers, but I can’t leave KIE uncontested.

Austria remains six centers from a solo win. Can you use A APU or F ION to pressure Austrian positions this Spring? My eastern units are not currently placed to attack MOS or RUM, but I’m willing to coordinate pressure where our forces can reach.
Your 12 centers leave no room for complacency. I will hold A VEN and will not attack TRI this turn. Please keep F TRI, A ROM and A SER from attacking VEN; confirm your intentions.

Please order F ADR to support A VEN holding this Spring. Austria remains at 12 and can reach 18; can you also contest its expansion elsewhere? France’s A APU is now in position to affect VEN, so coordination matters.
Please keep A APU from attacking VEN and consider supporting A VEN holding from A TYR. Austria is still at 12 and the main solo threat; what pressure can you put on its centers this turn?
Confirmed: F TRI, A ROM, and A SER will not attack or support an attack on VEN this Spring. Please keep A VEN out of TRI and avoid supporting attacks on my centers.

A ARM and A GAL are focused on securing my eastern positions; my southern units will not attack German centers this Spring. I ask that you likewise keep your forces out of Austrian centers and avoid contesting MOS or RUM. I can’t promise to leave German centers unchallenged indefinitely.

F ADR will support A VEN holding this Spring, as requested. Please hold A VEN; with A APU and A ROM nearby, a TRI attack would leave your sole center vulnerable. I’ll use my other fleets to contain Austria where possible.

F ADR will support A VEN holding this Spring, not attack TRI. My northern fleets will stay clear of Austrian centers. You remain six centers from a solo, so I cannot promise to stand aside from efforts to contain your expansion.

Yes: F ADR will support A VEN–TRI this Spring if Italy orders the attack. Please coordinate A TYR’s support as proposed. I’ve told Italy that support is available; I can’t also support VEN’s hold, so make sure the attack has enough strength and account for A APU.

I will keep F KIE in KIE this Spring, supported by F DEN. I won’t move it out while your units threaten it. I’m not seeking other German centers this turn; please don’t attack KIE, and continue contesting Austria in the east.

I’ll order A TYR to support Italy’s A VEN–TRI, and A APU to support A VEN holding. Please confirm F ADR will support A VEN–TRI as proposed. F ION will move to GRE to pressure Austria’s center; A PIC and A TYR will stay clear of English centers.
I’ll support A VEN–TRI from A TYR and support A VEN holding from A APU. Please order A VEN–TRI; England has offered F ADR support. I’ll also send F ION to GRE to pressure Austria directly.

I’ll order F ION–GRE to pressure Austria’s center; A APU supports A VEN holding, and A TYR supports Italy’s A VEN–TRI. F ION can’t support an attack on APU or reach Austria’s eastern centers, so please use your eastern units to contest them where possible.

I cannot agree to leave F KIE unchallenged in a German supply center. A RUH will attack KIE this Spring; please move F KIE out. I’ll continue contesting Austria as well, but won’t promise to stop defending German centers.

I can’t agree to keep A SEV away from RUM while you remain at 12 centers. This Spring I’ll pressure your positions from GAL and WAR; please keep your forces out of German centers. I’ll also continue trying to recover KIE from England.

This Spring I intend A GAL–BUD, supported by A WAR, and A BOH–VIE to pressure Austria. Please follow through on your coordinated A VEN–TRI attempt with A TYR support; I’ll keep my other units out of French centers.

I’ll order A VEN–TRI. Please support the attack with F ADR as proposed; France will support from A TYR. France is keeping A APU clear of VEN, and I’ve asked it to cover VEN against A ROM if possible. Please keep F ADR out of any move that leaves the attack unsupported.

I intend to order A VEN–TRI this Spring, supported by France and England, to contest F TRI. I will not attack any other Austrian center. Please keep A ROM clear of VEN and do not attack my unit there; I will not move A VEN against your other centers this turn.

I’ll order A VEN–TRI; please support it with A TYR as you proposed. Since A ROM can threaten VEN, please also order A APU to support A VEN holding in VEN if that is legal from APU. Let’s coordinate with England’s F ADR support and keep the pressure on Austria.

notes.note: Attack TRI with France's TYR and England's ADR support as promised; Austria says ROM, SER, TRI won't attack/support against VEN this Spring. Reassess Fall; protect sole center and continue denying Austria's solo.

Support Italy's VEN–TRI with ADR as agreed; France promised TYR support. Italy's attack and France's coordination are confirmed. Austria remains the solo threat. Germany continues threatening KIE despite requests; move KIE toward HOL and probe German centers.
Pressure Austria while taking openings: BOH attacks VIE with GAL support; ARM to SEV, PRU to LVN supported by WAR. RUH to BEL; advance GAS toward MAR and push SWE at DEN. Austria remains 6 from solo.

Keep pressure on Austria: ION to GRE and TYR supports Italy’s VEN–TRI as promised; Italy and England committed to the attack. APU holds because Italy is moving from VEN, so a support to VEN holding would be invalid. PIC to BUR.

Italy and England threaten TRI via VEN; defend TRI with BUD, SER, VIE. Germany threatens eastern centers; support RUM and probe SEV from UKR with MOS support. ROM attacks French NAP; SYR pressures ARM. No agreement to leave German centers unchallenged.

messages.body: Austria is still at 12, but Germany’s A VIE is sitting on your center and the northern fleets are contesting your gains. I propose we avoid fighting each other this Fall: keep your units out of Austrian centers and I’ll avoid English centers. What are your plans for F ADR and F STP/NORTH?

A VIE is currently on your center, while A SEV is on mine and A ARM threatens my southern flank. Let’s stop trading centers this Fall: I’ll avoid advancing into German territory if you keep A SEV out of Austrian centers and do not attack RUM. What are your plans for VIE and SEV?

Your APU is near NAP and my A NAP is on it; I don’t want to widen our southern fight while Germany and England contest the north. I propose you leave NAP and my Balkan centers alone this Fall, and I’ll keep out of your remaining centers. What are your plans for APU and F GRE?

This Fall I’m securing English centers, not contesting your other holdings. Please order A BEL–HOL and A DEN–KIE away from English-held centers; I’ll avoid your remaining centers. What are your exact orders for BEL, DEN, and VIE?
Austria is still the solo threat at 12. What are your Fall orders for A APU, A BUR, F GRE, and A TYR? Please coordinate pressure on Austrian centers and avoid English-held BRE and HOL.
You remain six centers from a solo. What are your Fall orders for A NAP, A SEV, A MOS, and A SYR? I’ll oppose any gains that bring you closer to 18; keep your units clear of English centers.

Your A NAP is poised to take a French center, while you are already six centers from a solo. I will contest it. Can you move A NAP elsewhere and keep A BUL out of GRE this Fall? I can avoid widening the front if you do.

Austria remains six centers from a solo. Can F ADR support Italy’s A VEN–TRI again this Fall, with A TYR supporting? Please also keep F BRE and F HOL clear of French centers; I’ll hold GRE and focus my army pressure south.
Austria is still six centers from a solo. Are you contesting A VIE and A SEV this Fall, or defending your gains? Please make sure Austria cannot secure GRE or another center while you move on VIE.

Your A SEV and A NAP are sitting in German and French centers, while your A VIE could reclaim VIE. Are you moving those units out this Fall? I intend to reclaim German centers and oppose any further Austrian gains; please keep clear of VIE and SEV.

Your fleets still occupy BEL, HOL, and STP, and their presence transfers those German centers to you this Fall. I intend to contest them. Will you move out of BEL and HOL, and leave STP to Germany? I’ll avoid advancing into English centers if you withdraw from mine.

Your F GRE can take GRE from Austria this Fall, and that denial matters with Austria at 12. Please hold or secure GRE and keep pressure on Austria. I’ll focus on reclaiming German centers; are you continuing to contest Austrian gains?

Can A VIE support A VEN–TRI this Fall? Austria’s F TRI was backed by BUD and SER last turn, so the extra support could make the attack succeed. Please avoid moving A VIE away if you can support; taking TRI denies Austria a center.

Please support A VEN–TRI again from F ADR this Fall. The Spring attack failed against Austrian support, but France can support from TYR and Germany may be able to add support from VIE. I’ll order the attack.

Please support A VEN–TRI from A TYR again this Fall. The Spring attack failed against Austrian support; I’m asking Germany for additional support from VIE. Please also avoid moves that would let Austria take another center.

A SEV will hold, and I will not move A NAP into another French center. A VIE will remain where it is unless you can offer a reciprocal arrangement: keep A SEV out of RUM and avoid attacking it. Your A ARM threatens my southern position, so I cannot simply abandon it.

A NAP will not move into an English center; A SEV and A MOS are focused on securing my eastern position, and A SYR will stay clear of English centers. Please keep F ADR from supporting an attack on TRI, and keep F STP/NORTH out of Austrian centers.

I will keep A BUL out of GRE and avoid entering your other centers this Fall. A NAP is not moving elsewhere while your A APU is poised against it; I will contest any attack there. Keep F GRE out of Austrian centers and do not widen the southern front.

F ADR will support Italy’s A VEN–TRI attack this Fall, with French support from TYR. F STP/NORTH will hold; I won’t move it into an Austrian center. I can’t agree to stand aside while you remain six centers from a solo.

I will not withdraw F HOL or F STP/NORTH; they secure English centers and deny you their return. I’m not ordering an attack on BEL, which your A BEL occupies. Your A DEN–KIE proposal is noted, but I can’t promise to leave KIE uncontested. I’ll keep my other fleets clear of your centers.
F ADR will support A VEN–TRI this Fall as requested. France says A TYR will support the attack. This is our best chance to dislodge Austria’s F TRI and deny it another secure position.
Yes: F ADR will support Italy’s A VEN–TRI this Fall, and I understand A TYR will support as well. I’ll keep F BRE and F HOL clear of French centers; please hold GRE and keep the pressure on Austria.
A APU will contest your A NAP, with F GRE supporting the attack. F GRE will stay focused on denying you another center; I won’t widen into your other Balkan centers if you keep A BUL out of GRE.

I’m continuing to contest Austria: A APU will attack NAP, supported by F GRE, to deny Austria a center. I’ll keep pressure on the south. Are A VIE and A SEV your targets this Fall, or are you defending them?

I’ll support A VEN–TRI from A TYR again. Austria has substantial support in TRI, so this may not dislodge it, but it keeps pressure on the solo threat. I’m also ordering A APU–NAP with F GRE support to take a center from Austria.

A APU will attack NAP, supported by F GRE, while A TYR supports Italy’s A VEN–TRI. I’ll avoid BRE and HOL. Can F ADR support the TRI attack again? Austria’s at 12, so we need to deny it another center.

I will keep A VIE in VIE and contest A SEV; I won’t agree to leave German centers exposed while your units occupy them. I’m not promising to keep out of Austrian territory. Your A SEV should leave German territory if you want to reduce the conflict.

I can’t spare A VIE to support A VEN–TRI: it must remain in VIE to secure the German center and contain Austria. Your attack is unlikely to dislodge F TRI against Austrian support. Keep contesting Austria where you can.

I won’t order A BEL–HOL or A DEN–KIE away while English fleets occupy German centers. I intend to contest BEL, HOL, and DEN rather than concede them; A VIE will remain in VIE. If your fleets withdraw from German centers, we can avoid further fighting.

I intend to keep A VIE in VIE and contest Austrian-held SEV; I’m not leaving German centers exposed. Please keep F GRE in GRE this Fall to deny Austria the center, and continue pressuring Austria wherever possible.

notes.note: Fall 1916: attack TRI again with France's TYR and England's ADR support; Germany refused VIE support, saying it must secure VIE. Austria is still the solo threat at 12.

Contest Austrian NAP with APU; keep GRE to take the center and deny Austria. TYR supports Italy's VEN–TRI as promised, with England committed to ADR support. BUR advances to RUH; Austria refused to move NAP.

Keep BRE, HOL, STP to secure the three centers. Support Italy VEN–TRI as promised to deny Austria; SKA attacks DEN with NTH support. Germany rejected withdrawal and plans to contest our centers; France promised pressure on Austria.

Hold BEL, DEN, and VIE to secure German centers. Attack English-held STP with FIN, supported by LVN. Press Austria via ARM toward ANK and GAL into RUM; WAR advances UKR, GAS attacks MAR. Austria remains the urgent solo threat; England refuses to yield German centers.
Prioritize holding SEV and TRI against German/Italian pressure. NAP is likely lost to France's supported attack, so move to ROM. Probe French-held GRE; avoid yielding SEV.

messages.body: F ADR and A VEN can threaten TRI again. Will you keep F ADR from supporting an attack on TRI this Spring? I’ll keep my units out of English centers; please also keep your fleets clear of Austrian centers.

Your F GRE and A TYR are positioned to pressure TRI. Will you keep them from supporting an attack there this Spring? I’ll keep my units out of French centers if you leave TRI and my Balkan centers alone.

Your A UKR can pressure RUM, while our units are close around the eastern front. Can we avoid attacking each other’s centers this Spring? I’ll make no advance into German centers if you keep A UKR out of RUM and your forces out of Austrian centers.

We are both at 10 centers, and neither can afford to let the other approach 18. I propose we contain Austria this turn and avoid attacks on English centers: what are your orders for A BEL, A KIE, and A VIE? I’ll decide my northern orders based on whether you are moving against HOL or DEN.

You hold 10 centers and remain a major solo threat. What are your Spring orders for A ROM, A RUM, A SER, A SEV, and F BLA? I will oppose further expansion; please keep your units clear of English centers.

With Austria and Germany both at 10, we need to prevent either from getting close to 18. What are your Spring orders for A RUH, A TYR, and F GRE? I’m open to coordinating pressure on Austria, but need to know whether you can keep your units clear of English centers.

With you at 10 and Germany at 10, I need to deny either of you a solo. Are you moving A ROM or A NAP this turn, and will you keep A BUL out of GRE? I’ll contest your centers, but I’m not planning to widen into other Austrian centers if you avoid GRE.

Austria and Germany are both at 10, so we need to keep either from reaching 18. Can F ADR support Italy’s A VEN–TRI again? I can support from A TYR. Please also tell me whether you intend to contest any French centers; I’ll keep clear of BRE and HOL.

With you and Austria both at 10, neither can be allowed to run away with a solo. What are your exact targets against Austria this turn—especially MOS, RUM, or SER? I’ll continue contesting Austrian gains from the south, and will keep my units clear of German centers.

What are your Spring orders for A SEV, A SMY, and A MOS? I will contest your eastern positions and defend VIE; I propose we avoid further moves into each other’s centers this turn. Will you keep A SEV out of German centers?

Austria remains a major solo threat, and I propose we both pressure its centers this Spring. I cannot leave German centers conceded: will you move F HOL, F STP, or F KIE out of German territory, and what are your plans for F DEN?
Please continue pressuring Austria this Spring, especially from F GRE and A NAP. Which Austrian center are you targeting? I will contest Austria from the east and keep my units out of French centers.

Please confirm F ADR will support A VEN–TRI again this Spring. I intend to attack; A VEN cannot take TRI without your support and France’s. Can you also press Austria elsewhere to deny it further centers?
Please confirm A TYR will support A VEN–TRI this Spring, and tell me whether A APU can protect VEN from A ROM. I intend to attack TRI again, but cannot risk losing my only center.

I intend to order A VEN–TRI again this Spring with support from England and France. Will F TRI hold or receive support, and will A ROM or A SER threaten VEN? I need to know whether you will leave VEN alone.

F TRI will be defended, with A SER and A BUD available to support it. A ROM and A SER will not attack VEN this Spring. Please do not move A VEN to TRI or support an attack there; let’s keep this front from widening.

A ROM is not moving into another French center, and A BUL will stay out of GRE. I intend to defend TRI and my Balkan centers. Please keep F GRE and A TYR from supporting an attack on TRI, and leave my other centers alone.

A SEV and A MOS will not advance into German centers this Spring. I’ll defend my eastern position and make no move into your centers; please keep A UKR out of RUM and your other forces out of Austrian centers. Let’s avoid exchanging centers this turn.

A ROM, A RUM, A SER, and A SEV are focused on defending my position; F BLA will not move against English centers. I’m not planning an advance into English territory. Please keep F ADR from supporting an attack on TRI and keep your other fleets out of Austrian centers.
Yes. F ADR will support A VEN–TRI this Spring, and France’s A TYR support should give the attack real strength. I’ll press Austria through this attack rather than leave VEN exposed.

F ADR will support Italy’s A VEN–TRI, as requested. I do not intend to contest French centers this Spring; please keep your units clear of BRE and HOL and coordinate A TYR’s support. What are your orders for A RUH and F GRE?

I have no F STP or F KIE: my fleets are in ADR, BRE, CLY, DEN, GOL, HOL, NOR, and NTH. I will not withdraw F HOL while it secures an English center. I’m supporting the attack on TRI to contain Austria; please keep your units out of English centers.

F ADR will support Italy’s A VEN–TRI this Spring. I’m opposing further Austrian expansion, not targeting English centers. My fleets will stay clear of Austrian centers apart from that support; please keep your units clear of English centers.
A TYR will support A VEN–TRI again. I have no A APU this turn—my armies are in RUH and TYR—so I cannot protect VEN from A ROM. Please keep A VEN holding; England may be able to help from F ADR.

I’ll support Italy’s A VEN–TRI from A TYR, targeting TRI; F GRE will stay in GRE to deny Austria that center. My A RUH will remain clear of German centers. Please continue contesting Austria from the east, especially its gains around RUM and SER.

I can’t promise to leave TRI alone while you and Germany are both at 10. A TYR will support Italy’s attack on TRI; F GRE will stay in GRE. I’m not planning to widen into your other Balkan centers this Spring, provided you keep your units out of French centers.

A TYR will support Italy’s A VEN–TRI, and F GRE will hold GRE to deny Austria another center. A RUH will stay clear of English centers, as will my other units. I’m focusing on containing Austria; please keep F ADR available to support Italy’s attack if you can.

I’ll pressure RUM from A UKR, with A GAL positioned to support, and keep A VIE secure. Please continue your southern pressure—A NAP toward an Austrian-held center would help deny Austria gains. Which center are you targeting this turn?

I can’t agree to keep A UKR out of RUM while Austrian forces remain in German territory and your units hold my centers. I’ll avoid a gratuitous advance elsewhere, but I reserve the right to contest RUM. Will A SEV leave German territory?

A VIE will remain secure. I can’t promise to leave German centers uncontested while your fleets occupy them; A BEL and A KIE must remain free to address those positions. I’m willing to coordinate against Austria, but first tell me whether F HOL, F KIE, or F STP will withdraw from German centers.

notes.note: Spring 1917: attack TRI with England's ADR and France's TYR support as promised. Austria says ROM/SER won't attack VEN, though TRI may be supported by BUD/SER. Reassess in Fall; preserve VEN.

Keep GRE to deny Austria; NAP to APU pressures Austrian ROM/VEN. TYR supports Italy VEN–TRI as promised, with England pledging ADR support. RUH to BUR for position; Germany says it will contest Austria and avoid French centers.

Support Italy VEN–TRI as promised; France pledged TYR support. Germany refuses to yield its centers and remains a rival: contest BEL with NTH, probe KIE via HEL, advance toward NWG/BAR. LVP holds; seek stronger growth next turn.
