Press Austria: UKR-RUM supported by GAL; LVN attacks MOS with STP support. Take open CON with ANK and pressure English HOL with BEL/KIE. VIE attacks French TYR with MUN support; MAR advances GAS. England and France proposed containing Austria; Austria asked for non-aggression, which I declined.

Defend TRI against English/Italian/French-supported attack: BUD and SER support hold; expect strength 3 attack. Layer BLA and SEV support on RUM against Germany’s UKR threat. Probe WAR and GRE; ROM presses NAP. Germany and France have both refused firm non-aggression; England openly backs TRI attack.

messages.body: Your A CON and A MOS are positioned to take two Austrian centers this Fall, while my A WAR occupies yours. Can we avoid exchanging centers? Keep CON and MOS in place and I will not advance A WAR into another German center. What are your orders for UKR and WAR?

I need to know whether F ADR will again support an attack on TRI this Fall. Please keep F ADR and your other fleets out of Austrian centers; I will keep my forces clear of English centers. What are your plans for F ADR?

A NAP is currently on your center, and A APU could contest it. I propose we avoid widening the southern front: keep A APU and F GRE out of Austrian centers, and I will keep my forces out of your other centers. What are your Fall plans for A APU and F GRE?

We are both at 10, and I will not cede English-held HOL or BEL. This Fall I’m focused on keeping my centers and preventing either rival from gaining freely. Are A HOL or your other units moving against English centers? I can avoid other German centers if you keep your units out of English centers.

Austria and Germany are both at 10, and either could become the main solo threat. What are your Fall orders for A APU, A BOH, A BUR, and F GRE? I’m willing to coordinate against their gains, but need your units to stay clear of English centers.

You and Germany are both at 10, so I’ll oppose further expansion by either. What are your Fall plans for A NAP, A SER, A SEV, and F BLA? Keep your units clear of English centers; I’ll keep pressure on the other solo threats.

This Fall your units appear set to take CON, MOS, and WAR, while England can gain BEL and HOL. What are your exact orders against England? I can avoid your centers and help contest English expansion, but need to know your plan.

With BEL and HOL poised to change to you, you may reach 11 centers. What are your Fall targets, especially against Germany? I’m not contesting BRE or HOL, but need to prevent either you or Germany from running away toward a solo.

Germany is poised to take CON, MOS, and WAR, while your A NAP occupies my center. What are your Fall plans for NAP and against Germany? I need to reclaim NAP and prevent Germany or England from building toward a solo.

This Fall I intend to take CON and MOS and reclaim WAR, while your A NAP threatens NAP. Please clarify whether A SEV and A RUM will leave German centers; I cannot agree to leave CON, MOS, or WAR uncontested while your units occupy them.

With both of us at 10 and Austria at 10, we cannot let Austria gain this Fall. I intend to contest CON, MOS, and WAR. Will your fleets leave BEL and HOL, or should I continue trying to reclaim them? Please avoid taking another German center.

Austria’s NAP unit is poised to reclaim NAP, while I’m contesting CON, MOS, and WAR. Can you keep A NAP from taking an additional center or otherwise pressure Austria this Fall? I’ll keep my units out of French centers.
Please confirm F ADR will support A VEN–TRI this Fall. I will order the attack; Austria’s F TRI is still the key obstacle, and your support is essential.
Can A TYR support A VEN–TRI this Fall? Your unit in TYR can support the attack and help dislodge Austria’s F TRI. I will keep A VEN out of any German centers.
I intend to order A VEN–TRI this Fall with English support. Will you be supporting F TRI from A SER or A BUD, and will A VEN remain unthreatened by your other units?

I won’t abandon Austrian centers to make this easier for you. A SEV and A RUM will defend my eastern position; A WAR will not advance into another German center. I can avoid widening the contest if you keep A CON and A MOS from taking my centers and do not attack WAR.

A NAP will defend my position, A SER will help protect TRI, and A SEV will defend the east. F BLA is not moving against English centers. I’m not planning an advance into your territory; please keep F ADR from supporting an attack on TRI.

A NAP will defend its position. I will keep A BUL out of GRE and avoid advancing into your other centers. Please keep A APU out of NAP and F GRE out of Austrian centers; Germany is threatening CON, MOS, and WAR, and I don’t want to widen our southern fight.

A SER will support F TRI, and I will keep A ROM and A SER clear of VEN. Please keep A VEN out of TRI and do not support an attack there; Germany is threatening my eastern centers, so I need to avoid opening another front.

I will not leave BEL or HOL: they are English centers, and your armies there are changing their ownership. I’ll contest those positions and avoid unrelated German centers where possible. Do not advance into English centers if you want to limit the fighting.

I’m contesting Germany’s hold on BEL and HOL rather than conceding English centers. I’ll also keep F ADR supporting Italy’s attack on TRI to deny Austria a gain. Please keep your units clear of BRE and HOL; with Austria and Germany both at 10, we need to contain both.

F ADR will again support Italy’s A VEN–TRI this Fall. I will keep my other fleets clear of Austrian centers, but I cannot stand aside while you and Germany remain at 10 centers. Please keep your units clear of English centers as you proposed.
Confirmed: F ADR will support A VEN–TRI this Fall. I’m keeping that commitment to help dislodge Austria’s F TRI and prevent Austria gaining another center.

I’m targeting NAP with A APU, supported by F GRE, to reclaim my center and deny Austria a gain. I won’t move into German centers this turn. Your best pressure against England is to secure BEL and HOL; let me know if you’re contesting either so I can avoid interfering.

A APU will attack NAP with F GRE supporting; I’m focused on reclaiming my center and denying Austria another gain. I’ll keep my units clear of BRE and HOL. I don’t have a direct attack on Germany’s northern centers from my current positions, but I support you contesting its expansion.

A APU will attack NAP, supported by F GRE. I can’t leave my center in your hands while you and Germany are both at 10. I’m not widening into your other centers this turn; keep A BUL out of GRE and your forces out of my remaining centers.

A HOL will hold, and I intend to contest BEL; I will not leave German centers to you. I’m taking CON and MOS and reclaiming WAR from Austria. You should avoid taking BEL or HOL this Fall; with Austria also in the fight, neither of us benefits from gifting the other centers.

I intend A TYR–TRI, supported by A VEN, to help dislodge Austria’s F TRI; A CON and A MOS will contest Austrian-held centers, and A GAL will reclaim WAR. I’ll keep my units out of French centers. Please keep pressure on Austria and avoid helping England take BEL or HOL.

I cannot leave CON, MOS, or WAR uncontested while your units occupy them. I intend to press those positions this Fall; you should move A WAR out of my center and avoid advancing further into German territory. I’m not agreeing to an exchange that leaves your gains intact.
Yes. A TYR will support A VEN–TRI this Fall. I’m also contesting Austria in CON, MOS, and WAR, so keep A VEN out of German centers and make the attack on TRI count.

notes.note: Fall 1917: attack TRI; England promised ADR support and Germany promised TYR support, Austria says SER supports TRI and asks me to stay out. Prioritize denying Austria's growth.

Attack Austrian-held NAP with APU, but GRE has no support option for that move, so NAP attack is unsupported. BOH to VIE and BUR to RUH pressure Germany; break my promise to avoid German centers to contain its growth. Austria/Germany both 10; England poised to gain.
Hold CON, HOL, MOS to secure Fall gains; support GAL–WAR with MOS and UKR to reclaim WAR. KIE contests DEN, MAR takes SPA if open, MUN advances RUH. TYR supports Italy’s VEN–TRI as promised.

Contest German captures: BLA supports BUL to dislodge CON; WAR supports SEV to retake MOS. Hold TRI with SER support against English-backed VEN attack. Evacuate NAP to ROM rather than lose the unit; France may take NAP. Germany rejected exchange; England and France remain hostile.

Keep BEL to secure its Fall transfer to England. Honor Italy promise: ADR supports VEN–TRI, though Austria's defense may hold. Germany occupies HOL; HEL holds rather than risk losing BEL. Probe MAO, NTH, SWE, and GOL.

messages.body: You now have 11 centers and can solo in seven. I propose we stop exchanging centers: keep A ANK out of CON and A UKR out of RUM; I will keep my forces out of German centers this turn. Are you willing to focus on England instead?

Germany is now at 11 and is the immediate solo threat. Will you stop supporting Italy’s attack on TRI and coordinate pressure on Germany instead? I can’t afford to leave TRI exposed while Germany advances through the east.

Germany’s 11 centers make it the immediate solo threat. Can we avoid attacks on each other this turn and focus on stopping its expansion? Please keep A TYR and F GRE from supporting an attack on TRI; I will keep my forces out of French centers.

At 11 centers, you are the immediate solo threat. What are A HOL, A DEN, and A BER doing this Spring? I will defend English-held BEL and keep my other units clear of German centers if you keep your units out of English centers. Any move against BEL risks opening a wider war.

Germany is at 11 and Austria at 9; neither can be allowed a free gain toward 18. Can we coordinate to contain Germany this turn? My fleets can defend BEL and pressure the north; please keep your units clear of English centers and tell me your plans for A BUR and A VIE.

Germany is at 11 and remains the leading solo threat. What are your plans for A SER, A SEV, and F BLA this Spring? I will keep my units clear of Austrian centers if you keep yours clear of English centers; I cannot stand aside if either Germany or Austria makes another unchecked gain.

Germany is at 11 and the immediate solo threat. I can move A BUR–MAR with A PAR supporting; MAR is currently unoccupied. Please tell me your plans against Germany, especially whether you can contest HOL and keep pressure on its northern centers.

Germany is at 11 and close to a solo. Can you direct your eastern units against German centers this turn and avoid pressure on VIE? I can target MAR from BUR with PAR support; let’s coordinate to deny Germany gains.

You are at 11, so I need to know your plans before orders. Are you targeting French or Austrian centers this turn? I intend to move against MAR unless you have a concrete proposal to contain England instead.

Your A WAR, A CON, and A MOS remain in positions I intend to contest. What are your orders for them and for A RUM? I’m willing to avoid widening the conflict if you stop advancing into German centers, but I won’t leave WAR uncontested.

Will your fleets contest Austria this turn, and what are your plans for F BEL and F HOL? I intend to reclaim German centers and cannot leave BEL or HOL uncontested. Please avoid taking another German center while we both contain Austria.

Please continue pressuring Austria from the south: what are your plans for A NAP and F GRE? I’m contesting Austrian positions in the east and will keep my units out of French centers. Coordinated pressure can deny Austria further gains.

Austria remains a major solo threat, and your A TYR can support A VEN–TRI. Please confirm you will support the attack again this Spring; I’ll order A VEN–TRI. What are your plans to stop Austria and protect your own centers?

Can A VIE support my A VEN–TRI this Spring? With your support and Germany’s A TYR, we may finally dislodge F TRI despite Austrian support. Please confirm, and tell me whether you can keep Austria from gaining centers elsewhere.
I intend to order A VEN–TRI this Spring. Will F TRI receive support from A SER or A BUD? Please keep A ROM and A SER clear of VEN; I will not attack any other Austrian center this turn.

A SER will support F TRI; A SEV will defend the east, and F BLA will not move against English centers. Germany’s A ANK threatens CON and its eastern army mass is the urgent danger. Please stop supporting Italy’s attack on TRI and use your position to contain Germany; I’ll keep my forces clear of English centers.

A SER will support F TRI this Spring, and A ROM and A SER will stay clear of VEN. Please keep A VEN out of TRI; Germany is the immediate solo threat, and we should not spend forces attacking each other while it advances.

I can direct eastern forces against Germany and avoid pressure on VIE. I cannot promise a move that leaves my centers exposed, but I’ll avoid French centers this turn. Please use A BUR and A PAR to contest MAR and coordinate with England to block Germany’s expansion.

A WAR will not advance into another German center, but I cannot abandon my positions or leave Austrian centers undefended. A RUM will defend against A UKR, and I will contest any attack on CON. Your A ANK is poised to threaten it; focus on England rather than widening the eastern fight.

Yes, I’ll stop supporting an attack on TRI this turn and focus on containing Germany. Please use A SER and F BLA to keep TRI secure and avoid English centers; tell me where A SEV is headed so we can coordinate pressure on Germany.

I’ll contest HOL with F BEL, supported from the north if needed, and defend BEL against Germany. A BUR–MAR with A PAR support is useful pressure on Germany; please proceed if that remains your plan. Keep your units clear of English centers.

I’ll keep F BEL defending English-held BEL and will not leave it open to your reclaiming move. Germany at 11 is the immediate solo threat, so I can’t promise to avoid contesting HOL. I’ll focus on containing you; do not move into English centers.

I can keep F GRE out of TRI; it will hold GRE. I have no A TYR. I intend to pressure Germany at MAR from BUR, with PAR supporting. A VIE is already in French hands, and I need your eastern units to contest Germany rather than pressure it.

A BUR will move to MAR with A PAR supporting; A VIE will support Italy’s attack on TRI, while A NAP and F GRE hold. Please contest Germany’s northern centers and prevent it from gaining in the north; I’ll keep my units clear of English centers.
Yes, A VIE will support A VEN–TRI. I’ll keep Austria from gaining in the south: A NAP and F GRE will hold, and I’m using A BUR with A PAR support to attack Germany’s MAR.

A NAP and F GRE will hold; I’m not directing them against Austria this turn. A BUR will attack MAR with A PAR supporting, and A VIE will support Italy’s A VEN–TRI. Your expansion is the immediate danger, so I’m coordinating to deny you further gains.

No. I will not leave WAR uncontested or promise to keep ANK out of CON while your units hold German centers. My priority is to recover WAR and take the openings available; if A WAR, A CON, and A MOS leave German centers, we can limit further clashes.

A HOL and A DEN will defend German interests and A BER will not move into an English center this Spring. I cannot promise to leave BEL or HOL uncontested while English fleets hold them. I’m willing to avoid unrelated English centers if you keep clear of German centers and help contain Austria.

I confirm A TYR will support A VEN–TRI again this Spring. My eastern units will contest Austrian positions and protect German centers; please keep A VEN out of German centers and proceed with the attack on TRI.

I’m targeting Austrian positions, not French centers, this Spring. I intend to keep my forces clear of MAR and other French centers. Please continue pressure from the south; your plans for A NAP and F GRE would help deny Austria gains.

notes.note: Spring 1918: attack TRI; France promised VIE support and Germany TYR support. Austria says SER supports TRI and asks me to stay out. Take TRI if possible; reassess Fall.

BUR attacks MAR, though PAR cannot support that move. GRE and NAP hold as promised to Austria; VIE supports Italy VEN–TRI. England plans to contest HOL and defend BEL; Germany says it will stay out of French centers while targeting Austria.
Germany is the immediate solo threat. Attack ANK from CON with ARM and BLA support; cover SEV and RUM, and keep TRI secure with SER support while Italy threatens it. Move ROM toward APU; TRI to ADR.

Contain Germany while protecting BEL; F GOL supports France’s BUR–MAR. France has promised pressure on Germany and to avoid English centers. Austria asked me to stop aiding TRI; I agreed. Germany still contests BEL/HOL and has not promised to leave them alone.
Press Austrian centers with ANK–CON and UKR–RUM; TYR supports Italy’s VEN–TRI as promised. Shift eastern forces toward LVN/GAL. Avoid duplicate destinations; HOL to KIE, MUN to RUH.

messages.body: Germany can still win with seven centers, and A SWE is sitting in its center. Please use F BAL to attack SWE and keep F ADR out of TRI. I’ll keep pressure on German positions and avoid English centers; can you confirm your orders?

Please keep A MAR in MAR this Fall so Germany cannot reclaim that center. Germany remains the immediate solo threat; can you also coordinate with England to contest its centers? I’ll avoid French centers.
Please move A TRI out of TRI this Fall, ideally to VEN, and do not support an attack on TRI. Germany is still close to a solo, so we need to stop trading Austrian centers among ourselves.

You are poised to gain MAR, SWE, and SMY this Fall and reach 14. I will contest SWE; do not move A SWE into NOR or otherwise attack English centers. What are your orders for A SWE, A HOL, and A PRU? I’ll coordinate to stop your gains.

Germany can gain MAR, SWE, and SMY this Fall. What are your orders for A MAR, A PAR, and F GRE? Please make sure Germany does not retain MAR, and coordinate with Austria and me to deny Germany further centers.

Germany is poised to gain MAR, SWE, and SMY this Fall. Please use A ANK and A SMY to deny its eastern gains, and keep your units clear of English centers. What are your orders for A ANK, A SEV, and F BLA? I’m contesting Germany in the north.

Germany can gain ANK and SWE, and its A SMY is poised to take your center. Please use A ANK–SMY and direct your eastern forces against German centers; I’ll hold A MAR with A PAR supporting to deny Germany MAR.

Germany is at 11 and may gain ANK, SMY, and SWE this Fall. Please use F BAL to contest A SWE, and keep pressure on Germany’s northern centers. I’ll hold A MAR with A PAR supporting, so Germany cannot reclaim it easily.

This Fall A ANK will secure ANK for Germany, and I intend to press for additional centers. Your A SMY is sitting in an Austrian center; will you move it out rather than contest German holdings? I will not leave German centers uncontested.
A MAR occupies a German center, and I intend to reclaim it. Please move A MAR out of MAR this Fall and do not support a defense there; I will keep my units out of your other centers where possible.
Your A TRI can take TRI from Austria by holding there this Fall. Please keep it in TRI and avoid German centers; denying Austria that center helps contain its expansion.
A TRI is now in position to take Austria’s TRI for Italy this Fall. Please order F ADR to support A TRI holding; Austria can attack from SER, so your support is crucial. Can you confirm?
Please have A VIE support A TRI holding this Fall. Keeping TRI out of Austria’s hands denies it a center and helps contain Germany’s solo threat. Can you confirm?

Please have A TYR support A TRI holding this Fall so Italy can retain TRI and deny Austria the center. With your 11 centers, preventing Austria’s recovery matters, but I will not support your expansion toward 18.

A ANK will contest A SMY, and A SEV will defend against German pressure. F BLA will support the eastern defense rather than move against English centers. I’m counting on F BAL to attack A SWE and F ADR to stay out of TRI as we discussed.

A ANK can attack A SMY, and I’ll direct my eastern forces against Germany rather than French centers. Please keep A MAR in place with A PAR supporting, and coordinate with England to deny Germany SWE and its other gains.

I won’t simply vacate A ANK while you threaten Austrian centers. Your A SMY is a direct threat to Austrian territory, so I will contest it. I’m willing to avoid widening the fight if you stop pressing my centers; otherwise I’ll defend them.
Confirmed: F ADR will support A TRI holding this Fall. Austria’s A SER is the threat, and keeping TRI denies Austria the center. I’ll also use F BAL to contest SWE and stop Germany gaining there.

Please hold A MAR with A PAR supporting as planned; Germany must not reclaim MAR. I’m contesting A SWE with F BAL and pressing the northern position. Keep your units clear of English centers, and let me know if you can further obstruct Germany’s eastern gains.

I’ll use F BAL to contest A SWE as requested. I can’t keep F ADR out of TRI: Italy needs support to hold it against A SER, and denying Germany’s projected gains is urgent. Please keep pressing Germany elsewhere and avoid English centers.

A MAR will hold with A PAR supporting its defense, denying Germany an easy recapture. I’m keeping F GRE and A NAP out of English centers. Please use F BAL to contest A SWE and continue pressure on Germany’s northern centers.
Confirmed: A VIE will support A TRI holding this Fall. Keeping TRI out of Austrian hands denies Austria a gain and helps contain Germany.
I will not move A MAR out or leave it unsupported. A MAR will hold with A PAR supporting its defense; Germany’s growth is the immediate threat, and I won’t help you reclaim MAR.
I’ll keep A MAR in MAR with A PAR supporting its defense, as you request, to deny Germany the center. I’ll avoid Austrian centers this Fall.

A SWE will hold, with A PRU supporting it; I will not move into NOR. A HOL will hold to secure the German center. I’m not conceding SWE or HOL, and I expect you to keep your fleets clear of other German centers.
A TYR will support A TRI holding in TRI this Fall. Keep A TRI there and out of German centers; denying Austria TRI is useful, but I cannot promise further support for Italian expansion.
I will keep A TRI in TRI to reclaim it for Italy and deny Austria the center. Please have A TYR support A TRI holding, as you proposed; I will keep clear of German centers.
I cannot move A TRI to VEN: holding TRI reclaims a center for Italy and denies you one. Germany is the immediate solo threat, so I will not support an attack on your other centers this turn.

notes.note: Hold TRI to reclaim Italy's center and deny Austria. England, France, and Germany each promised support for the hold; Austria asked me to leave, which I refused. Germany remains the solo threat.
Hold GRE, NAP, and PAR to protect French centers. Keep MAR to claim it for France and deny Germany, though PAR has no order to support MAR holding. VIE supports Italy’s TRI hold as promised.

Contest German gains: attack SWE (though unsupported), take open DEN, and attack HOL with BEL supported by HEL. Advance GOL to PIE, MAO to GAS, NWG to BAR; WAL returns to LVP. France says MAR holds with PAR support; Austria wants ADR out of TRI, but I promised Italy ADR support.

Secure SWE and SMY for the Fall. Attack BEL with HOL supported by RUH; press RUM with UKR supported by GAL, and move LVN to MOS. Support Italy's TRI hold as promised; TYR->BOH was an option but supporting TRI honors agreement.

Fall: convoy APU to TRI with ADR, supported by BUD and SER, to reclaim it from Italy. ANK attacks German-held SMY with ARM support, accepting the loss of ANK claim to deny Germany SMY. SEV probes MOS; preserve RUM. England says contest SWE; France holds MAR.

messages.body: Germany is at 11 and remains the only immediate solo threat. Will F BAL and your northern units contest German centers again this Spring? I’ll keep my units out of English centers; please keep F ADR out of TRI so I can focus on Germany.

Your 11 centers put you seven from a solo. I will defend Austrian centers and contest advances toward them. Will you agree to stop pressing RUM, SEV, and TRI and focus on England instead? I can avoid widening into German centers if you do.

Germany is still the immediate solo threat. Will A VEN stay out of TRI this Spring, and can you coordinate against German positions instead? I’ll avoid VEN; I need to keep Austrian forces available to defend against Germany.

Germany remains the solo threat at 11. Please coordinate pressure on its southern positions while holding MAR; what are A VIE and A MAR doing this Spring? I’ll contest German positions in the north, especially SWE and HOL.

Germany is still seven centers from a solo. Please use your eastern units to contest its positions and avoid English centers. What are A ARM, A SEV, and F BLA doing this Spring? I’ll keep pressure on Germany in the north.
You remain the immediate solo threat at 11. What are A SWE, A HOL, and A FIN doing this Spring? I intend to contest your northern positions and will not leave English centers open to your advance.

Germany remains at 11 and is still the immediate solo threat. What are your Spring targets? Please use your northern fleets to contest German centers—especially SWE, HOL, and DEN—and tell me whether you can pressure its northern position while I keep my units clear of English centers.

Germany is still one center from a dangerous 12 and remains the shared solo threat. What are your Spring orders against its eastern positions? Please direct your units toward German centers rather than French ones; I’ll avoid Austrian centers this turn.

You are still at 11, so I need to know whether you intend to attack French centers this Spring. I’m asking England and Austria to contest your expansion. I can avoid your centers if you keep your units out of French centers; what are your concrete orders?

Our forces are positioned against your eastern centers. Will A RUM, A SER, and A BUD hold or move this Spring? I’m willing to avoid widening the fight if you keep your units out of German centers, but I won’t promise to leave your centers uncontested.

Your A VIE and A MAR are close to German forces, and I need to know whether you intend to attack this Spring. I’m considering moves against French centers; if you keep clear of German centers and avoid supporting Austria, we can limit the fighting.

Germany needs room to recover centers. What are F BEL and F DEN doing this Spring? I ask that you avoid moves against German centers while I secure my position; I will not promise to leave BEL uncontested.

Germany is at 11 and is the immediate solo threat. Please support my A TRI holding from A VIE this Spring, and use your other units to contest German centers rather than open a front against me. What are your orders against Germany?

Germany is at 11 and needs to be stopped before it reaches 18. Please use your fleets to contest German centers, especially SWE or the northern coast, and tell me where you plan to apply pressure. I’ll keep A TRI secure against Austria.

Please have A TYR support my A TRI holding this Spring, as before, and keep A TYR from entering TRI. Germany’s lead makes it important to prevent Austria or you from gaining an easy center here. What are your plans to contain Austria this turn?

A ARM will contest SMY and A SEV will pressure MOS; A RUM and A SER will cover the eastern approach. I’ll keep my units out of French centers. Please continue denying Germany MAR and coordinate with England to contest its northern gains.

A ARM will contest SMY, A SEV will pressure MOS, and F BLA will stay in the eastern theater rather than move against English centers. I’ll keep A RUM covered against UKR. Please contest German centers in the north again, and keep F ADR out of TRI.

A RUM will hold, with A SER supporting its defense; A BUD will hold as well. Your forces remain a threat to my centers, so I won’t promise to leave German positions uncontested. I’m directing eastern pressure against your holdings rather than widening toward your western centers.

I’ll continue contesting Germany’s north, with F BAL targeting SWE and pressure on HOL. I have no F ADR in the current position, so I cannot support TRI. Please use A ARM/A SEV and F BLA to obstruct Germany’s eastern units and deny it centers; I’ll keep my forces clear of Austrian centers.

I’ll contest SWE from the Baltic and keep pressure on HOL; Germany must not be allowed another easy gain. Please hold MAR with A PAR’s support and press Germany from the south where possible. My fleets will stay clear of English centers, and I’d welcome coordinated pressure on German positions.

I’ll use F BAL to contest SWE and keep pressure on Germany’s northern positions, including HOL. I have no fleet in ADR now, so I can’t support TRI this turn. Please keep A TRI secure as promised and look for chances to obstruct Germany without exposing your center.

I can’t agree to leave German positions uncontested while you remain at 11 centers and refuse to leave BEL alone. I intend to contest SWE and HOL from the north. Keep your units out of English centers; I’ll avoid unrelated English-held positions where possible.

I’ll support A TRI holding from A VIE as requested. Against Germany, A MAR will hold and A PAR will support it; A VIE will stay committed to TRI, so I can’t also use it for another attack. Keep A VEN secure.

A MAR will hold with A PAR supporting its defense; A VIE will support Italy’s A TRI holding. I’ll keep my forces clear of English centers. Please contest German centers in the north, especially SWE, HOL, and DEN, and avoid allowing Germany another easy gain.

I will not promise to leave MAR undefended: A MAR will hold, supported by A PAR. A VIE is supporting Italy’s TRI hold. I have no order against your centers this Spring, but Germany remains the chief solo threat, and I’m coordinating with England and Austria to contain your expansion.

I will not promise to leave RUM, SEV, or TRI uncontested while Austrian forces threaten German positions. I’m willing to keep this turn’s eastern fighting limited if you keep your units out of German centers. What are A RUM, A SER, and A BUD doing?

I’m not committing to leave French centers alone while A MAR and A VIE remain near German positions. My immediate priority is securing German interests and preventing others from gaining freely; I won’t disclose exact orders. If you keep out of German centers and stop supporting Austria, we can limit the conflict.

A TYR will support A TRI holding this Spring, as requested. I’ll continue contesting Austria in the east, but I can’t promise further support for Italian expansion. Keep A VEN clear of German centers.

I won’t disclose exact orders for A SWE, A HOL, or A FIN. I need to secure German positions and cannot promise to leave English centers uncontested while English fleets hold German centers. If F BEL and F DEN avoid further German centers, we may be able to limit the fighting.

I can’t vacate TRI; it is an Italian center and holding it restores my position. I will turn pressure toward Germany instead: A TRI–VIE and A VEN–TYR. If A SER can support TRI–VIE, we can contest Germany’s foothold there while your forces defend against its eastern advance. I won’t attack your other centers this turn.

notes.note: Hold TRI while France and Germany have promised support; take vacant Austrian ROM with VEN. Austria says it will avoid VEN, but watch for a Fall counterattack. Germany remains the main solo threat.

Concentrate north: DEN to open KIE with BAL/HEL support; BEL attacks HOL, BAR takes open STP. MAO contests German SPA; PIE supports France's MAR hold. Keep pressuring Germany; France promised MAR defense, Austria promised eastern pressure; no new outcomes yet.

MAR holds to deny Germany, though PAR has no hold-support order available. NAP moves toward Austrian ROM; GRE to ION sets up a possible convoy toward TUN next turn. VIE supports Italy’s TRI hold as promised.

Contest German ANK and MOS; defend RUM against German pressure with BLA and BUD support. SER moves to vacated TRI as Italy heads for VIE. France still occupies VIE; England promised northern pressure, Germany refuses restraint.

Press Austria with UKR-RUM supported by GAL; CON advances on BUL. HOL attacks BEL with RUH support. Protect SWE against English fleets. Move SPA toward POR; LVN to MOS and SIL to BER. Austria, France, and England are coordinating containment; Italy asked for TYR support of TRI, not given.

messages.body: Germany remains seven centers from victory, and this Fall’s center changes are decisive. Please contest its gains in the north again and avoid Austrian centers. I’m holding the eastern line; what German centers are your units targeting?

I’m recapturing ANK and will defend my centers. With England contesting your northern gains, a fight here risks letting another power grow. Will you leave BUL and my other centers alone this Fall if I avoid advancing into your holdings?

Your Spring plan to move A TRI–VIE would attack a French-held center and could open another front. Germany is still the solo threat. Please avoid Austrian centers this Fall and direct pressure against German holdings instead; I’ll keep my forces focused on the eastern line.

Germany is at 11 and can still reach a solo. Please use your eastern units to contest German centers this Fall, especially ANK, BUL, and SMY, and keep your forces clear of English centers. I’ll continue contesting German-held centers in the north.

Germany’s 11 centers make this a critical Fall. Please contest its southern holdings and avoid letting it retain any easy gains; what are A MAR, A VIE, and your fleets doing? I’ll keep pressure on the north and defend English centers.

You remain seven centers from a solo, so I cannot agree to leave your positions uncontested. I’ll defend English-held BEL, KIE, and the northern centers. Keep your units out of English centers; are you planning moves against BEL or other English centers this Fall?

Germany’s 11 centers still make it the immediate solo threat. What are your Fall targets against its centers? I can keep A MAR supported from A PIC against a German attack; please use your northern units to contest Germany and deny its gains.

Please use your eastern units to contest German centers this Fall, especially from the approaches to MOS and ANK. I’ll keep A MAR protected against Germany; what are your concrete orders against its positions?

I’m not seeking German centers this Fall, but I will defend A MAR. Are you ordering an attack on MAR or another French center? Germany’s expansion is drawing coordinated opposition from England and Austria.

This Fall, will F KIE, F SPA/NORTH, and F STP/NORTH hold, or are you moving them? I intend to secure German centers and will contest these occupations. If you keep clear of German centers beyond those positions, we can limit the fighting.
A POR occupies a German center, and I intend to reclaim it. Will you move A POR out this Fall and avoid supporting a defense there? I will keep my units out of your other centers where possible.
A ANK and A BUL are positioned to secure German centers this Fall. Will A RUM, A SER, and A SMY contest them, or can we limit the fighting? I will not promise to leave Austrian centers uncontested.

Germany is poised to gain BEL, BUL, POR, KIE, SPA and STP this Fall, putting it near 17. Please prioritize denying those centers: can F NTH or F HEL contest BEL/KIE, and can your northern fleets dislodge the units in SPA/STP? I’ll keep A TRI in place to deny Austria TRI.

Germany may reach 17 centers this Fall. Please contest its unit in POR and target German positions from MAR/PIC/VIE wherever feasible. I’ll keep A TRI holding to deny Austria, and can support A VIE holding from TRI if that helps keep a foothold against Germany.

Germany is close to 18 and likely gains several centers this Fall. Please use your eastern units to dislodge German units in ANK/BUL or otherwise deny its gains, rather than attack TRI. I’ll keep A TRI holding; can you confirm your orders target Germany?

I’m contesting Germany’s eastern gains: A SMY will attack BUL, and I’ll use A SEV against MOS. A ANK will pressure the German position at CON; I’ll keep my other units defending Austrian centers. Please keep contesting German centers in the north.

I will not leave ANK or BUL uncontested while your forces threaten Austrian centers. I’m contesting BUL and pressing your eastern positions this Fall. With England also attacking in the north, continuing to fight each other risks handing someone else the win.
Yes. I’m targeting German-held BUL and pressing toward MOS and CON; I will not attack TRI. Please keep A TRI holding and direct A VEN against German positions rather than Austrian centers.

I’ll contest German-held BUL and pressure the eastern approaches to MOS and CON this Fall. My other forces will defend Austrian centers; I will not attack your centers. Please keep A MAR protected and continue denying Germany any gains you can.

I’m not holding all three. F KIE and the northern fleets will contest your gains and protect English centers; I won’t leave KIE, SPA, or STP undefended for your convenience. Your A BEL is also under threat. You remain the immediate solo danger, so I won’t agree to keep clear of German centers.

I’m contesting BEL and protecting KIE, SPA, and STP rather than letting Germany collect them uncontested. Please keep pressing its eastern positions—especially BUL, ANK, and SMY—and avoid English centers. Germany’s gains this Fall could put it dangerously close to victory.

I’ll use F NTH to attack A BEL with support from F HEL, contesting Germany’s expected gain there. F KIE, F SPA/NORTH, and F STP/NORTH will protect those occupations; I can’t dislodge those fleets with the forces available. Please keep A TRI secure and obstruct Germany wherever you can.

I’ll contest A BEL from F NTH with F HEL supporting, and keep the English-held KIE, SPA, and STP occupations protected. Germany’s other gains are difficult for me to reach this turn. Please continue holding MAR against Germany and use your southern units to contest its positions; it cannot be allowed near 18.

A MAR will hold; I can't support it from PIC, which is not adjacent. A VIE is committed to supporting Italy's A TRI hold. F ION will move toward TUN, and A NAP will pressure Austria. Please keep contesting German centers in the north.
I won't move A POR out or leave it undefended; it is occupying a French center. I have no unit that can support POR this turn, but I will keep A MAR. Germany's growth remains the immediate threat.

I can't reach POR this turn: none of my units is adjacent to it. A MAR will hold, and A VIE will support A TRI holding as requested. Please keep TRI secure; I’ll continue looking for feasible pressure on German positions.

A BEL will hold; I’m not planning a move into another English center this Fall. I need KIE, SPA, and STP restored to German control, so please move those fleets out rather than contesting them. If you keep clear of German centers beyond BEL, we can limit the fighting.

I can’t leave BUL uncontested while A BUL is positioned to take it, and I won’t promise to abandon ANK. If you avoid advancing into German centers, we can keep this to the existing positions; otherwise I’ll defend my claims.

I intend to reclaim POR, which A POR currently occupies; I’m not planning an attack on MAR or another French center this Fall. If you keep A MAR out of German centers and avoid supporting resistance in POR, we can limit the conflict.

I’ll keep A TRI and A VEN in place this Fall and won’t attack Austrian centers. Please use A ANK, F BLA, A RUM, and your other units to contest Germany’s gains in ANK and BUL; Germany must not reach 18. I can’t reach a German center from VEN or TRI this turn, but I will not help Germany.

notes.note: Hold KIE, SPA, STP to secure their transfers to England. HEL takes open HOL; BAL contests SWE. NTH to NWG sets up a CLY convoy to NOR next turn. Germany rejects restraint; Austria and France promised eastern/southern pressure.

Hold TRI to retain Italy’s center; take ROM with VEN if vacant, gaining a center and denying Austria. Austria promised not to attack TRI; England, France, and Austria are targeting Germany, but outcomes unconfirmed.

ION to TUN and PIC to BRE seek centers; NAP pressures Austrian ROM, MAR advances toward SPA. Keep promise to Italy by supporting TRI hold. England and Austria pledged pressure on Germany; monitor whether they follow through.
Keep ANK and RUM; attack German-held BUL with SER supported by BLA and RUM. SEV pressures MOS, SMY advances toward SYR. England promised to contest German north; Germany refused restraint.

Recover BEL, BUL, POR by staying; support BEL against attack. Press KIE from BER, UKR attacks RUM with GAL support; advance FIN to NOR and SWE to DEN. England remains immediate solo threat; Austria contests eastern centers.

messages.body: Germany remains our immediate shared threat. Please continue contesting its northern centers this turn, especially HOL, KIE, and SWE, and avoid Austrian centers. I’ll keep pressure on its eastern positions; can you confirm your targets?

Let’s avoid a fight over VIE this turn while Germany remains a threat. Please keep your units out of Austrian centers and contest German holdings where you can; I’ll focus my eastern forces on denying Germany gains. What are your concrete targets?

Your eastern units threaten my centers, so I will defend them and contest your positions. I’m willing to limit the fighting if you stop pressing Austrian centers this turn. Will you leave RUM, BUL, and SEV alone?

Germany is now at 9 and you at 8; we must deny either a quick solo. What are A SEV, A RUM, and F BLA doing against German-held MOS, WAR, and UKR? I’ll keep pressure on German centers in the north and avoid your centers.

Germany has fallen to 9, but still threatens a solo. Please contest its southern centers and avoid English centers. What are A MAR, A VIE, and F TUN targeting? I’ll pressure the northern German positions while protecting my centers.

You remain a potential solo threat, so I will continue contesting German centers and protect English holdings. Are A BEL, A DEN, and A NOR moving against English positions this Spring? Keep your units out of English centers and we can limit the fighting.

Germany is down to 9, but remains the largest rival. What are your Spring targets? Please direct forces toward German centers and keep out of French centers; I will prioritize consolidating French positions rather than pressure you.

Germany has 9 centers and is still our strongest rival. What northern targets are you contesting this Spring? I’ll avoid English centers; please coordinate against German positions rather than letting it rebuild.

With 9 centers, you remain the biggest threat to a solo. Are you planning to attack French centers this Spring? I’m not seeking German centers this turn, but I will defend French holdings and won’t leave them exposed.

With Austria also contesting me, a northern fight benefits neither of us. Will you keep F KIE, F HOL, and the northern fleets out of BEL, DEN, and NOR this Spring? I can avoid advancing into English centers this turn if you do.

England’s fleets are contesting German positions in the north. Can we limit our eastern fighting this Spring: keep A RUM, A SER, and A BUD out of German centers, and I’ll avoid advancing into Austrian centers this turn? What are those units doing?
I’m trying to prevent the northern and eastern fronts from widening. Will A GAS and A MAR stay out of POR and other German positions this Spring? I can keep A POR out of French centers if you do.
I’m ordering A VEN–ROM and A TRI hold. Your units are not positioned to stop the move this turn. Please keep A RUM and A BUL from supporting a defense of ROM; I’ll avoid attacking your other centers.
I’m ordering A VEN–ROM to take Austria’s vacant center while holding A TRI. Please keep A VIE clear of TRI and ROM this turn; let me know if you see a German threat that needs coordinating against.

A SEV will pressure MOS, while A RUM and A BUL cover the eastern line; F BLA will stay in the eastern theater. I cannot leave my centers exposed to Germany. Please continue contesting HOL, KIE, and SWE, and keep clear of Austrian centers.

I’ll use A SEV to pressure MOS and keep A RUM and A BUL focused on defending the eastern line against Germany. F BLA remains in the eastern theater. I’ll avoid French centers; please keep your units out of Austrian centers and contest German holdings where possible.

I can’t leave RUM or BUL open while your eastern forces threaten my centers. A RUM and A BUL will defend the line, and A SEV will pressure MOS. I’m willing to limit the fighting if you genuinely avoid Austrian centers, but I won’t leave them undefended.

A VEN–ROM attacks an Austrian center, so I will defend ROM. Please keep A VEN out of ROM and A TRI out of Austrian centers; I’ll avoid TRI. Germany remains the larger threat, and fighting over our centers only helps it.

I’ll continue contesting Germany in the north: F HOL can pressure BEL, while F KIE and F SWE can challenge DEN and F NWG can pressure NOR. I’ll protect English-held centers and avoid yours. Please keep pressing Germany’s southern positions rather than allowing it to rebuild.

I won’t agree to keep F HOL, F KIE, or my northern fleets out of BEL, DEN, and NOR while you remain a potential solo winner and still contest English occupations. I’ll continue to protect my centers and pressure yours. Keep your units out of English centers.

I’ll keep pressure on Germany in the north, especially BEL from F HOL and DEN from F KIE or F SWE; F NWG can also threaten NOR. I’ll protect English-held centers and avoid yours. Please continue contesting German positions in the east, particularly MOS, WAR, and UKR.

I’ll keep pressure on Germany’s southern positions: A VIE can contest CON, and I’m looking for a feasible way to threaten POR. A MAR will stay clear of English centers; F TUN is available to pressure the central Mediterranean. Which northern German center are you targeting?

I have no interest in widening the war with you this Spring. I’ll keep A MAR out of your centers, and A GAS is not committed to POR. Please keep A POR and your other units out of French centers; Germany remains vulnerable to pressure from several fronts.

I’ll keep A VIE clear of TRI and ROM this turn. I see your plan to take ROM; please make sure A TRI is secure. Germany remains the larger threat, so I’d welcome you contesting its positions if an opportunity opens.

I’ll keep my units out of Austrian centers. A VIE can pressure German-held CON, while I’ll look for another feasible way to contest Germany. Please direct your eastern forces against German holdings as promised, and tell me which center you plan to challenge.

I’m not planning an advance into an English-owned center this Spring. A BEL, A DEN, and A NOR will be used to secure German positions; I can’t promise to leave BEL, DEN, or NOR uncontested if your fleets move against them. Keep F KIE, F HOL, and the northern fleets clear of German centers and we can limit the northern fighting.

I’m not planning an attack on a French center this Spring. A GAS and A MAR will stay out of POR and other German centers; A POR will remain focused on German interests. I can keep this front quiet if you likewise keep your armies out of German positions and avoid supporting Austria against me.

I can’t promise to leave RUM, BUL, and SEV uncontested while Austrian forces threaten German positions. I’m willing to limit the fighting this Spring: keep A RUM, A SER, and A BUD out of German centers, and I’ll avoid advancing into Austrian centers this turn. We can revisit the line after the season.

notes.note: Spring 1920: hold TRI and take vacant ROM with VEN; Austria says it will defend ROM, but has no unit adjacent to contest it. France promised to keep VIE clear. Reassess TRI defense in Fall.

Advance BRE to PIC and take the BUR foothold with MAR supported by GAS and PAR. Support Italy's VEN–ROM to deny Austria a center; TUN to ION for future options. VIE to BOH pressures the German front without entering Austrian centers. England and Austria promised pressure on Germany; monitor.

Contest German centers: CLY convoyed to NOR with STP support; KIE attacks DEN with SWE support; HOL attacks BEL. GOL advances to PIE, SPA/NORTH to MAO. France and Austria pledged pressure on Germany; Germany asked me to stay clear, refused.
Attack German CON from ANK with BLA and BUL support; pressure MOS and GAL, move SYR toward ARM, and reinforce SER from BUD. Italy announced VEN–ROM; no available unit can reach ROM this turn.

Press England at HOL, SWE, and SPA; move toward Austrian SMY/RUM and MOS. France said GAS/MAR stay out of POR and German centers; avoid French centers. Austria refuses to leave German centers unpressured; no accommodation.

messages.body: Germany may rise to 10 as HOL and SPA change hands, while we risk losing centers in the east. Please keep pressure on German-held HOL and SPA and avoid Austrian centers. I’ll focus on preserving the eastern line; what are your concrete targets this Fall?

Germany’s possible gains at HOL and SPA make it the immediate threat. Can you contest SPA or another German-held center this Fall? Please keep A BOH and your other units out of Austrian centers; I’ll defend my eastern centers.

A ROM will take ROM from me if it holds this Fall. Please move A ROM out of ROM or otherwise avoid taking an Austrian center; I’ll avoid TRI. Germany may gain HOL and SPA, so let’s not spend this turn fighting over our centers.

This Fall decides whether Germany keeps gaining. Please contest its eastern centers, especially SMY and CON, and avoid English centers. I’ll keep pressure on German-held positions in the north. What are A ARM, A BUL, and A SEV targeting?

Please use your southern units to contest German-held centers and avoid English centers. I’ll keep pressure on Germany in the north. Germany is still dangerous, but neither of us should let another power collect uncontested centers; what are A BUR and A GAS targeting?

I will not leave German centers uncontested while either of us is close enough to threaten a solo. Keep your units out of English centers; I’ll contest your northern positions this Fall. Are you moving A BEL or A HOL against English-held centers?

This Fall we should deny Germany its northern gains. I can order A PIC–BEL; will you support that attack from F HEL, or tell me which German center your units are targeting? Please keep your forces out of French centers.
Germany remains the main solo threat. I can pressure its western centers from PIC/BUR; what specific German center will your units contest this Fall? Please keep your forces out of French centers.

With 9 centers, you remain the leading solo threat. Are you planning to attack French centers this Fall? I intend to contest German holdings; please specify whether you will keep your units out of French centers.

This Fall decides DEN, HOL, NOR, and SPA. I need to recover DEN and keep HOL; I’m willing to avoid advancing into other English centers if you avoid supporting attacks on my occupations. What are F DEN, A NOR, F SWE, and your fleets doing?

With England contesting the north, neither of us benefits from letting them gain centers. I will avoid advancing into Austrian centers this Fall if A RUM, A SER, and A BUL stay out of German centers. What are your units doing, especially A CON and A SMY?

I’m focused on the northern and eastern fights this Fall and don’t intend to attack French centers. Please keep A GAS, A BUR, and A PIC out of German centers and avoid supporting England or Austria against my units; I’ll keep my forces clear of French centers.

I will keep A TRI in TRI this Fall and will not attack another Austrian center. A VEN is in ROM; I expect you may contest it, but please do not support an attack on TRI. Germany remains the main threat.

Germany is still the danger, but my two armies cannot reach its centers this turn. What are your plans for the German-held centers? I will hold A TRI and try to retain ROM if Austria does not dislodge me.

I plan to hold A TRI and A ROM this Fall. Please keep A VIE clear of TRI; can your units contest German-held positions this turn? Germany remains a major threat, and I have no direct route to its centers.

I will not support an attack on TRI. But A ROM is occupying an Austrian center, so I will contest ROM this Fall; please move it out if you want to avoid a fight. I’m also securing CON and SMY against Germany.

A CON and A SMY will secure those positions this Fall; I can’t leave Austrian centers exposed while Italy occupies ROM and your forces threaten the east. I’m not promising to attack elsewhere, but I won’t withdraw from centers that can change hands.

A ARM will press toward ANK, A BUL and A RUM will contest ROM, and A CON and A SMY will hold their positions. I’m focused on securing Austrian centers and denying Germany’s eastern gains; I will stay clear of English centers.

A CON and A SMY are my specific German-held centers to contest by holding them for Austria. I’m also contesting ROM from the east because Italy occupies it. I’ll keep A BOH and your other units out of Austrian centers; please continue pressing Germany from PIC/BUR.

I’m contesting Germany’s northern centers: F HEL will support France’s A PIC–BEL, while my northern units will keep pressure on DEN, NOR, and SWE. Please hold A TRI and keep contesting Austria’s attempt on ROM.

F HEL will support France’s A PIC–BEL. My other northern units will contest your occupations rather than leave German centers uncontested. Keep your units out of English centers; I won’t agree to a stand-down while you remain a potential solo threat.

My concrete pressure is against BEL: F HEL will support France’s A PIC–BEL. I’ll also contest German positions in the north where possible and avoid Austrian centers. Please use your eastern units to contest German-held SMY and CON, rather than simply preserving the line.
Yes—F HEL will support A PIC–BEL. I’ll keep my remaining northern units contesting German positions and out of French centers. Please order A PIC–BEL as proposed.

I can contest Germany, but my units cannot directly reach its occupied centers this Fall. A VIE is no longer on the board; I’ll keep my forces clear of TRI and ROM. Hold your centers if you can, and look for any chance to take German territory.

I won’t promise to leave German centers unchallenged while you remain the largest power and a solo threat. I’ll keep my units defending French centers where needed. Do not attack French centers; any move against them will make this front an active war.

A PIC can attack BEL, but F HEL cannot support it: HEL is not adjacent to BEL. I’ll use my western units to contest Germany where feasible and avoid English centers. Please use your northern units to deny German gains, especially at HOL, DEN, and NOR.

My units will stay out of Austrian centers. I can’t contest SPA this Fall, and my western units can pressure German positions instead. Please follow through against German holdings with your eastern forces and avoid French centers.

A BEL will not move into an English center. A HOL will remain focused on securing HOL, not advance into another English center. I need DEN and NOR restored to German control; if you keep your fleets from supporting attacks there, we can avoid widening the fight. I cannot leave your occupations uncontested.

I do not intend to attack a French center this Fall; my units will stay out of French centers. Please keep A GAS, A BUR, and A PIC out of German centers and do not support England or Austria against my positions. I am focused on recovering German centers in the north and east.

I’ll keep A TRI holding and won’t attack another Austrian center. A ROM is already in ROM, and I won’t voluntarily vacate it: it is Italy’s center, and holding denies you a build. Please keep A SER and A BUL from supporting an attack on TRI. Germany’s gains must still be contained.

notes.note: Hold ROM to secure Italy’s center despite Austria’s announced contest. Send TRI–BUD to pursue an Austrian center; Austria promised not to attack TRI. Reassess after the result.

Keep DEN and NOR to secure their Fall transfers. Attack HOL from HEL and POR from MAO; advance the remaining fleets toward useful positions. France proposed PIC–BEL, but HEL cannot support it; Austria pledged eastern pressure.

Press BEL with PIC, supported by BUR and England's promised HEL support; BOH advances to vacant MUN. Hold GAS with PAR cover against SPA. ION to TYS for future convoy options; NAP supports Italy's ROM hold.

Hold HOL, SMY, SPA to secure Fall gains; HOL supports BEL against PIC/HEL. FIN contests English-held NOR. GAL supports UKR's attack on Austrian RUM. PRU advances to LVN. Austria has not promised to leave German positions uncontested and occupies CON/SMY.

Hold CON for Austria; ARM attacks German SMY with CON support. SEV presses MOS. Layer BLA/BUL/SER support on RUM against German pressure. Italy refuses to vacate ROM; cannot contest it this turn. England promised northern pressure.

messages.body: Germany is no longer the immediate center threat; Austria, France, and England each have 9 or close. I will defend my centers and contest Italy’s occupation of ROM. Please confirm your targets this turn, and keep your units out of Austrian centers.

With Germany reduced to 4, our balance is now the main issue. Please keep your forces out of Austrian centers, especially VIE and MUN; I will avoid French centers. What are your concrete targets this turn?

A ROM is in an Austrian center, and I will contest it. I will not support an attack on TRI if you keep A TRI there and out of Austrian centers. Germany is no longer the immediate threat; please tell me A ROM’s orders.
France is now as large as I am and can become the next solo threat. Would A HOL support my F NTH–BEL this Spring? I’ll avoid your German centers this turn if you help contest France’s position.

With Germany reduced to four centers, France is now a serious rival to my nine. What are A BEL, A BRE, and A MAR doing this Spring? Please keep your units out of English centers; I intend to protect my holdings.

We are tied at 9 centers, so the solo race is real. What are your Spring targets? I intend to avoid English centers for now; please keep your units out of French centers and tell me whether you plan to pressure Germany or Austria.

Your 8 centers make you a major rival. What are your Spring targets, especially around VIE, TRI, and the French border? I will defend French centers and cannot leave your expansion uncontested; please keep your units out of French centers.

Austria is at 8 and vulnerable around TRI and VIE. Are you willing to contest it this Spring with A VEN–TRI and A BUD–VIE? I can coordinate from my southern units, but need to know your intended orders.

With France and Austria both at 9 and 8 centers, neither of us benefits from a needless northern fight while they grow. What are F HEL, F DEN, and your other northern fleets doing? If you keep clear of HOL and support no attack on my German centers this turn, I’ll keep A HOL and A SPA out of English centers.

I will keep my units out of French centers this Spring. Can you keep A BUR, A MUN, and A GAS out of German centers and avoid supporting English attacks on HOL or SPA? Austria’s 8 centers are a danger to both of us; what are your units doing this turn?

What are A MOS, A RUM, A SER, and A SMY doing this Spring? I have no spare force for a major eastern advance, but I won’t leave German positions undefended. If you keep your armies out of German centers and avoid supporting attacks there, I can keep my units from advancing into Austrian centers this turn.

My A ROM and A VEN will stay clear of your centers this Spring. I’m considering A BUD–SER; are you ordering A SER against BUD or otherwise attacking my centers? I’d prefer to avoid a costly fight while we both contain the larger powers.
I’m not planning to attack your centers. Please keep A MAR clear of the Italian border and tell me whether you intend to move toward Austrian territory; I may press from BUD if Austria threatens me.
I have no direct route to German centers this turn. Are you pressing Austria or Germany? If you plan to contest Austrian expansion, let me know; I’m watching the threat to BUD and VEN.

A RUM and A SER will defend the southern line; A MOS and A SMY will hold their positions this Spring. I will not support an attack on German centers this turn if your forces stay out of Austrian centers. I cannot leave the eastern approaches undefended.

A SER will hold, so please do not order A BUD–SER. I accept that A ROM and A VEN will stay clear of my centers, and I will not support an attack on TRI this Spring. Let’s avoid spending units on each other while larger powers remain strong.

This Spring my priorities are securing the eastern line and preventing an Italian move into SER. A SER will hold; A MOS and A SMY will stay focused east. I have no order against VIE, TRI, or the French border this turn. Please keep your units out of Austrian centers, especially VIE.

I’ll keep my forces out of Austrian centers this Spring and focus on the western balance. My fleets will protect English holdings and contest French pressure where needed. Please continue holding your centers and avoid moves against English positions.

I’m not agreeing to leave French positions uncontested, but I have no plan to enter HOL or SPA this Spring. I’ll keep my fleets focused on protecting my centers and managing the French threat; please keep A HOL and A SPA clear of English centers.

I’m concentrating on the western balance rather than making a direct move against Austria this Spring. Your best course is to protect BUD, ROM, and VEN and contest Austria’s pressure on ROM. I’ll keep my forces out of Austrian centers for now.

I’ll protect my holdings and keep my units out of French centers this Spring. I’m focused on containing the broader solo race rather than opening a needless fight between us. Please keep your units clear of English centers, especially DEN and NOR.

My immediate priority is defending VIE and MUN, both French centers, and keeping my other units positioned to protect French holdings. I can't promise to leave Austrian territory unchallenged while our forces face each other. Please keep your units out of French centers; what are your concrete moves toward VIE or MUN?

I won't promise to leave German centers unchallenged or refrain from opposing English moves. My units will defend French centers and respond to threats on the western front. Please keep your units out of French centers; I have no agreement to coordinate against Austria.

A BEL will defend Belgium, A BRE and A PAR will protect the western front, and A MAR will stay clear of English centers. I’m focused on defending French holdings and the Austrian pressure around VIE and MUN, not on taking English centers this Spring. Which northern target are you pursuing?

A MAR will stay clear of Italian centers. Austria is the immediate concern around VIE and MUN, and I’m defending my French holdings there; I can’t promise an attack on Austrian territory this Spring. Are you actually ordering A VEN–TRI or A BUD–VIE? If so, tell me which move you want coordinated.

I can’t support F NTH–BEL while you occupy German centers and France is contesting my position. I’ll keep A HOL and A SPA out of English centers this Spring if you keep your units from attacking HOL and my other German-held positions. I won’t promise to leave BEL uncontested.

A ROM will hold this Spring. A BUD is moving toward VIE; I’m not ordering an attack on ROM or another of your centers from there. I’ll keep A VEN clear of your centers, as requested, provided you leave my Italian centers alone.
Yes. I’ll order A VEN–TRI and A BUD–VIE. Please support A VEN–TRI with A MUN if you can, and keep A MAR clear of the Italian border. I’ll let you know if Austria threatens BUD or my other centers.

notes.note: Press BEL with RUH support; SPA attacks POR. UKR contests Austrian RUM despite Spring restraint offer. England and France made no firm promises to leave German centers safe; Austria promised not to support attacks if I avoid its centers.

Support VEN–TRI and occupy TRI to secure the Italian center, as coordinated with France. ROM–TUS seeks expansion. Austria promised not to attack TRI; preserve that understanding and reassess after results.

Press BUD with SER, backed by RUM; BLA and BUL protect RUM from UKR. MOS probes WAR, SMY advances ARM, CON secures ANK. Italy said BUD moves toward VIE and ROM/VEN stay clear; I break my promise that SER holds.

Position fleets for northern pressure; NTH attacks HOL with HEL support, despite Germany's restraint offer. France pledged to avoid English centers this Spring; keep watch on its western army. No Austrian centers targeted.

Press Germany: BUR to RUH with BEL support, GAS supports MAR to SPA, MUN advances to BER. Keep southern pressure positioned via NAP–APU and TYS–WES. Italy promised VEN–TRI and BUD–VIE; Austria says no moves against VIE/TRI/French border.

messages.body: France is positioned to take BER and SPA this Fall, which would put it ahead of us. Please contest French gains where feasible and keep your units clear of Austrian centers. I’ll secure WAR and focus my eastern units on the immediate border; what are your concrete targets?

With both of us at 9, I need to know whether you intend to advance against Austrian territory, especially from BUR toward MUN or toward VIE. I will secure WAR this Fall and keep clear of French centers; please keep your units out of Austrian centers and tell me your targets.

Please confirm that A BUD and A TRI will stay out of Austrian centers this Fall. I will not support an attack on TRI, but I cannot leave the Austrian border exposed; what are your concrete orders for BUD, ROM, and TRI?

This Fall I’m considering F NTH–BEL with F HEL support, and F MAO–POR to contest Germany’s occupation. Will A SPA support MAO–POR, and will you keep your other units out of English centers? I’ll avoid French centers beyond the contest at BEL.

Your A POR is likely to hold against my F MAO alone. Will you vacate POR or support a move that restores it to English control? I’m considering F NTH–BEL with F HEL support; are you moving A HOL to support BEL or contesting English centers?

With France poised to gain BER and SPA, the solo race is shifting west. I’m considering F NTH–BEL with F HEL support and contesting POR from MAO. What are A WAR and your other units targeting this Fall? I’ll keep my units out of Austrian centers.

Your A WAR will secure Germany’s center, but our forces are now adjacent at MUN and VIE. What are A WAR, A SER, and your eastern units targeting this Fall? I will defend French centers; please keep your units out of VIE and MUN.

With us tied at nine, I want to avoid an immediate war while Germany and Austria remain positioned to grow. I’ll keep my units out of English centers this Fall; please keep yours out of French centers, especially BEL and SPA. What are your fleets and A WAL targeting?

My units are claiming BER and SPA this Fall, and I intend to hold those gains. Please keep A HOL, A RUH, and A POR out of French centers; what are your concrete targets? I will defend my holdings and cannot promise to leave German centers unchallenged.

Your units in BER and SPA will give you two centers this Fall and put you ahead of England. Please do not support England into POR; I will keep A POR out of French centers and can focus on containing your growth rather than widening the western front.

Please keep your fleets from attacking POR this Fall. A POR staying there transfers the center to Germany; I can keep A HOL and A RUH out of English centers and would rather contain France than fight you over POR.

Please do not move A WAR into a German center this Fall. France is positioned to gain BER and SPA and become the leading power; if you keep WAR out of German centers, I can avoid advancing into Austrian centers and we can both focus on containing France.
I’ll keep A TRI in TRI and A ROM in ROM. Please confirm you will leave BUD and TRI alone; I’m considering A BUD–SER if A SER moves or lacks support. What are your orders for A SER and A BUL?
With your units poised to take BER and SPA, are you planning any move toward Italian centers? I’ll keep A TRI and A ROM secure; please keep A MAR clear of TRI and avoid moving into Italian territory.

Your A POR is vulnerable to the expected change in POR ownership, while France is poised for BER and SPA. I have no direct route to those centers this turn. Are you planning to contest WAR or POR, and will you keep A UKR clear of BUD?

A WAR will remain in WAR to secure the center. A SER and A BUL will cover the Austrian line; I have no order into VIE or MUN this Fall. France’s gains in BER and SPA make you the leading threat—please keep your units out of Austrian centers.

A WAR is already in WAR, and I cannot give up the center this Fall. I agree France’s growth is dangerous, but my priority is securing Austria’s position and protecting the eastern line. Please keep your units out of Austrian centers.

A SER will hold, with A BUL guarding the line; I will not support an attack on TRI. I cannot promise to leave BUD unchallenged if A BUD threatens SER, so please keep A BUD out of Austrian centers. What is your exact order for BUD?

A WAR will hold WAR, and my eastern units will protect the Austrian line. France’s gains in BER and SPA are the immediate danger; please contest French positions where feasible and keep your units clear of Austrian centers. I will not move against English centers this Fall.

I cannot promise to keep clear of BEL: I intend F NTH–BEL with F HEL supporting, and F MAO–POR to contest Germany’s transfer. I have no unit able to contest BER or SPA directly this turn. Please do not move against English centers; I will not support an attack on yours.

I intend F MAO–POR, contesting A POR’s transfer, and F NTH–BEL with F HEL support. I won’t agree to leave POR uncontested, and your A POR may hold against my lone fleet. Keep A HOL and A RUH clear of English centers; I have no plan to attack them this turn.

I intend F NTH–BEL with F HEL supporting and F MAO–POR to contest Germany’s A POR. I’ll keep my units out of Austrian centers. France is positioned to take BER and SPA; please use your eastern units to contest French gains where feasible and protect WAR.

I will not support England’s move from MAO to POR. A SPA will remain in SPA, and I expect A POR and your other units to stay out of French centers. I’m securing BER and SPA this Fall; do not move against them.
A MAR will stay clear of TRI and other Italian centers. I have no move planned into Italy; my immediate concern is protecting French holdings and securing BER and SPA.
I will not support F MAO–POR; A SPA will remain in SPA. I also oppose F NTH–BEL with HEL support: BEL is French, and I will defend it. Keep your forces out of French centers, especially BEL and SPA.

I have no planned move into VIE or other Austrian centers this Fall, but I will defend French holdings, including MUN. Please keep A WAR and your other units out of French centers. What are A SER and your eastern units targeting?

A POR will hold and stay out of French centers. I’m not asking you to vacate BER or SPA, but I will contest my lost centers where I can; A HOL and A RUH are focused on German territory, not French centers. Please do not support England into POR.

I intend to keep A POR in place to secure the center and press WAR with A RUH if possible. A UKR will stay clear of BUD. Can you apply pressure on Austria from TRI or VEN? Austria’s current strength is the larger danger to both of us.

A POR will remain in POR; I won’t vacate it or support its return to England. A HOL will not support F NTH–BEL, and I’m not planning to move it into an English center. Please keep your fleets from attacking POR.

A TRI and A ROM will hold; A BUD will not move into SER or another Austrian center this Fall. Please keep A SER and A BUL from attacking or supporting an attack on TRI, and leave ROM uncontested. I cannot promise to keep these units out of Austrian centers indefinitely; we both need room to recover.

notes.note: Move BUD to GAL to approach RUM; ROM to TUS and TRI to VIE to capture a French center. Austria promised SER holds and no attack on TRI; France says it will stay clear of Italy.
Hold WAR to secure its capture. Take GRE with BUL; advance ARM toward SYR, RUM to GAL, SER to ALB. Italy promised BUD will stay clear of Austrian centers; protect RUM with BLA support.

Keep POR to gain it; RUH takes vacant MUN, UKR takes vacant MOS. Support England's NTH-BEL to cut France's growth despite no firm alliance. France asked me not to support it; England intends POR attack and BEL attack. Austria keeps WAR.

Secure BER and SPA captures. England announced NTH–BEL with HEL support; defend BEL with BUR and PIC support. Germany says POR holds and will contest lost centers; protect SPA with GAS and WES support. Austria promises no move into VIE/MUN.

Contest French BEL with NTH supported by HEL, and prevent Germany taking POR. Advance fleets toward useful sea lanes; occupy SWE and keep WAL on LVP. France and Germany both asked restraint but neither offered to vacate contested centers.

messages.body: France is at 8 and has armies across the west. I propose we contain its growth this turn: use your northern fleets against French positions where feasible, while I secure my eastern line. Which French centers can you realistically contest? I’ll avoid English centers.

We are both at 8, and neither of us can afford to let the other reach 18. What are your concrete targets this Spring, especially regarding MUN and Austrian centers? I will defend my position and ask that you keep your units out of Austrian centers.

Please keep A BUD and your other units out of Austrian centers this Spring. I need to secure my position and cannot leave VIE or SER threatened. What is A BUD’s exact order? I will avoid attacking Italian centers if you stay clear of mine.

The west is now the decisive contest. I’m considering F NTH–BEL with F HEL support this Spring. Will A BEL defend, and what are A PIC and A PAR targeting? Please keep your units out of English centers.

You are at 9 and adjacent to the western contest; France is also a serious rival. What are A WAR, A RUM, and A SER targeting this Spring? Please pressure French positions where feasible and keep your units clear of English centers.

I’m focused on the western balance and may pressure BEL. What are A HOL, A MUN, and A MOS targeting? Please keep your units out of English centers; I’m interested in coordinating to contain France’s growth.

A BEL must remain French; after your announced F NTH–BEL with F HEL support last Fall, I will defend it. Please keep F NTH and F HEL out of BEL this Spring. What are your concrete orders for those fleets? I’m willing to coordinate pressure on Germany instead.

Your 9 centers make you the leading solo threat. My units are focused on French defense and the German front; I have no Spring move planned into Austrian centers. What are A ANK, A WAR, and your other units targeting? Please keep clear of French centers.

With your four centers exposed, I expect to keep pressure on your holdings from the west. What are A HOL, A MOS, A MUN, and A POR targeting this Spring? Please keep your units out of French centers; I’m not coordinating an English attack on POR.

France now has 8 centers and is positioned to grow into German territory. Will you keep F HEL and F NTH from supporting attacks on HOL or BER this Spring? I can keep A HOL focused on German territory, but need to know whether you intend to contest my remaining centers.

Your 8 centers and pressure on BER put you in a position to eliminate Germany. What are A BER, A BUR, and A PIC doing this Spring? I can keep A HOL out of French centers if you will avoid supporting attacks on HOL or MUN.

France is now a major threat to both of us. Will A WAR and A MOS stay out of German centers this Spring, and will you avoid supporting France against my units? I can avoid Austrian centers this turn if you keep the line out of my territory.

What are your orders for A RUM, A WAR, A ALB, and A GRE? I need to protect BUD and VIE. I’m considering pressure on RUM from BUD; please confirm whether you intend to attack any Italian centers this Spring.

I can pressure Austria from BUD toward RUM while holding VIE. Can you apply pressure on WAR or another Austrian position this Spring? Please confirm your concrete orders, and I’ll keep my units clear of German centers.

I have no plan to enter French centers. Austria’s 9 centers are the immediate concern; can you apply pressure from BER or BUR toward Austrian territory this Spring? Please keep your units clear of Italian centers.

A WAR will hold WAR, and I have no unit in MOS or order against a German center this Spring. I will not support France against your units. Please keep your forces out of Austrian centers; we can both focus on containing the western powers.

A WAR will hold WAR and A RUM will defend RUM; my eastern units are focused on securing the line. I have no Spring move planned into French centers. Please keep your forces out of Austrian centers, especially VIE and SER.

A WAR will hold WAR and A RUM will defend RUM; I have no A SER on the board. My other units are focused on the eastern line, not English centers. Please contest French growth where feasible and keep your fleets clear of Austrian centers.

A RUM will defend RUM against pressure from BUD, and A WAR will hold WAR. A ALB and A GRE will stay clear of Italian centers; I have no A SER on the board. I intend no attack on Italian centers this Spring, provided your units stay out of Austrian centers.

I won't attack HOL or BER this Spring. F NTH can pressure BEL, but F HEL cannot support that move; I may move it to NTH instead. Please keep A HOL out of English centers and use your armies to contain France.

F NTH can move to BEL, but F HEL cannot support it, so I won't pretend I can force A BEL out alone. I may move F HEL to NTH and contest BEL; please use A BEL against German positions instead and keep your units out of English centers.

The only French center my northern fleets can directly contest is BEL: F NTH can attack, but F HEL cannot support from HEL, so I cannot guarantee dislodging A BEL. I’ll also pressure German positions where feasible. Please keep your units clear of English centers.

A BER and A BUR will pressure MUN this Spring; I cannot promise to leave your centers uncontested. I will not support England into POR. Keep A HOL and A POR out of French centers, and tell me whether A MUN will hold or move.

A BEL will hold, with A PIC supporting its defense. A PAR will move to BUR, and I’ll keep my other units out of English centers. I oppose F NTH–BEL; please keep F NTH and F HEL out of BEL. I’m willing to coordinate against Germany, but not at Belgium’s expense.
